fields.description: Typed lambda calculi and type inference: the simply typed lambda calculus (syntax, substitution, normalization, logical relations, normalization by evaluation, elaboration, its models), lambda calculus with references and type safety, and Hindley-Milner let-polymorphism with Algorithm W.

fields.title: Functional programming structures
fields.description: Functors, applicative functors, monads and traversal as structures of functional programming, together with recursive computations, lazy lists and streams. Abstract categories, functors and monads are treated under Category Theory.

fields.title: Program logics and verification
fields.description: Logics for proving programs correct: Hoare logic for partial and total correctness with soundness and relative completeness, weakest preconditions, verification-condition generation, and separation logic.

fields.title: Computer security
fields.description: Formal models of security policies and their decision problems, such as the access-matrix protection systems of Harrison, Ruzzo and Ullman.

fields.title: Computer systems
fields.description: Models of operating-system and hardware mechanisms and their correctness: paged address translation and page replacement, cache coherence protocols and memory consistency models.

fields.title: Machine learning
fields.description: Mathematical theory of learning from data, including the probabilistic modelling, inference and sampling methods used in machine learning.

subfields.title: PAC learning
subfields.description: Valiant's model of learning from random examples, on CSLib's PAC library (error, learners, version spaces, consistency, PAC learnability, VC dimension): Valiant's Bernoulli-trial bound, the Occam bound for consistent learners over a finite class, learning k-CNF by elimination, the fundamental theorem relating PAC learnability to the VC dimension, and the bridge between the 0-1 risk and CSLib's error. Uniform deviation bounds for the agnostic case are under [generalization bounds and concentration](../generalization-bounds-and-concentration/README.md); boosting weak learners is under [online learning and boosting](../online-learning-and-boosting/README.md).

subfields.title: Online learning and boosting
subfields.description: Mistake and regret bounds for sequential prediction: perceptron, weighted majority, Hedge (multiplicative weights) and AdaBoost.

subfields.title: Reinforcement learning theory
subfields.description: Theory of reinforcement learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes: stochastic policies, discounted state occupancies, the performance difference lemma, conservative policy iteration, the simulation lemma, and policy gradient methods with the global convergence of natural policy gradient.

subfields.title: Supervised learning and regression
subfields.description: Prediction from labelled data: least squares, ridge, lasso and kernel or Gaussian-process regression (including GBLUP), the bias-variance decomposition, Bayes classifiers and optimal predictors, log loss, decision-tree information gain, backpropagation, and sufficient input subsets. Ridge regression is the finite-dimensional case of [Tikhonov regularization](../../../Analysis/convex-analysis-and-variations/tikhonov-regularization/README.md); point estimation theory (risk, sufficiency, James–Stein shrinkage) is under [statistical estimation](../../../Probability/statistical-estimation/README.md), and Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares under [linear models and multivariate analysis](../../../Probability/linear-models-multivariate/README.md).

subfields.title: Unsupervised learning and matrix factorization
subfields.description: Structure in unlabelled data: k-means, single-linkage hierarchical clustering, archetypal analysis, nonnegative matrix factorization, the successive projection algorithm, and probabilistic PCA with the Gaussian factor-analysis marginal. Classical principal component analysis is under [linear models and multivariate analysis](../../../Probability/linear-models-multivariate/README.md).

subfields.title: Probabilistic graphical models
subfields.description: Bayesian networks and their Markov properties, structure scores and Markov equivalence, causal networks and adjustment, belief propagation and variable elimination, conditional random fields, hidden Markov models (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch) and the Kalman filter.

subfields.title: Bayesian inference and sampling
subfields.description: Bayes' rule and conjugate models, expectation-maximization for mixtures and latent-variable models, variational mean-field inference, and Monte Carlo, rejection, Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings sampling. Bayesian nonparametric priors (the Dirichlet process and urn schemes, and the Chinese restaurant and Indian buffet processes as infinite limits of finite mixture and feature models) are under [Bayesian statistics](../../../Probability/bayesian-statistics/README.md).

subfields.title: Attention and low-rank adaptation
subfields.description: Linear algebra of recent methods for adapting and running transformer layers: low-rank adaptation of a frozen weight matrix (LoRA), its initialisation from the principal singular values and vectors of the pretrained matrix (PiSSA), and the identity-plus-rank-one state transitions of delta-rule linear attention (DeltaNet). These pages are expositions of published methods without Lean formalization; each names the linear algebra it relies on, and how, under Informally uses. Singular value decompositions are under [matrix decompositions](../../../LinearAlgebra/matrix-decompositions/singular-value-decomposition/README.md).

subfields.title: Linear state-space sequence models
subfields.description: Linear algebra of recent state-space sequence layers such as Mamba and Mamba-2: for fixed parameters, a linear time-varying state-space recurrence acts along the sequence as multiplication by a semiseparable matrix, and a time-invariant one as a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix, that is, a causal convolution. These pages are expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names the linear algebra it relies on, and how, under Informally uses. Semiseparable matrices are under [special matrices](../../../LinearAlgebra/special-matrices/semiseparable-matrices/README.md).

subfields.title: Diffusion and flow-based generative models
subfields.description: Linear algebra of diffusion and flow-based generative models: for Gaussian data, the score and the optimal denoiser are spectral functions of the data covariance and the probability-flow ODE is a linear system with commuting coefficients whose flow map is an explicit affine map; for any differentiable velocity field, the divergence in the log-density computations of flow models is the trace of a Jacobian. These pages are AI-authored expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names what it relies on, and how, under Informally uses, and marks results not stated in its sources as derived.

subfields.title: Generalization bounds and concentration
subfields.description: Uniform deviation bounds between the empirical and the expected risk, obtained from concentration inequalities: for a finite class, Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound; for a general class, McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality concentrates the supremum of the deviations around its mean, and Rademacher averages control its expectation. The finite-class bound, the reduction of empirical risk minimization to a uniform deviation bound and the dimension-free Rademacher average of a ball of linear predictors are formalized; the two pages marked as expositions are AI-authored expositions of published results without Lean formalization.

Dynamics.title: Dynamical Systems
Dynamics.description: Dynamics studies systems evolving through iteration or time, including recurrence, stability, and long-term behavior.

fields.title: Ergodic theory
fields.description: Ergodic theory studies measure-preserving transformations and their statistical behaviour: ergodic averages, recurrence, mixing and the structure of measure-preserving actions.

fields.title: Topological and symbolic dynamics
fields.description: Topological dynamics studies continuous maps of topological spaces through orbits, periodic points and recurrence, and symbolic dynamics studies shift spaces and cellular automata on sequences of symbols.

fields.title: Low-dimensional dynamics
fields.description: Low-dimensional dynamics covers maps of the interval and circle, continued-fraction-type maps, flows in the plane and homeomorphisms of surfaces.

fields.title: Smooth dynamics
fields.description: Smooth dynamics studies differentiable maps and flows: hyperbolicity, stable manifolds and shadowing, Lyapunov exponents and entropy, Hamiltonian perturbation theory, and stability of flows given by differential equations.

fields.title: Complex dynamics
fields.description: Complex dynamics studies the iteration of holomorphic maps, especially polynomials, together with their Julia sets and parameter spaces such as the Mandelbrot set.

fields.title: Homogeneous dynamics
fields.description: Homogeneous dynamics studies flows and group actions on homogeneous spaces of Lie groups, such as unipotent and horocycle flows on quotients by lattices and Kleinian groups, with applications to values of quadratic forms, lattice point counting and circle packings.

FieldTheory.title: Field Theory
FieldTheory.description: Field theory studies extensions of fields, algebraic elements, automorphisms, and Galois-theoretic structure.

fields.title: Galois theory
fields.description: Galois theory relates a field extension to its group of automorphisms, covering the Galois correspondence, infinite Galois groups, Hilbert's theorem 90, solvability by radicals and essential dimension.

fields.title: Finite fields
fields.description: Finite fields and polynomials over them: irreducible and primitive polynomials, permutation polynomials, and the arithmetic of squares.

fields.title: Field extensions and algebraic closure
fields.description: Algebraic field extensions and closures: minimal polynomials, separable and purely inseparable extensions, base change to separably closed fields, algebraic closures of series fields and quasi-algebraically closed fields.

fields.title: Transcendental extensions and function fields
fields.description: Algebraic independence, transcendence bases and transcendence degree, separably generated extensions, fields of rational functions and Lüroth's theorem, and differential fields with Liouville's theorem on elementary integrals. Algebraic extensions are under field extensions and algebraic closure; the arithmetic of global function fields is under number theory.

GameTheory.title: Game Theory
GameTheory.description: Game theory studies strategic and combinatorial interaction, equilibria, winning conditions, and optimal play.

fields.title: Combinatorial game theory
fields.description: Combinatorial game theory studies two-player games of perfect information without chance: impartial games such as Nim and its variants (P-positions, Sprague–Grundy values, remoteness), partizan games such as Snort, and Maker–Breaker positional games.

fields.title: Cooperative game theory
fields.description: Cooperative game theory studies games in which coalitions of players can make binding agreements, and solution concepts such as the core and the Shapley value for dividing a coalition's worth.

fields.title: Mechanism design
fields.description: Mechanism design studies how to choose the rules of a game, with or without money, so that self-interested agents with private information reach a desired outcome in equilibrium: the revelation principle, incentive compatibility and Myerson's characterization of single-parameter mechanisms, revenue equivalence and optimal auctions, Vickrey–Clarke–Groves mechanisms, and impossibility results for bilateral trade.

fields.title: Noncooperative games
fields.description: Noncooperative game theory studies strategic games in which each player chooses a strategy to optimise its own payoff or cost: Nash equilibria and the minimax theorem, evolutionarily stable strategies, potential and congestion games, routing games with Wardrop equilibria, the price of anarchy and of stability, learning dynamics such as no-regret play, regret matching and Blackwell approachability together with correlated and coarse correlated equilibria, and mean field games with a continuum of players.

fields.title: Matching markets
fields.description: Two-sided matching markets: stable matchings of marriage and college-admissions markets, the lattice of stable matchings and the opposition of the two sides' interests, properties shared by all stable matchings such as the rural hospitals theorem, and the incentives of stable matching mechanisms, from Roth's impossibility theorem to the strategy-proofness of deferred acceptance for the proposing side. The stable marriage problem and the Gale–Shapley existence theorem are under GraphTheory/matchings-and-flows, and the deferred-acceptance algorithm under ComputerScience/graph-algorithms.

fields.title: Social choice theory
fields.description: Social choice theory studies rules that aggregate individual preferences into a collective ranking or choice, and the impossibility theorems that limit them.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.description: Geometry studies shapes, spaces, transformations, curvature, and the invariants preserved by geometric equivalence.

fields.title: Affine and projective geometry
fields.description: Affine spaces over modules: affine maps and equivalences, affine subspaces, affine combinations and barycentric coordinates, affine independence and simplices; and projective spaces of vector spaces with their subspaces, independence and collinearity. Metric notions are under Euclidean geometry.

fields.title: Euclidean geometry
fields.description: Classical synthetic and metric geometry of the Euclidean plane and space: triangles, circles, conics, polygons, isometries and the foundations of geometry.

subfields.title: Euclidean affine spaces
subfields.description: Real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces of any dimension: unoriented and oriented angles, orthogonal projections onto affine subspaces, signed distances, and volumes of simplices. Plane rotations and other Euclidean isometries are under isometries and symmetry.

subfields.title: Triangle geometry
subfields.description: Theorems about triangles, their centers, cevians, inscribed and circumscribed circles, and triangle inequalities.

subfields.title: Circles and conics
subfields.description: Configurations of circles and conics, tangency, chains of circles, lunes, and mathematical billiards in elliptic and polygonal tables.

subfields.title: Polygons and quadrilaterals
subfields.description: Theorems about quadrilaterals, cyclic polygons and squares erected on polygon sides.

subfields.title: Solid and spherical geometry
subfields.description: Metric relations for tetrahedra and other solids, and trigonometry on the sphere.

subfields.title: Isometries and crystallographic groups
subfields.description: Distance-preserving maps of Euclidean space, their classification, and discrete symmetry groups such as wallpaper and space groups.

subfields.title: Foundations and constructions
subfields.description: Axiom systems for plane geometry and the limits of compass-and-straightedge constructions.

fields.title: Convex geometry
fields.description: Convex sets and convex bodies in Euclidean space: Helly-type and Radon-type theorems, partitions, sections, valuations and linear optimization over polyhedra.

fields.title: Packings and coverings
fields.description: Optimal arrangements of congruent bodies in space and the smallest sets or fewest translates needed to cover given families of shapes.

fields.title: Discrete geometry
fields.description: Finite point configurations and their distances, polytopes and polyhedra, dissections and tilings, lattice points and extremal shape problems.

fields.title: Metric geometry
fields.description: Geometry of general metric spaces: curvature bounds via comparison, length spaces, isometric embeddings and low-distortion embeddings.

fields.title: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces
fields.description: Curvature, tangents and global properties of curves and surfaces in Euclidean space, including knotted curves and inscribed figures.

fields.title: Riemannian and Finsler geometry
fields.description: Manifolds with smoothly varying inner products or norms on tangent spaces: connections, curvature, geodesics, differential operators and rigidity theorems.

fields.title: Differential topology
fields.description: Smooth manifolds and smooth maps between them: immersions, submersions, transversality, Morse theory, neighbourhood theorems and smooth structures.

fields.title: Complex and symplectic geometry
fields.description: Manifolds with complex, almost complex, symplectic or contact structures, Riemann surfaces, and integrable Hamiltonian systems.

GraphTheory.title: Graph Theory
GraphTheory.description: Graph theory studies vertices and edges through connectivity, coloring, minors, flows, and extremal structure.

fields.title: Graphs, subgraphs and homomorphisms
fields.description: Simple graphs and multigraphs, adjacency, degrees, subgraphs, deletion and copies of graphs. The algebraic theory of homomorphisms, cores and covers belongs to Algebraic graph theory.

fields.title: Paths, cycles and connectivity
fields.description: Walks, paths and cycles in graphs, Eulerian and Hamiltonian cycles, and vertex and edge connectivity, including Menger's theorem and Fleischner's theorem on squares of 2-connected graphs.

fields.title: Graph coloring
fields.description: Vertex, edge, list and fractional colorings of graphs and the chromatic number, from Brooks' and Vizing's theorems to perfect graphs and the four color theorem.

fields.title: Matchings and flows
fields.description: Matchings and factors in graphs, stable matchings, and flows in networks, including Kőnig's theorem, Berge's lemma and the max-flow min-cut theorem.

fields.title: Independence, cliques and domination
fields.description: Independent sets, cliques and dominating sets in graphs, with bounds on their sizes and polynomials counting them.

fields.title: Extremal graph theory
fields.description: How many edges or copies of a subgraph a graph can have while avoiding a forbidden structure: Turán and Zarankiewicz problems, saturation, and extremal graphs of given girth.

fields.title: Ramsey theory for graphs
fields.description: Ramsey numbers of graphs, their known small values, and Ramsey–Turán problems.

fields.title: Algebraic graph theory
fields.description: Graphs studied through groups and matrices: Cayley and vertex-transitive graphs, strongly regular and Moore graphs, graph homomorphisms, Laplacians and the matrix-tree theorem, and named graphs such as the Petersen and Coxeter graphs.

fields.title: Planar graphs and minors
fields.description: Graphs drawn in the plane and on the square lattice, crossing numbers, Euler's formula, discrete Jordan curve and turning-number theorems, and the theory of graph minors.

fields.title: Graph invariants and labelings
fields.description: Numerical and polynomial invariants of graphs such as degree sequences, arboricity, induced forest number, Shannon capacity and the chromatic symmetric function, and graph labelings.

fields.title: Directed graphs and tournaments
fields.description: Directed graphs, orientations of undirected graphs, digraph colorings and tournaments.

fields.title: Graph families and operations
fields.description: Graph products, line graphs and other constructions, together with special families such as expanders and the hypercubic lattice.

fields.title: Random graphs and graph limits
fields.description: Random graph models such as Erdős–Rényi, random regular and random k-out graphs, the typical values of their invariants (chromatic number, independence ratio, connectivity, spectra), and graphons as limits of dense graph sequences.

fields.title: Social and complex networks
fields.description: Graph-theoretic models of social and information networks: degree statistics and the friendship paradox, clustering and centrality measures, structural balance of signed graphs, and deterministic threshold processes on weighted graphs.

GroupTheory.title: Group Theory
GroupTheory.description: Group theory studies symmetry through groups, actions, subgroups, quotients, and structural decompositions.

fields.title: Groups, subgroups and quotients
fields.description: Group axioms and homomorphisms, subgroups and their lattice, cosets and index, normal subgroups, quotient groups and the isomorphism theorems, centres and centralizers, simple groups and particular groups such as cyclic, dihedral and dicyclic groups. Actions, conjugacy classes, commutators, extensions and the structure of abelian groups have their own fields.

fields.title: Semigroups and monoids
fields.description: Magmas, semigroups and monoids and their morphisms: units and invertible elements, commuting and semiconjugate elements, submonoids and subsemigroups, monoids and groups with zero, congruences and quotients, free magmas, semigroups and monoids, localization of commutative monoids, the Grothendieck group and Ore localization, opposites and adjoined identities; groups proper are under Groups, subgroups and quotients.

fields.title: Abelian groups
fields.description: Structure of abelian groups: finite and finitely generated abelian groups (invariant factors, elementary divisors, torsion, ranks, dual groups), torsion-free and infinite abelian groups (Baer–Specker group, pure subgroups, direct-sum cancellation, ultraproducts of abelian groups); colourings and partitions of abelian groups go to Combinatorics in groups.

fields.title: Group orders, element orders and spectra
fields.description: Arithmetic of finite groups through orders: cyclic numbers and groups of a given order (groups of order 10, dihedral groups from an index-two cyclic subgroup), counts of elements of each order, the spectrum (set of element orders), recognition of groups by spectrum or by order and spectrum, Thompson's type, and totient sums; conjugacy-class sizes go to Conjugacy classes.

fields.title: Conjugacy classes
fields.description: Conjugacy classes of groups as a structural invariant: class sizes and breadth, the class number, commuting probability, Thompson's conjecture on class sizes, products of conjugacy classes, and relations between class sizes and group structure; class sizes of p-groups go to Finite p-groups, and character-theoretic class arguments to Characters of finite groups.

fields.title: Finite simple groups and involutions
fields.description: Finite simple and almost simple groups and the local analysis behind their classification: specific simple groups (Mathieu, Suzuki, PSL), strongly embedded subgroups (Bender–Suzuki), classification by Sylow 2-subgroups (Gorenstein–Walter, Brauer–Suzuki), Baer–Suzuki, Glauberman Z*, Brauer–Fowler, involution centralizers and 3-transpositions; generation questions go to Generation of groups and spectrum recognition to Group orders, element orders and spectra.

fields.title: Generation of groups
fields.description: Minimal and special generating sets: generator numbers of almost simple and soluble groups, (2,3)-generation, generation by elements of prime-power order, spread, coprime generation, two-generated direct powers, Eulerian functions and probabilistic generation.

fields.title: Sylow and Hall subgroups
fields.description: Sylow theory and its generalization to sets of primes: Hall π-subgroups, the classes E_π, C_π and D_π, pronormality and intersections of Hall subgroups, groups whose maximal subgroups are Hall; questions on supplements of Sylow maximal subgroups forcing solubility go to Soluble and supersoluble finite groups.

fields.title: Subgroup embedding and subgroup lattices
fields.description: How subgroups sit inside a group: subnormal, permutable, propermutable, pronormal, polynormal and paranormal subgroups, maximal subgroups and their conjugates, intersections of conjugates of nilpotent subgroups and injectors with the Fitting subgroup, centralizer lattices and complemented subgroup lattices.

fields.title: Soluble and supersoluble finite groups
fields.description: Structure of finite soluble groups: supersolubility criteria, p-solubility and p-length, chief factors and their complements, σ-solubility and σ-nilpotency, Schmidt subgroups, derived length bounds for finite groups of special type, and factorized groups; classes of groups closed under operations go to Formations and Fitting classes.

subfields.title: Formations and Fitting classes
subfields.description: Classes of finite groups: formations, local and hereditary formations, Fitting and radical classes, injectors, subgroup functors, residuals, and lattices of formations; varieties defined by laws go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations.

fields.title: Factorized groups
fields.description: Groups that are products G = AB of two or more subgroups, finite or infinite: solubility, nilpotency and derived length of products of abelian, nilpotent, minimax or soluble factors (Itô and Kegel–Wielandt type theorems), triple factorizations, subnormal subgroups of factorized groups, and classes of groups closed under such products; supersoluble factorizations and products of maximal subgroups stay in Soluble and supersoluble finite groups, formations and Fitting classes in general in Formations and Fitting classes, and products of periodic subgroups in Periodic and locally finite groups.

fields.title: Finite p-groups
fields.description: Groups of prime-power order: composition series, Frattini subgroups and Φ-extensions, special, powerful, metacyclic and Camina p-groups, conjugacy class sizes of p-groups, generalized quaternion groups, coclass and rank analogues, derived length bounds, and orders of automorphism groups of p-groups only when the p-group structure is the point.

fields.title: Characters of finite groups
fields.description: Complex characters and representations used to study finite groups: class functions and orthogonality, irreducible character bases, character degrees and values, McKay conjecture, rational groups, permutation characters, blocks of defect zero, Frobenius group determinant, convolution on finite groups, and Burnside's p^a q^b theorem; general representation theory of algebras and Lie groups belongs to RepresentationTheory.

fields.title: Permutation groups and group actions
fields.description: Groups acting on sets: orbits, stabilizers, fixed-point counts, transitivity, bases, closures, Frobenius groups, symmetric and alternating groups as permutation groups, and infinite permutation groups (highly homogeneous, cofinitary, oligomorphic, subdegree-finite).

subfields.title: Group actions
subfields.description: Actions of monoids and groups on sets in general: orbits, stabilizers and the orbit–stabilizer theorem, fixed points, quotients and orbit spaces, equivariant maps, invariant subsets, the conjugation action, actions on functions and pointwise actions on sets, faithful and pretransitive actions, and equidecompositions; finite and infinite permutation groups proper have their own subfields.

subfields.title: Finite permutation groups
subfields.description: Actions of finite groups on finite sets: Burnside-type counting, stabilizers, multiply and doubly transitive finite groups, Frobenius groups, bases and independent sets, 2-closures, regular orbits of linear actions, coverings and products in finite symmetric groups.

subfields.title: Symmetric and alternating groups
subfields.description: The symmetric group of a set as a group: support, cycles and cycle decomposition, cycle types and conjugacy classes, the sign homomorphism, generation by transpositions and cycles, the alternating group, its simplicity and its maximal subgroups, and centralizers of permutations; enumerative statistics of permutations are under Combinatorics.

subfields.title: Infinite permutation groups
subfields.description: Permutation groups on infinite sets: highly homogeneous groups of orders, circular orders and betweenness (Cameron), the pointwise topology on permutations, cofinitary and subdegree-finite groups, infinite sharply or doubly transitive groups, embeddings into the infinite symmetric group, class transpositions of the integers.

fields.title: Free groups and their automorphisms
fields.description: Free groups and free metabelian groups: subgroups (inert, compressed, retracts, fixed subgroups), elements (primitive, test, orbit-blocking words, normal closures), and the groups Aut(F_n), Out(F_n) and IA-automorphisms; equations over free groups go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations, and commutator length to Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions.

subfields.title: Subgroups and elements of free groups
subfields.description: Subgroup and element structure inside free and free metabelian groups: rank, inertness and compressedness, derived subgroups, retracts, primitive and equally distributed elements, independent sets, separation, Cayley–Hamilton analogues and characteristic quotients.

subfields.title: Automorphisms of free groups
subfields.description: The groups Aut(F_n) and Out(F_n): fixed points and fixed subgroups of automorphisms, word problem, automaticity, linearity of IA-automorphisms, embeddings of free products into Aut(F_n).

fields.title: Presentations and decision problems
fields.description: Combinatorial group theory: presentations, one-relator groups, HNN extensions and embeddings, SQ-universality, finitely presented simple groups, the word and conjugacy problems (Novikov–Boone, Boone–Higman), Andrews–Curtis moves, generic properties of presentations and torsion quotients.

subfields.title: Braid and Artin groups
subfields.description: Braid groups, pure braid groups and Artin–Tits groups of Coxeter matrices: endomorphisms, roots, conjugators and conjugacy questions.

fields.title: Geometric group theory
fields.description: Large-scale and analytic properties of finitely generated groups: growth, word-hyperbolic groups and their quotients, amenability and Følner sets, elementary amenable groups, property (T), soficity and permutation stability.

subfields.title: Branch, automaton and Thompson groups
subfields.description: Groups acting on rooted trees, branch and just-infinite groups of intermediate growth, finite-state (automaton) groups, and Thompson's group F and its piecewise-linear relatives.

fields.title: Orderable groups
fields.description: Left-, right- and bi-orderable groups: spaces of orders, generalized torsion, unique product groups, relatively convex subgroups, orderability of homeomorphism groups and amalgams, and decision problems for orderable groups.

fields.title: Varieties, quasivarieties and equations
fields.description: Groups defined by laws and quasi-identities: varieties, relatively free groups, test ranks, quasivarieties and their lattices, Hall's verbal conjectures, plus equations over groups, equationally Noetherian groups, geometric equivalence and elementary theories of groups.

fields.title: Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions
fields.description: Commutator calculus and nilpotency in (often infinite) groups: basic commutators, Engel elements, locally nilpotent and hypercentral groups, metabelian and polycyclic groups, localization of nilpotent groups, commutator width and length, word maps and their images, and local word identities.

fields.title: Automorphisms of groups
fields.description: Automorphism and endomorphism groups of groups other than free groups: their orders and realizations, outer automorphism groups, class-preserving automorphisms, and automorphisms with few fixed points or twisted conjugacy classes.

subfields.title: Automorphism groups
subfields.description: The automorphism group as an object: orders of automorphism groups, realizing groups as (outer) automorphism groups, class-preserving and inner automorphisms, automorphism orbits, endomorphism counts.

subfields.title: Fixed points of automorphisms
subfields.description: How an automorphism and its fixed points control a group: almost regular and fixed-point-free automorphisms, bounds on derived length and Fitting height, twisted conjugacy, e- and nil-automorphisms, squares of 2-automorphisms.

fields.title: Periodic and locally finite groups
fields.description: Infinite groups defined by torsion and finiteness conditions: Burnside problems and free Burnside groups, Golod groups, Tarski monsters, locally finite simple groups, periodic Frobenius groups, minimal and weak chain conditions, and embeddings into simple periodic groups.

fields.title: Profinite and topological groups
fields.description: Groups with topology or approximated by finite quotients: profinite and pro-p groups, residual finiteness and separability, profinite rigidity, Golod–Shafarevich inequality, just-infinite groups, totally disconnected locally compact groups, group topologies, Lie groups and their dense subgroups.

fields.title: Linear groups
fields.description: Groups of matrices over fields and rings: SL2, PGL2 and SU(2) and their conjugacy and subgroups (Dickson's classification), Jordan, Malcev and Selberg theorems, transvections, eigenvalues of elements of prime order, and linearity of specific groups.

fields.title: Group rings
fields.description: Group rings and group algebras: unit and zero-divisor questions (Kaplansky unit conjecture), Zassenhaus conjectures, augmentation and dimension subgroups, Ore conditions, Jordan decomposition, projective modules over group rings.

fields.title: Combinatorics in groups
fields.description: Additive and Ramsey-type combinatorics inside groups: approximate subgroups and product theorems, small doubling, partitions and colourings of groups, dense and coset-free partitions, subset factorizations, products of large normal subsets.

fields.title: Group extensions and cohomology
fields.description: Extensions and complements (Schur–Zassenhaus), splitting of extensions, homology and first cohomology of groups, cohomological dimension, and integrability of groups as derived subgroups.

InformationTheory.title: Information Theory
InformationTheory.description: Information theory quantifies information, uncertainty, compression, and transmission through entropy and coding.

fields.title: Entropy and mutual information
fields.description: Shannon entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Kullback–Leibler divergence, the basic measures of uncertainty and dependence between random variables.

fields.title: Information inequalities
fields.description: Inequalities relating entropies, divergences and mutual information, such as the log-sum, Pinsker, Fano, data-processing and Shearer inequalities.

fields.title: Source coding
fields.description: Lossless compression of information sources by variable-length codes, including prefix codes, the Kraft–McMillan inequality and Shannon's source coding bounds.

fields.title: Channel simulation
fields.description: Simulating a noisy channel with shared randomness and auxiliary random variables, including one-shot channel simulation and the functional representation lemma.

fields.title: Error-correcting codes
fields.description: Codes that detect or correct transmission errors, including linear codes, Hamming and Reed–Solomon codes, cyclic redundancy checks, and the Hamming-space geometry used to bound them.

fields.title: Channel coding
fields.description: Reliable transmission over noisy channels: channel capacity, Shannon's noisy-channel coding theorem, and its weak and strong converses.

fields.title: Signal processing and detection
fields.description: Discrete and continuous signals and linear time-invariant systems, sampling and reconstruction, filtering and frequency response, quantization, modulation and detection.

LinearAlgebra.title: Linear Algebra
LinearAlgebra.description: Linear algebra studies vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, duality, dimension, and spectral structure.

fields.title: Bases and dimension
fields.description: Linear independence, spanning families and bases of modules and vector spaces, rank and dimension (finite and infinite), finite-dimensional vector spaces, free modules and free modules over principal ideal domains, and the invariant basis number property.

fields.title: Linear maps and duality
fields.description: Vector spaces and modules, linear maps and their invariants such as trace, dual spaces, dual bases and perfect pairings, and exactness of sequences of linear maps.

fields.title: Matrices and matrix algebra
fields.description: Matrices over rings and their algebra: matrix multiplication, transposes and conjugate transposes, block matrices, permutation matrices, Kronecker products, matrices of linear maps and of bilinear and sesquilinear forms, invertibility and rank. Determinants, eigenvalues, decompositions and special classes such as diagonal matrices have their own fields.

fields.title: Eigenvalues and canonical forms
fields.description: Eigenvalues, eigenspaces and characteristic polynomials of matrices and endomorphisms, the normal forms they lead to (diagonalization, triangularization, Jordan and Smith normal forms), and eigenvalue algorithms (power iteration and the Rayleigh quotient).

fields.title: Matrix decompositions and linear systems
fields.description: Factorizations of matrices (QR, singular value, polar, Schur and LU decompositions), Gaussian elimination and the solvability of linear systems, linear least squares, Krylov subspace methods (Arnoldi, Lanczos, GMRES, conjugate gradients) and condition numbers.

fields.title: Determinants and matrix identities
fields.description: Determinant expansions and identities, determinants of special products and exponentials, derivatives of determinants, and algebraic identities between matrices.

fields.title: Positive definite matrices and matrix inequalities
fields.description: Positive definite and semidefinite matrices, criteria for definiteness, and inequalities for their determinants, traces and eigenvalues.

fields.title: Bilinear and quadratic forms
fields.description: Bilinear and quadratic forms on vector spaces and modules: rank, orthogonal sums, inertia and congruence, and lattices with their duals and neighbours.

fields.title: Tensor products and multilinear algebra
fields.description: Multilinear and alternating maps, tensor products of modules and of families of modules, tensor, symmetric and exterior powers and algebras, and Clifford algebras with their spin groups. Bilinear and quadratic forms have their own field.

fields.title: Root systems
fields.description: Root systems and root data in paired modules: reflections, root strings, simple roots and bases, Cartan matrices and their realizations, invariant bilinear forms and Weyl groups. Lie algebras constructed from root systems are under Algebra.

fields.title: Special matrices
fields.description: Classes of matrices defined by their structure or entries: Toeplitz, Hankel and circulant matrices, Hadamard and sign matrices, combinatorial matrices, nonnegative, row-stochastic, doubly stochastic and totally positive matrices.

Logic.title: Logic
Logic.description: Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.

fields.title: Type-theoretic foundations
fields.description: Propositional reasoning and constructions of dependent type theory: empty and inhabited types, unique existence, subtypes, quotients, universes and inductive and coinductive types. Formal propositional and first-order systems as objects of study have their own fields.

fields.title: Propositional logic and satisfiability
fields.description: Classical propositional logic: truth-table semantics, natural deduction and its completeness, functional completeness, normal forms and CNF transformations, resolution, interpolation, SAT-solving procedures (Davis–Putnam, DPLL, 2-SAT, Horn-SAT) and binary decision diagrams.

fields.title: First-order logic
fields.description: Syntax, proof calculi and semantics of first-order predicate logic, including soundness and Gödel's completeness theorem.

fields.title: Proof theory
fields.description: Structural study of formal proofs and provability: sequent calculi, linear logic and translations into it, and Gödel's incompleteness theorems.

fields.title: Modal logic
fields.description: Logics of necessity and possibility interpreted on Kripke models, their axiomatizations, completeness and decidability, and extensions such as epistemic logic, dynamic logic and the modal μ-calculus.

fields.title: Temporal logic and model checking
fields.description: Linear and branching-time temporal logics interpreted over infinite words and transition systems, with automata-theoretic and fixed-point model-checking procedures.

fields.title: Model theory
fields.description: Relations between formal theories and their structures: first-order languages of algebraic structures, quantifier elimination, categoricity and o-minimality.

MeasureTheory.title: Measure Theory
MeasureTheory.description: Measure theory provides the language of size and integration underlying probability and modern analysis.

fields.title: Measurable spaces and measurable functions
fields.description: σ-algebras and their generation, measurable maps and isomorphisms, product and countably generated σ-algebras, and Borel structures on topological and Polish spaces. Measures and their extensions are in Measures and measurable sets.

fields.title: Measures and measurable sets
fields.description: Construction and uniqueness of measures, atomless and vector measures, measures on Boolean algebras, and the limits of measurability shown by non-measurable sets and paradoxical decompositions.

fields.title: Absolute continuity, densities and decompositions
fields.description: Absolute continuity and singularity for pairs of positive measures, densities, the unsigned Hahn decomposition, Lebesgue decomposition and the Radon–Nikodym theorem. Signed and vector-valued analogues belong to Signed and vector measures.

fields.title: Signed and vector measures
fields.description: Signed, complex and vector-valued measures: construction, Hahn and Jordan decomposition, variation, Stieltjes vector measures and integration. Lyapunov’s range convexity theorem remains in Measures and measurable sets.

fields.title: Lebesgue measure
fields.description: Lebesgue measure on the real line and Euclidean space: volumes of concrete bodies, null sets and density phenomena.

fields.title: Covering theorems and differentiation of measures
fields.description: Vitali and Besicovitch covering theorems, Vitali families, differentiation of one measure with respect to another, doubling measures and Lebesgue's density and differentiation theorems; differentiation of real functions of bounded variation is in Differentiation of real functions.

fields.title: Haar measure and fundamental domains
fields.description: Invariant measures on locally compact groups, unimodularity, and fundamental domains for the actions of discrete subgroups.

fields.title: Integration and convergence
fields.description: The Lebesgue integral and its convergence theorems, modes of convergence of measurable functions, approximation by simple functions, product measures, convolution, differentiation under the integral sign and integral inequalities.

fields.title: Lebesgue spaces
fields.description: The spaces Lp of p-th power integrable functions: membership criteria, inclusions, dense subspaces, the essential supremum and weak convergence.

fields.title: Differentiation of real functions
fields.description: Absolutely continuous, Lipschitz and bounded-variation functions of a real variable, maximal functions and almost-everywhere properties of real functions.

fields.title: Optimal transport
fields.description: Couplings of probability measures, transport costs, existence of optimal couplings, Kantorovich duality, Wasserstein distances and Brenier's theorem, displacement convexity and Wasserstein gradient flows (the JKO scheme).

fields.title: Geometric measure theory
fields.description: Hausdorff measures and dimension, dimension functions and codimension, fractal sets such as attractors of iterated function systems, and the measure and dimension of distance sets.

NumberTheory.title: Number Theory
NumberTheory.description: Number theory studies integers, primes, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and their analytic and algebraic structure.

fields.title: Congruences and power residues
fields.description: Modular arithmetic: Wilson, Wolstenholme and Fermat-quotient congruences, lifting the exponent, primitive roots, Legendre/Jacobi symbols, reciprocity, covering systems.

subfields.title: Congruences and modular arithmetic
subfields.description: Congruences for factorials, quotients and power sums (Wilson, Wolstenholme, Fermat quotients), lifting the exponent, multiplicative order, primitive roots, residue systems.

subfields.title: Power residues and reciprocity
subfields.description: Quadratic and cubic residues, Legendre, Jacobi and Kronecker symbols, quadratic reciprocity and its extensions, Legendre-symbol sums.

subfields.title: Covering systems
subfields.description: Covering and exact covering systems of residue classes, minimum moduli, Erdős–Graham and Fraenkel-type results.

fields.title: Primes, divisibility and factorization
fields.description: Divisibility, factorization and individual primes: divisors, greatest common divisors, Bézout's identity, coprimality and prime factorization; special prime families, primality criteria, pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers, Fermat and Mersenne numbers.

subfields.title: Divisibility and factorization of integers
subfields.description: Elementary arithmetic of the natural numbers and integers: divisibility, divisors and divisor sets, greatest common divisors and least common multiples, Bézout's identity and the Euclidean algorithm, coprimality, prime factorization and multiplicities of prime factors; primality tests and special primes are in the neighbouring subfields, congruences in Congruences and power residues.

subfields.title: Primality tests and pseudoprimes
subfields.description: Primality criteria (Proth, Pocklington, Lucas–Lehmer), Fermat, Lucas, Frobenius and strong pseudoprimes, Carmichael and Korselt numbers.

subfields.title: Special classes of primes
subfields.description: Fermat, Mersenne, Sophie Germain, Wieferich, Cullen and other named prime families, Fermat numbers, Sierpiński–Riesel numbers, prime-producing formulas.

fields.title: Distribution of primes
fields.description: Counting primes: prime number theorem, explicit Chebyshev-type bounds, prime gaps and short intervals, primes in progressions, sieves, prime patterns.

subfields.title: Prime number theorem and explicit bounds
subfields.description: PNT and its proofs, Chebyshev theta and psi, explicit bounds for π(x) and the nth prime (Dusart, Axler, Rosser), Mertens constants.

subfields.title: Prime gaps and primes in short intervals
subfields.description: Bertrand-type and Breusch theorems, Ramanujan primes, prime gaps, bounded gaps, Sylvester–Schur on prime factors of consecutive products.

subfields.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions
subfields.description: Dirichlet density, PNT for progressions, Siegel–Walfisz, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Brun–Titchmarsh, prime races.

subfields.title: Sieve methods
subfields.description: Selberg, Brun and large sieves, almost primes, parity problem, counting integers with restricted prime factors via sieves.

subfields.title: Prime patterns and conjectures
subfields.description: Twin primes and Brun's constant, Hardy–Littlewood tuples, Goldbach/Lemoine-type statements, primes represented by polynomials (Friedlander–Iwaniec).

fields.title: Arithmetic functions
fields.description: Divisor sums, totients, Möbius and multiplicative functions, their mean values and extremal orders, and integers classified by them.

subfields.title: Perfect numbers and their relatives
subfields.description: Perfect, multiperfect, odd perfect, abundant, practical, Zumkeller, Giuga, amicable numbers, spoof factorizations, Lehmer's totient problem.

subfields.title: Divisor and totient functions
subfields.description: σ, τ, φ, Jordan and Dedekind ψ, unitary and biunitary divisors, gcd-sums, Ramanujan sums, totient multiplicities and values.

subfields.title: Multiplicative functions and mean values
subfields.description: Dirichlet and unitary convolution, completely multiplicative and additive functions, Wintner and Euler-product mean values, additive uniqueness sets, Mertens bounds.

subfields.title: Integers with restricted factorization
subfields.description: Squarefree, k-free, k-full and powerful, smooth and rough numbers, highly composite numbers, integers with prescribed prime factors.

fields.title: Zeta and L-functions
fields.description: Riemann zeta and xi, Dirichlet characters and L-functions, Dedekind and Artin L-functions, Riemann hypothesis criteria, multiple zeta values.

subfields.title: Riemann zeta function
subfields.description: Continuation and zeros of ζ, zero-free regions, moments and subconvexity, RH criteria (Robin, Lagarias), de Bruijn–Newman constant, zeta values.

subfields.title: Dirichlet characters and L-functions
subfields.description: Dirichlet characters, conductors, primitive and quadratic characters, Dirichlet series continuation, L-function bounds, Artin and Selberg-class functions.

subfields.title: Multiple zeta values
subfields.description: Multiple zeta and zeta-star values, Hoffman bases, word algebras, cyclic sum formulas, finite and q-analogue multiple zeta values.

fields.title: Exponential and character sums
fields.description: Gauss sums, Weyl and Vinogradov sums, incomplete exponential sums, Burgess bounds, Dirichlet polynomials, trigonometric and cotangent sums.

fields.title: Diophantine equations
fields.description: Integer and rational solutions of polynomial and exponential equations, Pell equations, Thue equations, Diophantine tuples, Egyptian fractions.

subfields.title: Exponential Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Equations with unknown exponents: Pillai, Catalan, Størmer, Nagell–Ljunggren, Ramanujan–Nagell and Terai-type equations, powers plus one.

subfields.title: Pell and quadratic Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Pell and negative Pell equations, norm equations, Pythagorean triples, Markov triples and quadratic equations in two or three variables.

subfields.title: Higher-degree Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Thue equations, generalized Fermat equations, sums of cubes, x^y = y^x, abc conjecture, Brocard–Ramanujan and symmetric-function equations.

subfields.title: Diophantine tuples and Egyptian fractions
subfields.description: Diophantine m-tuples, Erdős–Straus problem, Egyptian fraction representations and greedy unit-fraction algorithms.

fields.title: Quadratic forms and sums of squares
fields.description: Representations by quadratic forms: sums of two, three and four squares, binary forms and class numbers, universality theorems, Waring's problem.

subfields.title: Sums of squares and representation numbers
subfields.description: Two-, three- and four-square theorems, Jacobi-type counts, Gaussian and Hurwitz integer methods, x²+2y² and similar representations.

subfields.title: Binary and higher quadratic forms
subfields.description: Reduction theory, discriminants and class numbers of binary forms, quaternary forms, 15 and 290 theorems.

subfields.title: Waring's problem and figurate numbers
subfields.description: Hilbert–Waring, g(3)=9, Fermat polygonal theorem, polygonal, triangular and polytopic numbers and their sums.

fields.title: Diophantine approximation and transcendence
fields.description: Approximating reals by rationals or algebraics, Roth and subspace theorems, linear forms in logarithms, transcendence, uniform distribution, geometry of numbers.

subfields.title: Transcendence and irrationality
subfields.description: Hermite–Lindemann, Lindemann–Weierstrass, Gelfond–Schneider, Mahler functions, irrationality and linear independence of constants.

subfields.title: Roth's theorem and linear forms in logarithms
subfields.description: Thue–Siegel–Roth, Ridout, Schmidt subspace, Baker, Baker–Wüstholz, Matveev bounds, Baker–Davenport reduction, approximation by algebraic numbers.

subfields.title: Uniform distribution and metric approximation
subfields.description: Weyl equidistribution, three-gap theorem, Duffin–Schaeffer, normal numbers, Beatty sequences, discrepancy, lattice points and Minkowski-type theorems.

fields.title: Continued fractions and expansions of reals
fields.description: Continued fractions, Farey sequences, Stern–Brocot tree, Engel, Pierce, Lüroth and similar series expansions of real numbers.

fields.title: Heights and Mahler measure
fields.description: Absolute heights of algebraic numbers, Mahler measure, Lehmer's problem, Dobrowolski bounds, Schinzel–Zassenhaus, house and trace problems.

fields.title: Algebraic number theory
fields.description: Number fields and rings of integers: quadratic and cyclotomic fields, discriminants, ramification, ideals, adeles and ideles, class field theory, Galois cohomology and p-adic representations.

subfields.title: Number fields and embeddings
subfields.description: Number fields, their rings of integers, embeddings and signatures, CM fields, Minkowski geometry and class-number finiteness. Units, regulators, ideals and ramification belong to Discriminants, ramification and ideals; the theory of places belongs to Adeles, ideles and class field theory.

subfields.title: Quadratic fields and integer rings
subfields.description: Gaussian, Eisenstein and ℤ[√d] integers, prime factorization there, imaginary quadratic discriminants, class numbers, Stark–Heegner.

subfields.title: Cyclotomic fields
subfields.description: Cyclotomic fields and polynomials, real cyclotomic polynomials, 2cos(2πk/n), cyclotomic units, ramification and inertness in cyclotomic fields.

subfields.title: Discriminants, ramification and ideals
subfields.description: Discriminants and their bounds, ramification and inertia, orders, units, ideal counting, local degrees under completion, field enumeration and towers.

subfields.title: Adeles, ideles and class field theory
subfields.description: Places, adeles and ideles, ray class groups, Artin map, Hilbert class fields, Neukirch–Uchida-type Galois characterization.

subfields.title: Galois representations and p-adic Hodge theory
subfields.description: ℓ-adic and p-adic representations of the Galois groups of local and global fields and their Galois cohomology: Galois cohomology of local and global fields (local Tate duality, Euler characteristic formulas, the Poitou–Tate sequence, Selmer and Bloch–Kato groups), Weil–Deligne representations and the ℓ-adic monodromy theorem, Fontaine's period rings with crystalline, semistable, de Rham and Hodge–Tate representations and (φ, Γ)-modules, p-adic comparison theorems for varieties and p-divisible groups, and prismatic cohomology. Class field theory is under Adeles, ideles and class field theory, cohomology of abstract groups under group cohomology, ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes under Grothendieck topologies on schemes, and Galois representations of elliptic curves under elliptic curves.

fields.title: p-adic numbers and local fields
fields.description: p-adic integers and expansions, valuations of integer sequences, Hensel lifting, Strassmann's theorem, Hilbert symbols, p-adic gamma, local fields.

fields.title: Modular forms, q-series and partitions
fields.description: Modular forms and functions, congruence subgroups, Ramanujan tau, theta functions, mock theta functions, Lambert series, partition congruences.

subfields.title: Modular forms
subfields.description: Modular and cusp forms, congruence subgroups, cusps, Eisenstein series congruences, Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture, spectral gaps.

subfields.title: Theta functions and q-series
subfields.description: Jacobi and Ramanujan theta functions, q-Pochhammer symbols and Euler products, Rogers–Ramanujan and related continued fractions, mock theta functions, Lambert series and q-series identities.

subfields.title: Partition congruences
subfields.description: Ramanujan-type congruences, dissections and densities for partition functions and their variants (overpartitions, regular, cubic, core, colored, mex, designated-summand and smallest-part partitions), proved with q-series and eta quotients.

fields.title: Linear recurrence sequences
fields.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Pell, Tribonacci and other linear recurrences: identities, divisibility, periods, primitive divisors and Diophantine properties.

subfields.title: Fibonacci and Lucas numbers
subfields.description: Identities, sums, reciprocal series, determinants and generating functions specifically for Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.

subfields.title: Lucas sequences and primitive divisors
subfields.description: General Lucas sequences U_n, V_n, Lucas pairs, divisibility, Bang–Zsigmondy and primitive-divisor theorems, Fibonacci prime divisibility.

subfields.title: Pell, Jacobsthal and other second-order sequences
subfields.description: Pell, Pell–Lucas, Jacobsthal, gibonacci, Horadam, Leonardo, Oresme, bi-periodic and (a,b)-Fibonacci sequences.

subfields.title: Tribonacci and higher-order sequences
subfields.description: Tribonacci, tetranacci, pentanacci, k-generalized Fibonacci, Padovan, Perrin and Narayana sequences, dominant roots and Binet forms.

subfields.title: Fibonacci and Lucas polynomials
subfields.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Jacobsthal and gibonacci polynomials, their sums, squares and generating function values.

subfields.title: General theory of recurrences
subfields.description: C-finite, P-recursive and MC-finite sequences, Binet formulas, Skolem–Mahler–Lech, growth, generating functions and decomposable forms.

subfields.title: Recurrences modulo m
subfields.description: Pisano periods, periods and zero indices of recurrences modulo primes and prime powers, residue distribution.

subfields.title: Diophantine problems in recurrences
subfields.description: Squares, perfect powers, repdigits, factorials and powers of two among terms of recurrence sequences.

fields.title: Special numbers and polynomials
fields.description: Arithmetic of classical number families: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers, harmonic numbers, binomial and Catalan-type coefficients.

subfields.title: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
subfields.description: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, identities, denominators, Kummer congruences, Faulhaber sums, Appell sequences, higher-order and Apostol variants.

subfields.title: Euler, Genocchi and poly-Bernoulli numbers
subfields.description: Euler numbers and polynomials, Genocchi numbers, poly-Bernoulli, Bernoulli of the second kind, degenerate variants.

subfields.title: Harmonic numbers and harmonic sums
subfields.description: Harmonic, hyperharmonic and multiple harmonic sums, binomial-harmonic identities, non-integrality, harmonic congruences, Euler–Mascheroni bounds.

subfields.title: Binomial coefficients and factorials
subfields.description: Divisibility and valuations of binomial coefficients, Lucas-type theorems, factorial ratios and Fibonomial coefficients; b-nomial, totienomial and other generalized binomial coefficients go to Combinatorics.

subfields.title: Catalan and Fuss–Catalan numbers
subfields.description: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Lucasnomial and FiboCatalan numbers: integrality and prime divisibility.

fields.title: Digits and numeration systems
fields.description: Base-b digits of integers, repdigits and palindromes, Kaprekar and happy numbers, Zeckendorf and base-φ systems, automatic sequences.

subfields.title: Digit properties of integers
subfields.description: Digit sums and products, Niven, happy, Kaprekar, Keith numbers, comma sequences, decimal expansions of fractions (Midy, repetends).

subfields.title: Repdigits, palindromes and reverse multiples
subfields.description: Repdigits, palindromes, reverse multiples and Young graphs, permutiples, digit reversal, special squares by digits.

subfields.title: Numeration systems and automatic sequences
subfields.description: Zeckendorf, base-φ, negative and signed bases, Cobham's theorem, base-recognizable sets, Mahler substitution, regular sequences.

fields.title: Integer sequences
fields.description: Named nonlinear integer sequences: Collatz and iterated maps, self-referential sequences, Sylvester and Euclid sequences, realizable and Dold sequences.

subfields.title: Iterated maps and self-referential sequences
subfields.description: Collatz problem, EKG, Stern diatomic, Hofstadter, Golomb, Ulam, Ducci, Josephus and Conway-type sequences.

subfields.title: Arithmetic properties of sequences
subfields.description: Dold, Newton and realizable sequences, Sylvester, Euclid and Göbel sequences, gcd and divisibility sequences, OEIS-specific sequences.

fields.title: Additive number theory
fields.description: Representing integers as sums from special sets, and the density of integer sets: sumsets of integers, subset sums and complete sequences, primitive sets, natural and logarithmic density, Romanoff's theorem; additive bases and complements and zero-sum constants go to additive combinatorics.

fields.title: Numerical semigroups and the Frobenius problem
fields.description: Sylvester's coin theorem, Frobenius numbers, pseudo-Frobenius sets and numerical semigroups generated by special sequences.

fields.title: Arithmetic geometry
fields.description: Rational points of varieties over number fields: torsion and rank of elliptic curves, naive heights, Hasse principle, local-global failures.

fields.title: Arithmetic of function fields
fields.description: Number-theoretic analogues over F_q[T] and finite fields: polynomial primes, h-free polynomials, function-field adeles, positive-characteristic zeta values.

Order.title: Order Theory
Order.description: Order theory studies comparison relations, lattices, intervals, monotonicity, and order-complete constructions.

fields.title: Ordered sets
fields.description: Partial, strict and total orders, dense linear orders, monotone maps and sequences, and representations of finite posets.

fields.title: Well-founded orders and order types
fields.description: Well-founded relations and well-orders, well-founded and partially well-ordered sets, well-quasi-orders, initial and principal segments, order types and their arithmetic, and transfinite constructions along well-orders. Ordinals and cardinals are under Set Theory.

fields.title: Intervals, covers and graded orders
fields.description: Intervals and order-connected sets, locally finite orders, the covering relation, successor and predecessor orders, chains and relation series, graded orders, and the height and Krull dimension of partially ordered sets.

fields.title: Lattices and Boolean algebras
fields.description: Lattices and Boolean algebras, their representation theorems, and Boolean functions viewed as maps between Boolean lattices.

fields.title: Filters and ultrafilters
fields.description: Filters on a set as an order-theoretic structure: the lattice of filters, filter bases, images and products of filters, eventual properties and limits along filters (including limits at infinity and limits superior and inferior), germs, ultrafilters and ultraproducts. Convergence in topological spaces is under Topology; order ideals and filters of a lattice are under lattices.

fields.title: Fixed points and domain theory
fields.description: Least and greatest fixed points of monotone and Scott-continuous maps, Kleene iteration, and the complete partial orders that underlie denotational semantics.

Probability.title: Probability
Probability.description: Probability studies random phenomena through distributions, expectation, independence, concentration, and stochastic processes.

fields.title: Foundations of probability
fields.description: Probability measures and laws of random variables, expected value and the change of variables formula, construction of probability measures and processes (Kolmogorov extension, measures from Stieltjes functions), independence and the Borel–Cantelli lemmas, conditional expectation and regular conditional distributions, exchangeability and de Finetti's theorem, and zero–one laws for sequences (Kolmogorov, Hewitt–Savage); zero–one laws for continuous processes go to Brownian motion and stochastic calculus, tail sigma-algebras of random walks to Random walks.

fields.title: Markov kernels and disintegration
fields.description: Measurable families of measures, their composition, products, integration, densities, disintegration and the Ionescu–Tulcea theorem. Regular conditional distributions are in Foundations of probability; Markov chains as processes have their own field.

fields.title: Expectation, variance and moments
fields.description: Means, variances and covariances, among them the variance of a sum and Chebyshev's inequality, central moments, conditional variance, covariance forms and operators, and moment- and cumulant-generating functions; the definition of the expected value and the change of variables formula are in Foundations of probability. Characteristic functions and probability-generating functions have their own field, as do the other concentration inequalities.

fields.title: Stochastic processes and stopping times
fields.description: General processes indexed by time: filtrations, adapted, progressively measurable and predictable processes, stopping times, stopped processes and hitting times, indistinguishable processes and modifications, finite-dimensional distributions and localization of process properties; martingales and Brownian motion have their own fields.

fields.title: Probability distributions
fields.description: Named discrete and continuous laws and their moments, densities, mass functions and tails, together with distribution functions, quantiles, medians and joint laws; sampling laws used in tests (t, F) go to Linear models and multivariate analysis.

subfields.title: Discrete distributions
subfields.description: Laws on countable sets, with their mass functions, moments and tails: discrete uniform, binomial, Poisson, Poisson binomial, hypergeometric, multinomial, negative binomial and beta-binomial laws, and expectation under a probability mass function.

subfields.title: Continuous distributions
subfields.description: Laws with densities, with their moments and tails: beta, gamma, exponential, Laplace, chi-square, log-normal, Weibull and Dirichlet laws, the multivariate normal law with Gaussian conditioning, orthant probabilities and L² limits, and the Poisson–Gamma duality.

subfields.title: Distribution functions and quantiles
subfields.description: Cumulative distribution functions and their continuity points, quantile functions and inverse transform sampling, medians, and joint laws.

fields.title: Characteristic functions and generating functions
fields.description: Characteristic functions, probability generating functions and positive-definite functions (Bochner), Taylor bounds for characteristic functions, lattice support, Lévy's continuity theorem and Cramér's decomposition theorem for the normal law.

fields.title: Infinitely divisible laws and regular variation
fields.description: Infinitely divisible and stable distributions, convolution powers, the Lévy–Khintchin representation, and regularly varying and slowly varying functions (Karamata's theorem, Potter bounds, generalized inverses) with the truncated moments and tail integrals of heavy-tailed laws.

fields.title: Convergence of probability measures
fields.description: Weak convergence and convergence in probability, tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, Helly selection, Skorokhod representation, the continuous mapping theorem, the Cramér–Wold device and total variation distance; specific limit laws go to the limit-theorem fields.

fields.title: Laws of large numbers and random series
fields.description: Almost-sure behaviour of sums of independent variables: strong and weak laws of large numbers, Kolmogorov's three-series theorem and maximal inequality, truncation techniques, the law of the iterated logarithm, and the Monte Carlo variance rate of sample means.

fields.title: Central limit theorems and Poisson approximation
fields.description: Convergence in law of normalized sums and their error terms: central limit theorems (Lindeberg–Feller, lacunary and infinite-variance variants), Berry–Esseen bounds and constants, global and local de Moivre–Laplace theorems, Edgeworth expansions, Donsker's invariance principle, and Poisson limit theorems for binomial and urn models.

fields.title: Concentration inequalities
fields.description: Non-asymptotic tail and moment bounds: Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Efron–Stein, Khintchine and Paley–Zygmund inequalities, sampling without replacement, sub-exponential variables and Bernstein's inequality, chi-square and Gaussian Lipschitz concentration, sub-Gaussian convex comparison, Talagrand's convex distance and concentration inequality, and hypercontractivity (Bonami–Beckner, p-biased two-point inequalities) on the discrete cube.

fields.title: Large deviations
fields.description: Large deviation principles and rate functions, Cramér's theorem and Chernoff bounds for empirical means, log-moment generating functions and the Legendre–Fenchel transform used to build them, principles at other speeds, and the Ben Arous–Guionnet principle for the empirical spectral measure of Gaussian ensembles.

fields.title: Martingales and optional stopping
fields.description: Discrete-time martingales, sub- and supermartingales: convergence theorems (almost sure, L^p, backwards, Lévy's downward theorem), uniform integrability, Doob's maximal inequalities, orthogonality and conditional variance of increments, optional stopping in all its forms, and Wald's equations for stopped sums. Finite-horizon optimal stopping by the Snell envelope, and the secretary problem. Martingale measures and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing.

fields.title: Random walks
fields.description: Sums of i.i.d. steps as processes: the drift/oscillation dichotomy, limsup and liminf of partial sums, tail measurability of asymptotic events, the strong Markov property of i.i.d. sequences at stopping times, and ballot theorems.

fields.title: Markov chains
fields.description: Discrete-time Markov chains (construction, path measures, finite-dimensional distributions, Chapman–Kolmogorov, Markov and strong Markov properties), finite chains, ergodicity and convergence to stationarity, mixing, reversibility and Kolmogorov's cycle criterion, finite continuous-time Markov chains with rate matrices, semigroups and hitting times, and Dirichlet forms of symmetric Markov processes.

fields.title: Branching processes
fields.description: Galton–Watson processes, extinction probabilities, total progeny and the hitting-time theorem, and linear birth–death processes.

fields.title: Brownian motion and stochastic calculus
fields.description: Continuous-time processes with continuous paths or independent increments: the construction and sample-path properties of Brownian motion, Kolmogorov's continuity theorem, Blumenthal-type zero–one laws, the simple and strong Markov properties and the reflection principle, quadratic variation, the Itô integral and Itô's formula, Lévy's characterisation and Girsanov's theorem, stochastic differential equations, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and Fokker–Planck equations for diffusions.

fields.title: Point processes and stationary processes
fields.description: Poisson processes on the line and Poisson point processes on general spaces (arrival times, counts, restriction theorem), and stationary random functions.

fields.title: Random fields on lattices
fields.description: Spin and bond configuration spaces, Bernoulli product measures and cylinder events, Gibbs-type conditional distributions given the outside of a region, translation invariance and ergodicity, weak and monotone limits of measures on configuration space, and marginals and conditional independence for weights on finite configuration spaces.

fields.title: Percolation
fields.description: Bernoulli bond and site percolation: percolation probability, critical points, number and uniqueness of infinite clusters, sharpness and sharp thresholds, and crossing estimates in two dimensions.

subfields.title: Phase transition and critical probability
subfields.description: The percolation probability theta, bounds 0 < p_c < 1 (Peierls and enclosure arguments), percolation on product graphs, the number and uniqueness of infinite clusters (Burton–Keane), and sharp thresholds from influences (KKL).

subfields.title: Sharpness of the phase transition
subfields.description: The Duminil-Copin–Tassion proof of exponential decay below p_c: the quantity phi_p(S), Russo's formula and pivotal edges, exploration and last-exit decompositions, the differential inequality, the mean-field bound and subcritical decay.

subfields.title: Crossing probabilities in two dimensions
subfields.description: Crossings of rectangles and annuli in bond percolation on Z^2, the box-crossing property, gluing and square-root tricks, Russo–Seymour–Welsh theory and planar separation lemmas.

fields.title: Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination
fields.description: Inequalities comparing probabilities of monotone or disjointly occurring events under product measures, and stochastic orderings and monotone couplings of measures.

subfields.title: Harris, FKG and BK inequalities
subfields.description: Increasing events, the Harris and FKG inequalities, Holley's inequality, disjoint occurrence and the van den Berg–Kesten inequality (finite, countable and inhomogeneous), pivotal coordinates and Russo's formula on product spaces.

subfields.title: Reimer's inequality
subfields.description: Reimer's inequality for arbitrary events and its proof machinery: configurations as finsets, down-compression, doubled ground sets, disjoint-pair counts and weighted pair sums, and special and mixed-monotone cases.

fields.title: High-dimensional and geometric probability
fields.description: Probability in high dimension and on geometric objects: log-concave and uniform convex-body laws, isotropic constants, the KLS and thin-shell conjectures and their bounds, random matrices (singularity of Bernoulli matrices, Tracy–Widom limits, singular values of Gaussian matrices, Wigner's semicircle law), free probability (free independence, free cumulants, the R-transform and the free central limit theorem), random Euclidean optimization (Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley), suprema of selector and positive empirical processes (Park–Pham theorems), and uniform laws of large numbers via Rademacher complexity.

fields.title: Statistical estimation
fields.description: Point estimation theory and confidence sets: bias, risk and mean squared error, likelihood and maximum likelihood (consistency and asymptotic normality), Fisher information and Cramér–Rao, sufficiency, factorization (Fisher–Neyman, Halmos–Savage) and Rao–Blackwell, Stein's lemma and James–Stein shrinkage, contiguity and Le Cam's lemmas, asymptotic efficiency (Hájek's convolution theorem and adaptive estimation), and the bootstrap with the Mallows metric. The local asymptotic normality of the log-likelihood ratio is under [local power of the likelihood-ratio test](../hypothesis-testing/local-power-of-the-likelihood-ratio-test/README.md) in Hypothesis testing. Penalized least squares (ridge regression, and the lasso with its soft-thresholding solution for an orthonormal design) is under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md) in Machine learning.

fields.title: Hypothesis testing
fields.description: Tests and their validity and power: Neyman–Pearson, likelihood-ratio, score and Wald tests, monotone likelihood ratio, exact conditional tests (Fisher, Hardy–Weinberg), rank tests and ROC area (Mann–Whitney), permutation p-values, sequential tests (Wald's sequential probability ratio test) and quickest change detection (Shiryaev's rule and CUSUM), multiple testing (familywise error control by Bonferroni, Holm and closed testing; false discovery rate control by Benjamini–Hochberg; and the two-groups model with local and tail-area false discovery rates, Storey's positive false discovery rate and q-values), and meta-analysis and heterogeneity statistics.

fields.title: Linear models and multivariate analysis
fields.description: Multivariate normal theory and linear models: Gaussian maximum likelihood, Cochran's theorem on quadratic forms, t and F sampling laws, Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares, principal component analysis, regularized covariance estimation by banding, Gaussian graphical models, and sparse high-dimensional regression: exact recovery by basis pursuit under the restricted nullspace property, and ℓ₂- and prediction-error bounds for the Lasso under restricted eigenvalue conditions. Ridge regression and the lasso as penalized least squares are under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md), and probabilistic principal component analysis, with the factor-analysis marginal, under [probabilistic principal component analysis](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/unsupervised-learning/probabilistic-principal-component-analysis/README.md), both in Machine learning.

fields.title: Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis
fields.description: Distribution-free and semiparametric methods: empirical distribution functions (Glivenko–Cantelli), U-statistics, the Kaplan–Meier estimator, Cox partial likelihood and the log-rank test, and design-based causal inference with potential outcomes. Park and Pham's theorem on when the supremum of a positive empirical process over a finite family of nonnegative functions is large compared with its expectation is under [suprema of selector and empirical processes](../high-dimensional-probability/suprema-of-selector-and-empirical-processes/README.md) in High-dimensional and geometric probability.

fields.title: Bayesian statistics
fields.description: Bayesian inference and nonparametric priors: the Dirichlet process and stick-breaking, Pólya and Blackwell–MacQueen urns, Ferguson conjugacy, infinite limits of finite mixture and feature models (the Chinese restaurant and Indian buffet processes), and posterior computations. Parametric conjugate models, Bayesian linear regression, expectation–maximization, mean-field variational inference, and Monte Carlo and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling are under [Bayesian inference and sampling](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/bayesian-inference-and-sampling/README.md) in Machine learning. The two-groups model for large-scale testing, in which the local false discovery rate is the posterior probability of the null, is under [Hypothesis testing](../hypothesis-testing/two-groups-model-and-local-false-discovery-rates/README.md).

fields.title: Queueing theory
