fields.description: Sample-path relations between arrivals, sojourn times and occupancy, and normalized balance laws for queueing rate models.

QuantumInformation.title: Quantum Information
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum information studies states, channels, measurement, entanglement, communication, and quantum computation.

fields.title: Quantum foundations
fields.description: Quantum foundations studies what quantum mechanics rules out and allows at the level of measurement outcomes, including contextuality, Bell nonlocality and bounds on quantum correlations.

fields.title: Quantum operations and channels
fields.description: Quantum operations and channels covers the physically allowed transformations of quantum states, such as isometries and completely positive maps, and impossibility results like the no-cloning theorem.

fields.title: Quantum error correction
fields.description: Quantum error correction protects quantum information against noise by encoding it into a subspace of a larger system: quantum codes, the Knill–Laflamme conditions for correctability, and stabilizer and CSS codes.

fields.title: Quantum Shannon theory
fields.description: Information transmission and source coding for quantum states: accessible information, random-access codes, Holevo bounds and Schumacher compression. Quantum error-correcting codes have their own field.

fields.title: Quantum states, distances and entropy
fields.description: Density operators and their purifications, trace distance and fidelity, and continuity bounds for quantum entropy. Transformations of states and channel properties are under quantum operations and channels.

RepresentationTheory.title: Representation Theory
RepresentationTheory.description: Representation theory studies symmetry by realizing groups and algebras as transformations of linear spaces.

fields.title: Representations of groups and monoids
fields.description: Linear representations of monoids and groups over commutative rings: subrepresentations, intertwining maps, invariants and coinvariants, restriction, induction and coinduction, and the category of representations. Ordinary representation theory of finite groups and continuous representations have their own fields.

fields.title: Representations of finite groups
fields.description: Ordinary representation theory of finite groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero: characters, irreducibility, Schur's lemma, multiplicities and the Wedderburn decomposition of the group algebra.

fields.title: Group cohomology
fields.description: Homology, cohomology and Tate cohomology of groups with coefficients in modules, with their functoriality, additivity, periodicity and the Herbrand quotient.

fields.title: Representations of topological and Lie groups
fields.description: Representations of infinite groups and Lie algebras: continuous and unitary representations of compact and topological groups (Peter–Weyl theorem, complete reducibility), continuous representations over topological rings, representations of Lie algebras and of general linear groups (Schur–Weyl duality), and groups characterized by their irreducible representations.

fields.title: Reductive groups over local fields and their representations
fields.description: Reductive groups over archimedean and non-archimedean local fields and their representations: structure theory (parabolic subgroups and their Langlands decompositions, Cartan, Iwasawa and Bruhat decompositions, symmetric spaces of real groups, Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahoric subgroups and Moy–Prasad filtrations, dual and L-groups); smooth and admissible representations of p-adic groups (parabolic induction and Jacquet modules, cuspidal, square-integrable and tempered representations, the Bernstein–Zelevinsky and Zelevinsky classifications for GL(n), Iwahori-fixed vectors and depth); admissible representations, Harish-Chandra modules and smooth globalizations of real reductive groups such as U(p, q), with their discrete series; and the classical and p-adic local Langlands correspondences. Representations of compact and general topological groups and of Lie algebras, and Schur–Weyl duality, are under representations of topological and Lie groups; the Weil representation and the theta correspondence, local and global, are under automorphic forms and representations.

fields.title: Automorphic forms and representations
fields.description: Automorphic forms and automorphic representations of reductive groups over number fields and their adele rings: smooth adelic functions of moderate growth, constant terms and cusp forms, Whittaker models, the decomposition of automorphic representations into local components, multiplicity one, Eisenstein series, the spectral decomposition and trace formulas, Rankin–Selberg and doubling integrals and the L-functions they define, base change, the cohomology of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces with its Hecke action, and the Weil representation and the theta correspondence, local and global (Howe duality, the Siegel–Weil and Rallis inner product formulas). Classical modular forms, theta functions and q-series are under modular forms, q-series and partitions, adelic points of algebraic groups with their measures and class numbers under algebraic number theory, and the representations of the local groups have their own field.

RingTheory.title: Ring Theory
RingTheory.description: Ring theory studies addition and multiplication through ideals, modules, localization, dimension, and homological structure.

fields.title: Commutative rings and ideals
fields.description: Ideals of commutative rings and the operations on them: generation, sums, products, colons and quotients, prime and maximal ideals, radicals, nilpotent elements, coprimality and the Chinese remainder theorem, the Jacobson radical and Jacobson rings, and the prime and maximal spectra with the Zariski topology. Localization is under ideals, localization and ring constructions; fractional ideals are under Dedekind domains.

fields.title: Factorization in integral domains
fields.description: Unique factorization domains and monoids, principal ideal domains, Euclidean and Bézout domains, multiplicities and radicals of elements, contents of polynomials and Gauss's lemma, and criteria for factoriality and irreducibility over integral domains. Divisibility and GCD monoids as such are under algebra; factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains is under Dedekind domains.

fields.title: Noetherian and Artinian rings
fields.description: Rings and modules with chain conditions: Noetherian and Artinian rings and modules, the Hilbert basis theorem, the Hopkins–Levitzki theorem, associated primes and primary decomposition. Krull dimension and length of modules are under local rings.

fields.title: Integral extensions and integral closure
fields.description: Integral and algebraic elements over commutative rings, integral closure and integrally closed domains, primes lying over and the going-up and going-down theorems, and Noether normalization. Dedekind domains have their own field; algebraic field extensions are under field theory.

fields.title: Dedekind domains and ideal theory
fields.description: Dedekind domains and their characterizations, unique factorization of fractional ideals into primes, the ideal class group, invertible fractional ideals and the conductor of an order.

fields.title: Ramification theory
fields.description: How primes split, ramify and stay inert in finite extensions of Dedekind domains and discrete valuation rings, measured by the different, the discriminant, ramification indices, inertia degrees and Frobenius elements.

fields.title: Valuation rings and Henselian rings
fields.description: Discrete valuation rings and general valuation rings, their completions and finite extensions, residue fields, Hensel's lemma and the Krull–Akizuki theorem.

fields.title: Local rings, dimension and completion
fields.description: Local rings and their residue fields, Krull dimension, adic completion, regular local rings and length of modules.

fields.title: Ideals, localization and ring constructions
fields.description: Ideals and submodules under localization, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, Gröbner bases, toric ideals and Markov bases, zero divisors, products of rings and fields, and ring constructions such as Witt vectors.

fields.title: Étale algebras, norms and differentials
fields.description: Algebras over commutative rings: étale algebras and the trace form, norm and trace maps, Kähler differentials and derivations.

fields.title: Syzygies and free resolutions
fields.description: Free resolutions of modules over polynomial rings, Hilbert's syzygy theorem, and graded Betti numbers and Poincaré series of multigraded modules.

fields.title: Formal power series
fields.description: Rings of formal power series in one or several variables and Hahn series, with formal exponentials, derivatives, coefficient operators and Lagrange inversion.

fields.title: Modules over commutative rings
fields.description: Projective, free and finitely generated modules over commutative rings and module-finite extensions: Kaplansky's theorem, the Quillen–Suslin theorem, descent of Noetherianness (Eakin–Nagata) and the direct summand theorem.

fields.title: Invariant theory
fields.description: Rings of invariants of finite groups acting on commutative rings: finiteness of invariant rings and Hilbert–Poincaré series of modular invariant rings of polynomial algebras.

fields.title: Cluster algebras
fields.description: Cluster algebras of Fomin and Zelevinsky: exchange matrices and matrix mutation, seeds and seed mutation, the Laurent phenomenon, rank-two cluster algebras and their periodicity in finite type, Somos sequences, and the finite type classification by Cartan–Killing types. Total positivity of matrices is under Linear algebra.

SetTheory.title: Set Theory
SetTheory.description: Set theory studies membership, cardinality, ordinals, infinity, and foundational constructions for mathematics.

fields.title: Sets, functions and relations
fields.description: Sets and their operations, images and preimages, products, disjoint unions, quotients, functions, bijections, partial maps, relations and countability. Finite subsets and cardinal numbers have separate fields.

fields.title: Finite sets and finite types
fields.description: Finite subsets and finite types: cardinality, lattice operations, products, powersets, bounded natural numbers, finite tuples and symmetric powers. Lists and multisets have their own field; enumerative identities are under Combinatorics.

fields.title: Lists and multisets
fields.description: Finite sequences and collections with repetition: operations on lists, chains, permutations, multisets and multiplicities, fixed-length lists, association lists and finite maps. Sorting algorithms are under Computer Science.

fields.title: Finitely supported functions
fields.description: Functions and dependent families that vanish outside a finite set, their supports, singletons, algebraic operations, orders and descriptions by multiplicities. Free modules and polynomials are treated under Linear Algebra and Algebra.

fields.title: Number systems
fields.description: Construction, embeddings, arithmetic and order of the natural numbers, integers, rationals, real and complex numbers, and extensions by infinity. Divisibility, factorization and modular arithmetic are under Number Theory.

fields.title: Ordinals and ordinal arithmetic
fields.description: Ordinals as order types of well-orders, transfinite arithmetic, normal functions, fixed points, fundamental sequences and ordinal notation. Cardinal arithmetic and general well-founded orders have separate fields.

fields.title: Cardinal arithmetic and cardinal characteristics
fields.description: The arithmetic of infinite cardinals, including the continuum hypothesis and the singular cardinals hypothesis, together with cardinal invariants of the continuum and the cofinal structure of directed sets.

fields.title: Axiomatic set theory and models of ZFC
fields.description: Models of Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, sets and classes, transitive sets, von Neumann ordinals, rank and the cumulative hierarchy, and hereditarily finite sets with atoms. Forcing and large cardinals have their own fields.

fields.title: Large cardinals
fields.description: Cardinals with strong closure or reflection properties, such as inaccessible, Mahlo, weakly compact and measurable cardinals, whose existence cannot be proved in ZFC.

fields.title: Infinitary combinatorics
fields.description: Combinatorics of infinite and uncountable sets: clubs and stationary sets, partition relations, Δ-systems, almost disjoint families, combinatorial principles such as diamond and square, set-theoretic trees, Ramsey ultrafilters and the structure of P(ω)/fin.

fields.title: Forcing and forcing axioms
fields.description: The forcing method and the axioms that assert the existence of generic filters, such as Martin's axiom and the proper forcing axiom, together with combinatorial dichotomies like the open coloring axiom and the P-ideal dichotomy that follow from them.

fields.title: Infinite games and determinacy
fields.description: Infinite two-player games of perfect information on A^ℕ: the Gale–Stewart theorem for open and closed games, Martin's Borel determinacy, analytic determinacy from a measurable cardinal, the failure of the axiom of determinacy under the axiom of choice, and the regularity properties (perfect set property, property of Baire, measurability) that determinacy gives to sets of reals. The Banach–Mazur game on the reals is under Topology/descriptive-set-theory.

StatisticalMechanics.title: Statistical Mechanics
StatisticalMechanics.description: Statistical mechanics studies lattice models of interacting spins and bonds through Gibbs measures, partition functions, correlation inequalities, and phase transitions.

fields.title: Lattice spin models
fields.description: Spin models on finite graphs: the Ising Hamiltonian, Gibbs distribution and partition function and their agreement with the canonical ensemble, the pressure and its independence of boundary conditions, and the Lee–Yang theorem on the zeros of the partition function.

fields.title: Correlation inequalities for spin systems
fields.description: Inequalities for the correlations of ferromagnetic Ising models: the Griffiths (GKS) and FKG inequalities, monotonicity in the couplings and the temperature, and the Griffiths–Hurst–Sherman inequality with its consequences for the magnetization.

fields.title: Gibbs states and phase transitions
fields.description: Infinite-volume states of the Ising model and its phase transition: weak limits of box measures and the DLR condition, translation invariance, ergodicity and extremality of the plus state, spontaneous magnetization and the critical temperature, and Peierls' contour argument for long-range order.

fields.title: Exact solutions and duality
fields.description: Exact results for the two-dimensional Ising model: Kramers–Wannier duality between high- and low-temperature expansions, and Onsager's formula for the free energy through Kac–Ward determinants, Sherman's loop identities and the homology of the torus.

fields.title: Random currents and sharpness
fields.description: The random-current representation of Ising correlations and the switching lemma, and the sharpness of the Ising phase transition: the Simon–Lieb inequality, exponential decay of correlations below the critical point and the mean-field lower bound on the magnetization above it.

fields.title: Random-cluster model
fields.description: The random-cluster (Fortuin–Kasteleyn) model and its Edwards–Sokal coupling with the Potts and Ising models: finite-volume measures, the FKG inequality and comparison with Bernoulli percolation, infinite-volume limits, translation invariance and ergodicity, the free energy, agreement of free and wired measures, and the critical point.

fields.title: Mean-field spin glasses
fields.description: Disordered mean-field spin systems with Gaussian couplings: the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model and its free energy, the Parisi functional, Guerra's replica-symmetry-breaking bound and the Parisi formula.

TheoryOfComputation.title: Theory of Computation
TheoryOfComputation.description: The mathematical study of what can be computed and at what cost: machine models, computability and undecidability, automata and formal languages, and computational complexity.

fields.title: Turing machines
fields.description: Definitions, semantics and programming of Turing machines (single-tape, multi-tape and multi-stack), simulations between tape models, and universal machines with their machine codes. Results showing that a model computes exactly the recursive functions go to Equivalence of models of computation.

subfields.title: Single-tape Turing machines
subfields.description: Single-tape machines: configurations, steps, halting, composition of machines, tape views, state restriction, and translation of multi-stack machines to one tape (simulation and its halting behaviour, not its time cost).

subfields.title: Multi-tape and multi-stack machines
subfields.description: Multi-tape and multi-stack (TM2) machines and their program library: bit primitives, cleanup, composition, stack embeddings and generic host machines that run component machines, and state relabelling.

subfields.title: Universal Turing machines
subfields.description: Codes for machines, clocked evaluators and universal machines, completeness of codes, and the cost of universal simulation. Diagonalization against time-bounded codes goes to Hierarchy theorems.

fields.title: Equivalence of models of computation
fields.description: Register (URM), counter and RAM machines, and theorems that Turing machines and other models compute exactly the partial recursive functions or decide and recognize exactly the recursive and r.e. predicates (Church–Turing equivalences).

fields.title: Computability and undecidability
fields.description: Recursive and recursively enumerable predicates and their closure properties, the halting problem, Rice's and Rice–Shapiro theorems, the recursion and s-m-n theorems, enumerators, index sets such as totality, finiteness and minimal programs, and Busy Beaver functions.

fields.title: Degrees of unsolvability and the arithmetical hierarchy
fields.description: Turing and many-one reducibility, Turing degrees and the jump, recursive isomorphism (Myhill), productive, creative, simple and immune sets, r.e.-completeness, and the arithmetical hierarchy.

fields.title: Undecidable problems
fields.description: Specific undecidable problems and the reductions proving them undecidable: the Post correspondence problem and its variants, string rewriting, undecidable questions about context-free grammars (ambiguity, intersection, universality, regularity), and emptiness of linear bounded automata.

fields.title: Decision procedures for automata, grammars and strings
fields.description: Algorithms deciding questions about finite automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars given as data: emptiness, membership, universality, equivalence, and computable grammar reduction, together with the encodings of automata and grammars they operate on; and satisfiability of string constraints (word equations with regular membership and length bounds).

fields.title: Finite automata and regular languages
fields.description: Deterministic, nondeterministic, two-way and ε-automata, transducers, regular expressions and Kleene's theorem, closure properties of regular languages, automaton minimization, and the algebraic theory of recognition by monoids.

subfields.title: Automata and regular expressions
subfields.description: DFA, NFA, ε-NFA and two-way automata, sequential transducers and Mealy and Moore machines, regular expressions, Thompson's construction and Kleene's theorem, star height, and closure of regular languages under homomorphism, quotient, shuffle and substitution.

subfields.title: Automaton minimization
subfields.description: Nerode equivalence, the minimal automaton and its universal property, and the minimization algorithms of Moore, Hopcroft and Brzozowski with their correctness and cost.

subfields.title: Syntactic monoids and algebraic recognition
subfields.description: Recognition of languages by monoid morphisms, syntactic congruences and monoids, transition monoids, language contexts and quotients, and inverse images under word morphisms.

fields.title: Automata on infinite words and infinite games
fields.description: Büchi, generalized Büchi, parity, Rabin, Streett and Muller automata on infinite words, their emptiness and conversions, and parity games with attractors and traps.

fields.title: Context-free languages
fields.description: Context-free grammars and derivations, normal forms, parsing algorithms, pushdown automata, deterministic and ambiguous languages, closure and non-closure properties, pumping and Ogden's lemmas, and Parikh images.

subfields.title: Grammars, parsing and pushdown automata
subfields.description: Grammar basics and derivation forests, Chomsky and Greibach normal forms, ε- and unit-production elimination, CYK and Earley recognizers, leftmost derivations and (inherent) ambiguity, pushdown automata, deterministic context-free languages, and the grammar–PDA equivalence.

subfields.title: Closure properties and pumping lemmas
subfields.description: Closure of context-free languages under union, concatenation, star, homomorphism, inverse homomorphism, substitution, regular intersection and quotients, non-closure under intersection and complement, the pumping and Ogden lemmas, and Parikh's theorem.

fields.title: Context-sensitive languages
fields.description: Context-sensitive grammars, linear bounded automata and space-bounded single-tape machines, and the equivalence between them.

fields.title: Complexity classes
fields.description: Definitions of time and space complexity on machine models (P, NP, PSPACE, EXP, L, NL, the polynomial hierarchy, FPT and W[1]), polynomial-time encodings and reductions, simulation overheads, Blum measures, and inclusions and collapses among deterministic and nondeterministic classes (Savitch, Immerman–Szelepcsényi, Karp–Lipton, Ladner, Mahaney). Randomized, counting, circuit and quantum classes have their own fields.

fields.title: Hierarchy theorems and proof barriers
fields.description: Time and space hierarchy theorems and diagonalization against time-bounded machines, separations such as P ≠ EXP, and barriers to separating classes: relativization (Baker–Gill–Solovay, oracle separations), natural proofs and algebrization.

fields.title: Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity
fields.description: Probabilistic classes (RP, BPP), Arthur–Merlin and interactive proofs (AM, MA, IP = PSPACE, graph (non)isomorphism), BPP versus nonuniform and alternating classes, randomized reductions (Valiant–Vazirani), and quantum classes BQP and QMA.

fields.title: Counting complexity
fields.description: #P and PP: #P-completeness (counting SAT, permanent), PP-completeness, Toda's theorem, threshold languages, and approximate counting algorithms and schemes (Stockmeyer, Karp–Luby, Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda).

fields.title: Pseudorandomness and one-way functions
fields.description: Complexity-theoretic foundations of cryptography and derandomization: one-way functions, hardcore predicates (Goldreich–Levin), hardness amplification (Yao's XOR lemma), hardness-versus-randomness generators (Nisan–Wigderson), and Impagliazzo's five worlds.

fields.title: Communication complexity
fields.description: Yao's two-party model: deterministic protocols as trees, the rectangle lemma, fooling-set and rank lower bounds, the deterministic complexity of equality, the log-rank conjecture, and randomized protocols with public or private coins (Newman's theorem). Yao's minimax principle for randomized algorithms in general goes to Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity.

fields.title: Boolean circuit complexity
fields.description: Boolean circuits as a model of computation, including arithmetic circuits built from gates (adders, two's complement), parallel classes AC0, NC1 and NC, and circuit lower bounds (parity and majority not in AC0, Smolensky, Razborov's monotone bound, Shannon counting, Williams).

fields.title: Algebraic complexity
fields.description: Arithmetic circuits over a field and the complexity of algebraic problems: matrix multiplication exponents (square, rectangular, dual) and their bounds, tensor rank, and the bit complexity of integer multiplication.

fields.title: Descriptive complexity
fields.description: Logical characterizations of complexity classes on finite structures: Fagin's theorem, Immerman–Vardi (least fixed point and P), and transitive closure logic and NL.

fields.title: Kolmogorov complexity
fields.description: Algorithmic information content of individual strings: universal description methods, incompressible strings, non-computability and upper semicomputability of Kolmogorov complexity.

fields.title: NP-completeness
fields.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and NP-completeness of specific decision problems, by the problem's domain; includes both machine-level Karp reductions and stated NP-completeness results.

subfields.title: Cook–Levin theorem
subfields.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and its machinery: SAT verifiers, dense and binary CNF encodings and converters between them, tableau formulas and the generator machines that emit them.

subfields.title: Satisfiability and constraint satisfaction
subfields.description: Variants of SAT and CSP: 3SAT and the SAT-to-3SAT reduction, bounded-occurrence, monotone, not-all-equal and 1-in-3 SAT, MAX-SAT, MAX-2SAT, MIN-ONES, circuit SAT, binary CSP and betweenness.

subfields.title: Cliques, covers and domination in graphs
subfields.description: Clique, independent set, vertex cover, domination variants, feedback vertex and arc sets, odd cycle transversal, bicliques, densest subgraph, induced matching and minimum fill-in.

subfields.title: Graph coloring, cuts and layouts
subfields.description: Vertex, edge, list and precoloring-extension coloring, achromatic number, graph homomorphism, maximum and k-cuts, bisection, multiway cut, partition into triangles or paths, bandwidth, linear arrangement and linear ordering.

subfields.title: Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems
subfields.description: Hamiltonian paths and cycles, longest paths and cycles, disjoint paths and path covers, constrained spanning and Steiner trees, minimum equivalent digraph, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing, and (induced) subgraph isomorphism.

subfields.title: Network design, spanning trees and routing
subfields.description: Constrained spanning trees and forests (bounded diameter, bounded components, capacities), connectivity and diameter augmentation, superconcentrators, phylogenetic tree construction, and arc, postman, bus and delivery routing. The classical spanning tree, Steiner tree, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing problems are under Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems.

subfields.title: Code generation and register allocation
subfields.description: Optimal code generation: parallel assignments, address expressions, unfixed variable locations, and expression evaluation with unlimited registers, with and without commutativity.

subfields.title: Number partitioning, knapsack and packing
subfields.description: Subset sum, subset product, partition, 3-partition, multiway partition, knapsack variants, bin and strip packing, numerical 3-dimensional matching and 0-1 integer programming.

subfields.title: Set systems, assignment and location
subfields.description: 3-dimensional matching, exact cover, set cover, set packing, set splitting, maximum coverage, minimum test set, generalized and quadratic assignment, facility location, k-center and k-median.

subfields.title: Databases, concurrency control and protection
subfields.description: Relational database design and querying (keys, prime attributes, normal forms, covers of functional dependencies, evaluation, containment and folding of conjunctive queries, index selection, anonymization), concurrency control (serializability of histories, locking policies, deadlock) and safety of protection systems.

subfields.title: Scheduling problems
subfields.description: Single-machine, parallel-machine, flow-shop, precedence-constrained and resource-constrained scheduling with deadlines, tardiness or weighted completion objectives.

subfields.title: Strings, puzzles and Latin squares
subfields.description: String problems (closest string, longest common subsequence, shortest common supersequence) and puzzles (Sudoku, Nonogram, Akari, Minesweeper, Latin square completion).

fields.title: Probabilistically checkable proofs and inapproximability
fields.description: The PCP theorem and Dinur's gap amplification, optimization classes (NPO, APX, MAXSNP), and hardness of approximation results such as Håstad's MAX-3SAT bound and the absence of a PTAS for MAX-CUT.

fields.title: Completeness for other complexity classes
fields.description: Problems complete for classes other than NP: P (circuit value), NL (s-t connectivity), coNP (UNSAT), PSPACE (TQBF, Geography), levels of the polynomial hierarchy (QSAT_k), EXP, NEXP and EXPSPACE (succinct problems, regular expressions with squaring).

fields.title: Problems solvable in polynomial time
fields.description: Proofs or statements that specific problems lie in P or L: graph reachability (PATH) with its marking machine, undirected connectivity in L, 2-SAT, primality, matching, maximum flow, linear programming, integer programming in fixed dimension, and hypergraph matching and cut questions.

fields.title: Fine-grained and exponential-time complexity
fields.description: Exact running times of hard problems beyond the polynomial/non-polynomial divide: exponential, subexponential and quasipolynomial algorithms for NP-hard or NP-intermediate problems, such as the tensor-network 2^o(n)-time algorithm for 3-SAT and Babai's quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism theorem, and the exponential time hypothesis.

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.description: Topology studies continuity, open sets, compactness, connectedness, and invariants preserved by homeomorphism.

fields.title: Topological spaces and continuous maps
fields.description: Foundations of point-set topology: open and closed sets, closure and interior, neighbourhood filters, limits and cluster points, continuity, bases and countability axioms, subspace, product, sum and quotient topologies, the lattice of topologies, embeddings, open, closed and quotient maps, and homeomorphisms; connectedness, separation and finer invariants are in General topology.

fields.title: General topology
fields.description: Point-set topology of topological and metric spaces: connectedness, separation and cardinal invariants, homogeneous spaces, direct and inverse limits of spaces, restricted products, and dimension theory.

fields.title: Compactness and compactifications
fields.description: Compact, locally compact, σ-compact, Lindelöf, countably compact and paracompact spaces, compactly generated spaces, proper maps, and the one-point and Stone–Čech compactifications; compactness in metric and uniform spaces is under those fields.

fields.title: Metric spaces
fields.description: Metric, pseudometric and extended metric spaces: balls, boundedness and diameter, Cauchy sequences and completeness, Lipschitz, Hölder and antilipschitz maps, isometries and dilations, Hausdorff distance and thickenings, covering numbers, ultrametrics and metrizability; curvature, geodesics and Gromov–Hausdorff convergence are in Geometry's metric geometry.

fields.title: Uniform spaces
fields.description: Uniform structures and uniform continuity, Cauchy filters, completeness and Hausdorff completion, total boundedness, uniform, locally uniform and compact convergence, equicontinuity and the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem; uniform groups and rings are under Topological groups and Topological rings, fields and algebras.

fields.title: Ordered topological spaces
fields.description: Order topologies and order-closed topologies on ordered sets: the intermediate value theorem, compactness of intervals, monotone functions and their one-sided limits, liminf and limsup, local extrema, semicontinuity, the extended real line, upper, lower, Scott and Lawson topologies, topological lattices, and Priestley and Esakia spaces.

fields.title: Spaces of continuous functions
fields.description: Spaces of continuous maps with the compact-open topology, bounded continuous functions, functions vanishing at infinity or with compact support, algebras and ideals of continuous functions, locally constant functions, and the Stone–Weierstrass theorem; Banach-space theory of function spaces is in Analysis.

fields.title: Descriptive set theory
fields.description: The topology of Polish spaces and their definable subsets: classical characterizations of Cantor space, Baire space and the rationals, Borel complexity, Bernstein sets and topological games.

fields.title: Continuum theory and infinite-dimensional topology
fields.description: Compact connected spaces, Peano continua and space-filling curves, absolute retracts, hyperspaces, the Hilbert cube and fixed-point properties.

fields.title: Topological groups
fields.description: Groups carrying a compatible topology: metrizability, profinite groups and profinite completions, and functions on locally compact groups.

fields.title: Topological rings, fields and algebras
fields.description: Rings, fields and algebras with compatible topologies: ideals, localization and completion of topological rings, adic and linear topologies, nonarchimedean and valued rings and fields, topological algebras and star algebras, and topological monoids with zero; topological modules and vector spaces have their own field.

fields.title: Topological modules and vector spaces
fields.description: Modules and vector spaces over topological rings with continuous operations: continuous linear, multilinear, alternating and affine maps and equivalences, closed submodules and topological complements, finite-dimensional spaces, module topologies, weak and weak-star topologies, and topologies on spaces of continuous linear maps; normed and Banach spaces are in Analysis.

fields.title: Infinite sums and products
fields.description: Unconditional summation of families in topological monoids, groups, rings and modules: summable families with their sums and products, summation filters, regrouping and reindexing, sums over ℕ and ℤ, sums in ordered spaces and the extended nonnegative reals, uniformly convergent sums of functions and discrete convolution; convergence tests and closed-form series are in Analysis.

fields.title: Categories of spaces and locales
fields.description: Categories of topological spaces and their limits and colimits, compact Hausdorff, profinite and Stonean spaces as used in condensed mathematics, convenient categories such as compactly generated and delta-generated spaces, topological pairs, and locales and frames; individual topological properties are in the point-set fields.

fields.title: Sheaves on topological spaces
fields.description: Presheaves and sheaves on topological spaces with values in a category: equivalent forms of the sheaf condition, stalks, sheafification and étale spaces, pushforward and pullback, skyscraper and flasque sheaves, and sheaves of functions and of rings; sheaves on general sites are in Category theory and sheaves of modules in Algebra.

fields.title: Algebraic topology
fields.description: Homotopy groups, singular homology and other algebraic invariants of spaces, with classical theorems such as Borsuk–Ulam, Hurewicz and Hopf invariant one, and their use on data in topological data analysis: Čech and Vietoris–Rips complexes, persistence modules and barcodes, and Mapper.

fields.title: Simplicial homotopy theory
fields.description: The simplex category, simplicial and cosimplicial objects, simplicial sets with their standard simplices, horns, boundaries, skeleta and subcomplexes, Kan complexes and quasicategories, nerves and homotopy categories, anodyne extensions, simplicial homology, geometric realization, and the Dold–Kan correspondence; model categories are in Model categories and homotopical algebra.

fields.title: Model categories and homotopical algebra
fields.description: Quillen model categories and categories with fibrations, cofibrations and weak equivalences: fibrant and cofibrant objects, cylinders, path objects and homotopies, homotopy categories and the fundamental lemma, Reedy categories and relative cell complexes; localization of categories as such is in Category theory.

fields.title: Manifolds and geometric topology
fields.description: Topological and smooth manifolds in low and high dimensions: surfaces, 3- and 4-manifolds, the Poincaré conjecture, exotic spheres, triangulations, diffeomorphism groups and transformation groups.

fields.title: Knot theory
fields.description: Embeddings of circles in three-space up to ambient isotopy: knot and link diagrams, chirality, slice knots, and geometric invariants such as ropelength, distortion and quadrisecants.

Economics.title: Mathematical Economics
Economics.description: Mathematical economics studies accounting identities, markets, decisions and the quantitative structures used in economic models.

fields.title: Choice, utility and risk
fields.description: Individual decision making: preference relations and choice, ordinal utility representations, revealed preference and Afriat's theorem, expected utility and its paradoxes, risk aversion, certainty equivalents, insurance and stochastic dominance as seen by an expected-utility maximizer. Stochastic orders of measures in general are under Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination in Probability.

fields.title: Consumer theory
fields.description: The consumer's problem and its duality: budget sets, Marshallian demand and its properties, demand for standard utility families, the expenditure and indirect utility functions, Shephard's lemma, the Slutsky equation and matrix, the envelope theorem, and money measures of welfare change such as compensating variation and consumer surplus.

fields.title: Producer theory
fields.description: The competitive firm: production sets and profit maximization, the profit and cost functions and their convexity, concavity and homogeneity, Hotelling's lemma, the law of supply, returns to scale and product exhaustion.

fields.title: Partial equilibrium and public economics
fields.description: Single markets in isolation: supply and demand, existence of partial equilibrium, elasticities, price controls, the incidence and deadweight loss of taxes, and the correction of externalities and provision of public goods (Pigouvian taxes, the Coase theorem, the Samuelson condition). Markets with market power are under imperfect competition.

fields.title: Imperfect competition
fields.description: Markets in which firms have market power: monopoly pricing and the Lerner rule, monopsony, and oligopoly models such as Cournot and Bertrand competition. Equilibrium concepts for strategic games in general are under Game theory.

fields.title: General equilibrium and input–output analysis
fields.description: Economies with many interacting markets: exchange economies, Walras' law, existence of competitive equilibrium, the first and second fundamental theorems of welfare economics, and Leontief's input–output model of interindustry production.

fields.title: International economics
fields.description: Trade between countries and the prices that link them: comparative advantage and Ricardian gains from trade, the Stolper–Samuelson theorem, tariffs, and real exchange rates.

fields.title: Labor markets and income distribution
fields.description: Labor supply and human capital, wage decompositions, flows between employment and unemployment, and the measurement of inequality and poverty: the Gini coefficient, the principle of transfers, inequality-averse social welfare and poverty indices.

fields.title: National accounts, money and prices
fields.description: Macroeconomic measurement and its identities: the product, income and expenditure measures of national accounts, sector balances, stock-flow accounting, price indices and real values, the quantity equation and the Fisher equation linking money, inflation and interest rates.

fields.title: Macroeconomic models
fields.description: Models of the aggregate economy: Solow growth, the golden rule and growth accounting, overlapping generations, intertemporal consumption and Ricardian equivalence, government debt dynamics, the Keynesian cross and IS–LM, loanable funds, the Phillips curve, the Lucas critique and the stability of linear policy models.

fields.title: Financial accounting
fields.description: The arithmetic of a firm's books: double-entry ledgers and the accounting equation, closing entries and retained earnings, depreciation schedules, inventory cost flows, the cash flow statement, and financial ratios such as the DuPont decomposition and the cash conversion cycle.

fields.title: Interest theory and fixed income
fields.description: Present values of deterministic cash flows: discounting and internal rates of return, annuities, perpetuities and loan amortization, bond prices and discount factors, duration, convexity and immunization, cash-flow matching and swap rates. Defaultable bonds, forwards and options are under Asset pricing and financial risk.

fields.title: Asset pricing and financial risk
fields.description: Asset pricing by absence of arbitrage and the measurement of financial risk: static replication, parity relations and no-arbitrage bounds (option payoffs and put–call parity, properties of call prices, forwards and futures, covered interest parity), pricing by replication in one-period and multi-period binomial models and the early exercise of American calls, the Black–Scholes formula and its sensitivities, state prices and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing in state-price form, the law of one price, stochastic discount factors and linear factor pricing, asset and portfolio returns, mean–variance portfolios, the tangency portfolio and the capital asset pricing model, value at risk and expected shortfall, credit risk (expected loss, defaultable bonds), and optimal execution: liquidation schedules trading off quadratic impact costs against inventory risk. The fundamental theorem of asset pricing for martingale measures, in gain form, and finite-horizon optimal stopping and the Snell envelope are under Martingales and optional stopping in Probability; present values of deterministic cash flows, annuities and bonds are under Interest theory and fixed income, and the valuation of firms and their securities under Corporate finance.

fields.title: Corporate finance
fields.description: Valuation of firms and their securities: dividend discount and Gordon growth models, retained earnings and the value of growth, capital structure and the Modigliani–Miller theorems, the debt tax shield, payout policy, debt and equity as claims on the firm's assets, and real options. Pricing of forwards and options by absence of arbitrage, and asset and portfolio returns, are under Asset pricing and financial risk; present values of deterministic cash flows are under Interest theory and fixed income.

fields.title: Inventory, transport and spatial models
fields.description: Quantitative models of stocks and of movement in space: inventory dynamics with lead times and backlogging, accessibility measures of transport networks, and spatial interaction models distributing trips or demand among destinations.

fields.title: Actuarial mathematics
fields.description: Mathematics of insurance and pensions: life tables and survival functions, life insurance and annuity present values and their identities, multiple-state and multiple-life models with reserve recursions and Thiele's equation, aggregate loss models and stop-loss premiums, ruin theory, credibility theory and claims reserving. Interest-only present values are under Interest theory and fixed income; survival estimation from data is under Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis in Probability.

Physics.title: Mathematical Physics
Physics.description: Mathematical physics describes mechanical, electromagnetic and quantum systems through mathematical models and their laws.

fields.title: Quantities, units and measurement
fields.description: Physical quantities and their dimensions in the International System of Quantities, unit conversions and dimensionless groups, and the propagation of measurement uncertainty through linear, linearized and Lipschitz models. Calibration in analytical chemistry is under Chemistry.

fields.title: Classical mechanics
fields.description: Newtonian mechanics of particles, rigid bodies and simple systems, and its application to flight and spaceflight: work, energy and potentials, harmonic, damped, forced and nonlinear oscillators, modal analysis and random response, frames and rigid-body dynamics, statics, linkages and impacts, Newtonian gravitation and orbits, aircraft and spacecraft motion, and elementary models of muscle power and the energy budget of exercise. Elastic structures are under Elasticity and structural mechanics.

subfields.title: Particles, work and oscillations
subfields.description: Newtonian dynamics of particles and lumped systems: kinetic energy, power and the work of conservative forces, harmonic, damped, forced, base-excited and nonlinear oscillators, modal analysis of linear multi-degree-of-freedom systems, the random response of a first-order mechanical system, and elementary models of muscle power and the energy budget of exercise.

subfields.title: Rigid bodies, frames and mechanisms
subfields.description: Frames and rigid bodies: body-fixed and inertial frames, rotating frames and the Coriolis force, rigid-body motion, angular momentum and Euler's equations, statics of force systems, a constrained two-link pendulum, gear trains and linkages, and impacts.

subfields.title: Gravitation and orbital mechanics
subfields.description: Newtonian gravitation and orbits: potentials of point masses and uniform spheres and their superposition, Kepler's third law and orbit averages, two-body orbits, the vis-viva equation and impulsive manoeuvres, regularity of the inverse-square field and the restricted three-body problem.

subfields.title: Flight mechanics and spaceflight
subfields.description: Motion of aircraft and spacecraft: aircraft performance, six-degree-of-freedom flight dynamics with trim and linearization, rocket and electric propulsion, ballistic atmospheric entry, spacecraft attitude with reaction wheels, and mission resource ledgers.

fields.title: Elasticity and structural mechanics
fields.description: Linear elasticity and the mechanics of structures: Cauchy stress, small strain and Mohr's circle, isotropic elastic energy, Euler–Bernoulli beams and their vibration modes, the stiffness method for beams and frames, trusses and their load envelopes, plastic collapse of beams, rigid footings on elastic foundations, and fracture under linear elastic fracture mechanics.

fields.title: Fluid mechanics
fields.description: Hydrostatics and elementary fluid dynamics: hydrostatic pressure and buoyancy, Bernoulli's theorem, Stokes settling, and continuum models of traffic flow with their shocks. Rotating and stratified flows of the ocean and atmosphere, water waves and open-channel hydraulics are under Earth Science.

fields.title: Waves and acoustics
fields.description: Linear waves and acoustics: frequency, wavenumber and wavelength, travelling-wave solutions of the wave equation, sound intensity and pressure levels, transmission of sound through patches and limp panels, Sabine reverberation and the energy of coupled structural–acoustic systems. Water waves are under Earth Science.

fields.title: Quantum mechanics
fields.description: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics: states, observables and the Born rule in finite dimensions, unitary evolution, and exactly solvable models such as the particle in a box and the harmonic oscillator. Quantum chemistry is under Chemistry and quantum information under Quantum Information.

fields.title: Engineering thermodynamics and heat transfer
fields.description: Thermodynamic states and balances of engineering systems, power and refrigeration cycles, exergy, and conduction, convection and radiation heat transfer.

fields.title: Nuclear reactor physics
fields.description: Neutron diffusion and transport models of nuclear reactors: one-group diffusion, buckling and the criticality of bare reactors.

Chemistry.title: Mathematical Chemistry
Chemistry.description: Mathematical chemistry studies quantitative models of chemical systems and reactions.

fields.title: Amounts, composition and stoichiometry
fields.description: Amounts of substance, molar masses and composition, flows of process streams, and the stoichiometry of balanced reactions: conserved balance coordinates, reaction extents, limiting reagents and yields.

fields.title: Chemical thermodynamics
fields.description: Equilibrium thermodynamics of gases and chemical systems: equations of state and the kinetic theory of gases, the canonical ensemble, the first and second laws, the fundamental relation, thermochemistry, Gibbs energy, phase equilibria and the phase rule.

fields.title: Solutions and aqueous equilibria
fields.description: Concentrations of solutions and the equilibria of aqueous systems: charge and mass balances and the proton condition, acid dissociation, carbonate speciation and alkalinity, Henry's law and air–water gas exchange.

fields.title: Chemical kinetics and reactors
fields.description: Rates of chemical reactions and reactors: integrated rate laws and half-lives, the Arrhenius law, conservation laws, deficiency and stochastic dynamics of reaction networks, Turing patterns of the Brusselator, and stirred-tank and box reactors. Biochemical reaction networks are under Biology.

fields.title: Quantum chemistry and spectroscopy
fields.description: Quantum models of atoms and molecules and their spectra: angular momentum, the rigid rotor and hydrogen-like atoms, variational and perturbation methods and Hückel theory, molecular symmetry and vibrational modes, and nuclear magnetic resonance.

fields.title: Analytical chemistry
fields.description: Quantitative chemical analysis: statistical treatment of replicate measurements, calibration lines and inverse prediction with their error budgets, and mass spectrometry and isotope patterns.

EarthScience.title: Earth Science
EarthScience.description: Earth science uses mathematical models to describe the Earth and its physical systems.

fields.title: Solid Earth geophysics
fields.description: Physics of the solid Earth: isostasy and flexure, the density structure of the interior, conductive geotherms and convection, plate motions, the geomagnetic dipole, seismic waves, rays and earthquake magnitudes, and the optics of minerals.

fields.title: Geochronology and stratigraphy
fields.description: Dating of rocks and sediments: radioactive decay and decay chains, radiometric ages, isochrons and the concordia curve, cosmogenic exposure ages, sediment accumulation, hiatuses and decompaction.

fields.title: Geochemistry and biogeochemical cycles
fields.description: Chemical processes in the Earth system: melting and partitioning of trace elements, isotope fractionation, box models of reservoirs and the carbon and nutrient cycles. Aqueous equilibria are under Chemistry.

fields.title: Atmosphere, radiation and climate
fields.description: Thermodynamics and radiation of the atmosphere and the energy balance of the climate: hydrostatic and adiabatic structure, static stability, water vapour and cloud droplets, radiative transfer and optical depth, planetary energy balance and climate feedbacks.

fields.title: Geophysical fluid dynamics
fields.description: Rotating and stratified flows of the ocean and atmosphere: geostrophic and thermal wind balance, Ekman layers, Sverdrup balance, Rossby waves, potential vorticity and quasigeostrophic conservation, shallow-water and surface gravity waves, buoyancy frequency and box models of the ocean circulation.

fields.title: Hydrology and surface processes
fields.description: Water at and below the land surface and the materials it moves through: catchment budgets, infiltration, hydrographs and flood routing, flood frequency, open-channel hydraulics, groundwater flow and solute transport, river water quality, hillslope evolution and soil mechanics.

fields.title: Geophysical data and inversion
fields.description: Observation and analysis of geophysical data: coordinates and grids on the sphere, satellite positioning, sampling and filtering of time series, spatial interpolation and kriging, remote-sensing indices and the null space of tomographic inverse problems.

Algebra.title: Algebra
Algebra.description: Algebra studies structures defined by operations and the laws, morphisms, and symmetries that organize them.

fields.title: Rings and fields
fields.description: Elementary theory of semirings, rings, division rings and fields: homomorphisms and isomorphisms, subrings and subfields, units, idempotents, characteristic and Frobenius, Boolean rings, formally real rings and sums of squares. Divisibility has its own field, ideals and local rings are under ring theory, and extensions of fields are under field theory.

fields.title: Divisibility and greatest common divisors
fields.description: Divisibility in monoids and rings: units and associated elements, irreducible, prime and primal elements, cancellative and regular elements, normalization and GCD monoids, greatest common divisors and least common multiples of finite families; unique factorization domains and ideal-theoretic factorization are under Ring Theory, divisibility of integers under Number Theory.
fields.title: Ordered algebraic structures
fields.description: Monoids, groups, rings, fields and modules with compatible orders: monotone operations, positive cones, lattice-ordered groups and their order-induced absolute values, ring orderings, Archimedean properties, floor and ceiling functions, and order-preserving maps. Orders and lattices as such are under order theory, orderable groups under group theory, and general absolute values and their completions under analysis.

subfields.title: Ordered monoids and groups
subfields.description: Ordered, canonically ordered and linearly ordered monoids and groups: monotonicity of multiplication, truncated subtraction, absolute values, positive and negative parts, lattice-ordered groups, adjoined top and bottom elements, ordered groups with zero, order-preserving monoid homomorphisms and arithmetic of intervals.

subfields.title: Ordered rings and fields
subfields.description: Ordered semirings, rings and fields: positivity and monotonicity of multiplication, order-induced absolute values, positive and nonnegative elements as algebraic structures, positive cones and ring orderings, ordered modules and algebras, and star-ordered rings.
subfields.title: Archimedean structures and floor functions
subfields.description: Archimedean ordered groups and fields, Archimedean classes and the Hahn embedding theorem, conditionally complete ordered fields, floor and ceiling functions, fractional part and rounding, and reduction modulo an interval.
Algebra.title: Finite sums and products
Algebra.description: Sums and products over finite sets, multisets, lists and finitely supported families in commutative monoids: reindexing, splitting and interchange of sums, sums over intervals and antidiagonals, averages, sums in rings and groups with zero, inequalities for finite sums in ordered structures and congruences of sums; infinite sums are under Topology.
Algebra.title: Star rings and involutions
Algebra.description: Involutions on monoids, rings and algebras; self-adjoint, skew-adjoint, normal and unitary elements, projections, star homomorphisms and star subalgebras. Star-ordered rings are under ordered algebraic structures, and C⋆-algebras under analysis.
Algebra.title: Modules over rings
Algebra.description: Modules over rings and semirings: linear maps and equivalences, submodules and their lattice, kernels and images, torsion and torsion-free modules, projective, injective and finitely presented modules, presentations, localization of modules, direct limits and ℤ-lattices. Vector spaces, bases, dimension and matrices are under linear algebra; module-theoretic results of commutative algebra are under ring theory.
Algebra.title: Associative rings and algebras
Algebra.description: Noncommutative rings and finite-dimensional associative algebras, including division and central simple algebras, quaternion algebras, polynomial identities, nil ideals and Hopf algebras. Group rings are under Group Theory.
Algebra.title: Direct sums and graded structures
Algebra.description: Direct sums of groups and modules, internal direct sum decompositions, and graded monoids, rings, algebras and modules, including gradings of monoid algebras. Homogeneous ideals and projective spectra are under ring theory; tensor products are under linear algebra.
Algebra.title: Lie algebras and nonassociative structures
Algebra.description: Lie algebras and their structure and representations, free Lie algebras, Poisson algebras, and racks and quandles.
Algebra.title: Algebraic identities and operations
Algebra.description: Polynomial and product identities, sum-of-squares identities, functional equations on rings, and elementary operations on functions and sets.
Algebra.title: Polynomials and power series
Algebra.description: Univariate and multivariate polynomials and formal power series as algebraic objects: coefficients, derivations, symmetric polynomials, irreducibility, polynomial maps and rational series.
Algebra.title: Univariate polynomial arithmetic
Algebra.description: Arithmetic of polynomials in one indeterminate: coefficients and monomials, degree and leading terms, evaluation and composition, formal differentiation and Taylor expansion, and division with remainder. Multivariate polynomials, special irreducibility criteria and formal power series remain in the parent field; zeros and their multiplicities have their own field.
Algebra.title: Zeros of polynomials
Algebra.description: Location, counting and multiplicity of the zeros of polynomials: real-rootedness, stability, interlacing, root bounds and Sturm sequences.
Algebra.title: Orthogonal polynomials and polynomial sequences
Algebra.description: Classical and combinatorial families of polynomials, their recurrences and generating functions, and orthogonality via Favard's theorem, J-fractions and Riordan arrays.
Algebra.title: Categories of algebraic structures
Algebra.description: Concrete categories of algebraic objects (semigroups, monoids, groups, rings, algebras, coalgebras, Hopf algebras and modules), their limits, colimits, adjunctions and monoidal structures, and presheaves and sheaves of modules. General category theory and abelian categories as such are under category theory.
Algebra.title: Categories of groups and monoids
Algebra.description: Categories of semigroups, monoids, groups, groups with zero and abelian groups: limits and colimits, free–forgetful adjunctions, monomorphisms and epimorphisms, and the abelian category of abelian groups.
Algebra.title: Categories of rings and algebras
Algebra.description: Categories of rings, commutative rings, Boolean rings, algebras, coalgebras, bialgebras and Hopf algebras over a commutative ring: limits, colimits, adjunctions and monoidal structures.
Algebra.title: Categories of modules
Algebra.description: Categories of modules and finitely generated modules over a ring: abelian and monoidal structure, change of rings, injective and projective objects, Ext over a ring, and topological modules. Presheaves and sheaves of modules have their own subfield.
Algebra.title: Presheaves and sheaves of modules
Algebra.description: Presheaves and sheaves of modules over presheaves and sheaves of rings on a site: limits and colimits, sheafification, pullback and pushforward, free, locally free and quasi-coherent sheaves of modules, and presheaves of differentials.

AlgebraicGeometry.title: Algebraic Geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Algebraic geometry studies spaces cut out by polynomial equations and translates between their geometric and algebraic invariants.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Schemes and morphisms
AlgebraicGeometry.description: The scheme-theoretic foundations of algebraic geometry: points, immersions, smooth morphisms, varieties over a field and properties that persist under base change.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Grothendieck topologies on schemes
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Sites attached to schemes: the Zariski, étale, pro-étale, fpqc and quasi-compact topologies, their points and sheaves, representability of sheaves by schemes, and ℓ-adic cohomology. Grothendieck topologies and sheaves on general sites are under category theory.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Varieties and projective geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Classical algebraic geometry of affine and projective varieties: hypersurfaces and their singularities, tangent spaces, plane configurations, intersection multiplicities, counts of solutions of sparse polynomial systems, tropical varieties, linear systems and birational maps.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Birational geometry and vanishing theorems
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Resolution of singularities and principalization of ideals in characteristic zero, vanishing theorems (Kodaira, Kawamata–Viehweg, Nadel), multiplier ideals, positivity of line bundles and divisors (nef and big classes, volumes), L² extension theorems, and the minimal model program. Rational maps of particular varieties, Cremona groups, linear systems on projective space and intersection multiplicities are under varieties and projective geometry, and complex manifolds as such under complex and symplectic geometry.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Algebraic curves
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Algebraic curves and their invariants, including divisors, the genus, Jacobians and the Abel–Jacobi map.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Elliptic curves
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Elliptic curves given by Weierstrass equations, their points over finite fields and number fields, torsion, reduction and Galois representations.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Abelian varieties and abelian schemes
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Abelian varieties over fields and abelian schemes over general bases: duals and polarizations, Zarhin's trick, Néron models and semistable reduction, complex multiplication, p-divisible groups and deformations (Serre–Tate, Grothendieck–Messing), and moduli of polarized abelian varieties, including toroidal and minimal compactifications in the principally polarized case, and degenerations through semi-abelian schemes. Jacobians of curves are under algebraic curves, and abelian varieties of dimension one under elliptic curves.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Arithmetic geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Rational points and point counts of varieties over number fields and finite fields, including the Mordell conjecture and the Weil conjectures.
AlgebraicGeometry.title: Arakelov geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Arithmetic varieties over the integers or over rings of integers, with hermitian vector bundles and Green currents on their complex points: arithmetic Chow groups and intersection theory, arithmetic Chern classes and degrees, the arithmetic Riemann–Roch and Hilbert–Samuel theorems, heights of cycles, and arithmetic volumes and positivity of hermitian line bundles, and Arakelov divisors of number fields. Heights of algebraic numbers and of points of projective space are under heights and Mahler measure.

Analysis.title: Analysis
Analysis.description: Analysis studies limits, approximation, continuity, and infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and operators.
Analysis.title: Real functions and calculus
Analysis.description: Functions of one or several real variables: differentiation, partial derivatives and multivariable calculus, the Riemann integral and evaluation of definite integrals, continuity and pathological functions, and functional equations on the reals.
Analysis.title: Differential calculus of one variable
Analysis.description: Derivatives of real functions of one real variable: mean-value and second-derivative tests, Taylor polynomials and remainders, Borel's lemma, interchange of limits and derivatives, monotone and C^n gluing results; not nowhere-differentiable constructions (see continuity subfield).
Analysis.title: Multivariable calculus
Analysis.description: Functions on R^n: partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, implicit functions, regular level sets and tangent spaces, curve length, Green's theorem, multivariable Taylor expansions and counterexamples about mixed partials or continuity at the origin.
Analysis.title: Riemann integration and definite integrals
Analysis.description: The Riemann integral via tagged partitions, iterated-integral formulas, moments, and closed-form evaluations of specific definite integrals (Serret's integral, integrals of 1/(1+u^n), areas between cosine powers, sinc squared); integrals defining a named special function go to Special functions.
Analysis.title: Continuity, regularity and functional equations
Analysis.description: Fine structure of real functions: Blumberg's theorem, continuous nowhere-differentiable functions (Weierstrass, Takagi), the rising sun lemma, approximate continuity, midpoint convexity, and the Cauchy, exponential and almost-additive functional equations including Hyers–Ulam stability.
Analysis.title: Differential calculus in normed spaces
Analysis.description: Differentiation on normed spaces, from Fréchet derivatives and tangent cones to smooth and analytic maps, inverse functions, vector fields and differential forms. Gradients, the implicit function theorem, symmetry of mixed partials and multivariable Taylor formulas remain under Real functions and calculus, including their normed-space formulations.
Analysis.title: Fréchet derivatives
Analysis.description: The Fréchet derivative and the derivative of functions of one variable over a normed field: rules for sums, products, compositions, inverses and linear and bilinear maps, strict differentiability, mean value inequalities, tangent cones and unique differentiability, and line (Gateaux) derivatives.
Analysis.title: Higher derivatives and smooth maps
Analysis.description: Iterated Fréchet and ordinary derivatives, finite-order Taylor jets, Cⁿ maps, bounds on higher derivatives, the Faà di Bruno formula, smooth bump functions and termwise differentiation. Convergent power series belong to Analytic maps and power series, and symmetry of mixed partials to Multivariable calculus.
Analysis.title: Analytic maps and power series
Analysis.description: Formal multilinear series and their radius of convergence, analytic maps between normed spaces, change of origin, composition and inversion of power series, continuously polynomial maps, the binomial series, and the principle of isolated zeros and uniqueness of analytic continuation.
Analysis.title: Inequalities
Analysis.description: Classical inequalities for sums, sequences, means and integrals of real or complex numbers: Hardy, Hilbert, Carleman, Wirtinger, Opial, Landau–Kolmogorov, Hermite–Hadamard, Kantorovich and Popoviciu, power-sum and elementary log/exp bounds; inequalities stated with Sobolev norms go to Function spaces, eigenvalue inequalities to Operator theory.
Analysis.title: Sequences, series and summability
Analysis.description: Convergence of numerical sequences and series and of series of functions, summability methods and Tauberian theorems, and closed-form evaluation of infinite series and products.
Analysis.title: Convergence of sequences and series
Analysis.description: Convergence tests (root test, rearrangement theorem, Stolz–Cesàro), normal and uniform convergence of series of functions, and specific limits of sequences and partial sums.
Analysis.title: Summability and Tauberian theorems
Analysis.description: Matrix summability methods (Silverman–Toeplitz, Cesàro means, permanent methods) and Tauberian theorems of Tauber, Hardy–Littlewood, Wiener and Newman.
Analysis.title: Series for π, ζ(3) and other constants
Analysis.description: Series and infinite products evaluating constants: π, Catalan's constant, Euler's constant, √2, ζ(3), reciprocal central binomial sums.
Analysis.title: Trigonometric and harmonic-number series
Analysis.description: Closed forms for series in powers of sin, cos or tan, central binomial series in trigonometric arguments, partial-fraction series of trigonometric functions, and identities with harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, as in Ramanujan's notebooks Chapter 9.
Analysis.title: Power series and series transformations
Analysis.description: Identities and transformations of power series and exponential-type series: Lagrange inversion and the tree function, Abel- and Jensen-type exponential series, coefficients of exp of a power series and Newton's identities for summable sequences, transformations of factorial series and Taylor-shift transformations, and Touchard / generalized Bell series.
Analysis.title: Asymptotic analysis
Analysis.description: Asymptotic expansions and methods: Euler–Maclaurin and Watson's lemma, Laplace-type integrals, coefficient asymptotics of power series (Bender's lemma), Stirling-type and inverse-factorial expansions, and asymptotic expansions of power sums, Lambert series and log sums; complex-analytic saddle-point results on entire functions go to Complex analysis.
Analysis.title: Special functions
Analysis.description: Named transcendental functions and their series, integral representations and identities: gamma and digamma, hypergeometric functions, exponential and logarithmic integrals, Lambert W, Bessel, Dickman, Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions, and elliptic functions (elliptic-function topics sit directly in the field).
Analysis.title: Gamma and digamma functions
Analysis.description: The gamma, digamma and trigamma functions: series and integral representations, factorial series, growth bounds against exponentials, and Ramanujan's digamma identities.
Analysis.title: Hypergeometric functions
Analysis.description: Generalized and basic hypergeometric series and their summation theorems (Gauss, Dougall, Dixon, Klamkin, Frisch). Orthogonal polynomial families go to Algebra/orthogonal-polynomials.
Analysis.title: Exponential, logarithmic and related functions
Analysis.description: Exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric-type functions and their relatives: exponential integral E1 and Ein, logarithmic integral, Lambert W, logistic function, x^y = y^x, exponential sums, Mittag-Leffler expansion of 1/(e^u − 1), modified Bessel functions, Dickman–de Bruijn function, Bell-polynomial functions.
Analysis.title: Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions
Analysis.description: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials and their generating-function identities, Berndt's φ_r and power-difference series, Clausen functions, the inverse tangent integral and dilogarithm identities; results whose content is values of ζ, Dirichlet L or β functions belong to NumberTheory.
Analysis.title: Complex analysis
Analysis.description: Holomorphic and meromorphic functions of one and several complex variables: Cauchy theory, entire functions, conformal and univalent maps, zeros of polynomials, and Hilbert and Banach spaces of analytic functions.
Analysis.title: Complex integration, residues and singularities
Analysis.description: Contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem, residues, argument principle, Rouché, Laurent series, isolated singularities (Casorati–Weierstrass, great Picard), Schwarz reflection, Looman–Menchoff, normal families and local properties of holomorphic functions on discs and annuli.
Analysis.title: Entire and meromorphic functions
Analysis.description: Growth and value distribution of entire and meromorphic functions: Wiman–Valiron theory and maximum term, Hayman admissibility, Weierstrass factorization, Mittag-Leffler, Liouville-type rigidity, preimages and zeros/ones on lines.
Analysis.title: Geometric function theory
Analysis.description: Conformal and univalent maps: Riemann mapping, Koebe and Bloch theorems, Schwarz–Pick and half-plane self-maps, starlike and univalent coefficient problems, Loewner equation, holomorphic motions.
Analysis.title: Polynomials in the complex plane
Analysis.description: Analytic behaviour of complex polynomials: location of zeros (Eneström–Kakeya, Sendov's problem, Jentzsch), flat and Littlewood polynomials, complementary polynomials and sup norms on the unit circle. Algebraic properties of polynomials go to Algebra; Mahler measure goes to NumberTheory.
Analysis.title: Several complex variables
Analysis.description: Holomorphic functions on C^n: Hartogs extension and separate analyticity, Weierstrass preparation, complex Hessians.
Analysis.title: Spaces of analytic functions
Analysis.description: Hardy, Bergman, Dirichlet and Fock spaces and their reproducing kernels, H^∞, boundary behaviour (Fatou, F. and M. Riesz), cyclicity and polynomial density.
Analysis.title: Potential theory
Analysis.description: Harmonic and subharmonic functions in the plane and in R^n, the maximum principle, harmonic conjugates, the Newton and logarithmic potentials and fundamental solutions of the Laplacian.
Analysis.title: Harmonic analysis
Analysis.description: Fourier series, the Fourier transform on R^n, Fourier analysis on finite groups and the Boolean cube, wavelets and multiscale analysis, real-variable methods (maximal functions, the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, BMO), singular integrals, and other integral transforms and moment problems.
Analysis.title: Fourier series
Analysis.description: Fourier series on the circle and torus: Fejér and Dirichlet kernels, pointwise and Cesàro convergence, Riemann–Lebesgue, uniqueness, absolutely convergent series and Wiener's theorems, periodic convolution, Fourier optimization on the torus.
Analysis.title: Fourier transform and uncertainty principles
Analysis.description: The Fourier transform on R^n and Schwartz functions: convolution, Bochner, Hausdorff–Young, Heisenberg and fractal uncertainty, band-limited functions and Bernstein inequalities, sampling and Fourier interpolation, Kakeya sets, Beurling–Ahlfors and other singular integrals.
Analysis.title: Discrete Fourier analysis
Analysis.description: Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups and the Boolean cube: DFT and FFT, Plancherel, finite uncertainty, Young and Hausdorff–Young, Riesz–Thorin on finite sets, influences and noise operators.
Analysis.title: Wavelets and multiscale analysis
Analysis.description: Wavelet orthonormal bases and multiresolution approximations, the Haar system, conjugate mirror filters and fast two-channel filter banks, and wavelet scattering transforms built from cascades of wavelet modulus operators. Frames and Riesz bases of general Hilbert spaces are under Hilbert spaces; sparse approximation in bases and dictionaries is under Approximation theory.
Analysis.title: Integral transforms and moment problems
Analysis.description: Laplace, Mellin and Radon transforms (Ramanujan's master theorem, Fourier slice theorem) and Hausdorff moment problems.
Analysis.title: Real-variable methods
Analysis.description: Dyadic intervals and stopping times, the dyadic and Hardy–Littlewood maximal functions, the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, Lebesgue differentiation along dyadic intervals, vector-valued maximal inequalities, bounded mean oscillation, the John–Nirenberg inequality and H¹–BMO duality.
Analysis.title: Normed groups, rings and fields
Analysis.description: Norms and seminorms on groups, rings and fields, including ultrametric norms, normed homomorphisms, completions and quotients. Abstract infinite sums belong to Topology, analytic convergence tests to Sequences, series and summability, and equivalence of absolute values and spectral norms on field extensions to p-adic numbers.
Analysis.title: Banach space theory
Analysis.description: Normed, Banach and topological vector spaces: duality, weak topologies, geometry of the unit ball, bases and classical sequence spaces.
Analysis.title: Normed spaces
Analysis.description: Seminormed and normed vector spaces, balls and spheres, finite-dimensional norm equivalence, completions, complemented subspaces, linear isometries, normed affine spaces and operator norms of multilinear and alternating maps. Geometric isometry theorems such as the Mazur–Ulam theorem belong to Geometry of Banach spaces.
Analysis.title: Duality, weak topologies and reflexivity
Analysis.description: Hahn–Banach, annihilators and bipolars, weak and weak-star convergence and topologies, Goldstine, James, Eberlein–Šmulian, Krein–Šmulian, Banach–Alaoglu, Mazur's lemma, Banach limits, Hamel bases and discontinuous functionals, F-spaces and locally convex spaces, Choquet theory.
Analysis.title: Geometry of Banach spaces
Analysis.description: Convexity and smoothness of norms (uniform convexity, Kadec–Klee, Birkhoff–James), extreme points of balls, Auerbach and Schauder bases, approximation property, isometries (Banach–Stone, Mazur–Ulam), Banach–Mazur, Dvoretzky–Rogers, Grothendieck, Rademacher type, Daugavet, Bishop–Phelps.
Analysis.title: Classical sequence spaces
Analysis.description: ℓ^p and c₀: duality, Schauder bases, compactness criteria, Schur and Rosenthal ℓ¹ theorems, Pitt's theorem, quotients of ℓ¹, finite ℓ^p geometry, convolution on ℓ^p(ℤ).
Analysis.title: Hilbert spaces
Analysis.description: Geometry of inner product spaces: nearest-point projections, orthonormal and Hilbert bases, separability and ℓ², frames and Riesz bases, weak convergence (Opial, Radon–Riesz), Kirszbraun extension, derivatives of the norm, representer theorems; operators on Hilbert spaces go to Operator theory, analytic RKHS to Complex analysis.
Analysis.title: Operator theory
Analysis.description: Bounded linear operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces: spectra, compact and Fredholm operators, shifts and other concrete operators, and eigenvalue inequalities.
Analysis.title: Spectral theory
Analysis.description: Spectra and spectral theorems: self-adjoint, normal and compact self-adjoint spectral theorems, approximate and essential spectrum, numerical range and radius, Cayley transform, spectra of finite-rank and rank-one operators, almost Mathieu operator.
Analysis.title: Compact and Fredholm operators
Analysis.description: Compact and finite-rank operators, Schauder's theorem, complete continuity, Hilbert–Schmidt operators, Riesz–Schauder theory, Fredholm alternative and index, closed-range theorems.
Analysis.title: Bounded operators and operator topologies
Analysis.description: General bounded operators: Douglas lemma, direct sums, strong and weak operator convergence, uniform boundedness, Hellinger–Toeplitz, invariant subspaces (Lomonosov), hypercyclicity criteria, Wold decomposition.
Analysis.title: Shift, Toeplitz and Hankel operators
