Analysis.description: Unilateral, bilateral and weighted shifts and their spectra, indices and numerical ranges, Rolewicz backward shifts, Toeplitz, Hankel and composition operators on ℓ².
Analysis.title: Integral, multiplication and diagonal operators
Analysis.description: Volterra and kernel integral operators, Cesàro and Hilbert operators, multiplication operators on C(X) and L², diagonal operators, Schur tests, L^p bounds for integral operators.
Analysis.title: Eigenvalue inequalities and perturbation
Analysis.description: Courant–Fischer, Weyl, Ky Fan, Cauchy interlacing, Schur–Horn, Eckart–Young, Bauer–Fike, Peierls–Klein for self-adjoint operators; statements only about finite matrices move to LinearAlgebra.
Analysis.title: Banach and operator algebras
Analysis.description: Banach algebras and C*- and von Neumann algebras: exponentials and product formulas in Banach algebras, GNS, Gelfand–Naimark, bicommutant, Kaplansky density, Russo–Dye, Stinespring, Kadison–Singer and the Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava theorem.
Analysis.title: Function spaces and Sobolev inequalities
Analysis.description: L^p and Sobolev spaces of functions: embeddings (Morrey, Rellich, radial, trace), Ehrling, Agmon, Ladyzhenskaya, Gagliardo–Nirenberg and weighted Hardy–Sobolev inequalities, sup-norm bounds by H¹ energy, L^p limits and weak convergence in L^p.
Analysis.title: Distributions
Analysis.description: Test functions, Schwartz functions, tempered distributions and distributional derivatives: principal values, Plemelj limits, Dirac comb, partitions of unity.
Analysis.title: Ordinary differential equations
Analysis.description: Existence and uniqueness (Cauchy–Peano, Picard, maximal solutions), linear systems and fundamental matrices, stability and Lyapunov's indirect method, Sturm–Liouville and boundary value problems with their Green's operators and eigenfunctions, oscillation and comparison theorems.
Analysis.title: Control theory
Analysis.description: Mathematical control theory of finite-dimensional systems: controllability of linear systems (controllability Gramian, Kalman rank condition, Hautus test), pole placement and stabilisation by state feedback, Lie-bracket conditions for nonlinear controllability, Brockett's obstruction to continuous feedback stabilisation and the return method; system identification by recursive least squares and the capability and limits of feedback for uncertain discrete-time systems. Optimal control and dynamic programming are under Convex analysis and calculus of variations and Computer science.
Analysis.title: Rough paths and path signatures
Analysis.description: Signatures of paths and controlled differential equations: iterated integrals of a path, Chen's identity, signatures of piecewise-linear paths, the shuffle identity, time reversal and reparametrisation, the Lévy area, signature series of linear controlled equations, uniqueness of the signature up to tree-like equivalence, universal approximation by linear functionals of the signature, and multiplicative functionals of finite p-variation with Lyons's extension theorem. Brownian motion and stochastic integrals are under Probability.
Analysis.title: Partial differential equations
Analysis.description: PDE existence, regularity and qualitative results: Cauchy–Kovalevskaya, heat and Airy equations, weak solutions and elliptic regularity, Euler singularity formation, σ₂ Hessian estimates, radial symmetry, viscosity solutions, reaction–diffusion systems and Turing instability, Dirichlet and Neumann spectra of the Laplacian.
Analysis.title: Convex analysis and calculus of variations
Analysis.description: Convex functions and sets in analysis and optimization: Fenchel conjugates, polar sets, Moreau decomposition, convex projections, KKT conditions, gradient descent rates, Stampacchia, Tikhonov regularization, Euler–Lagrange, mountain pass and Ekeland principles; linear programming goes to convex geometry. Ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization of a finite-dimensional least-squares problem, is under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md) in Machine learning.
Analysis.title: Fixed-point theory
Analysis.description: Fixed points of nonexpansive, Lipschitz and affine maps: the Browder–Göhde–Kirk theorem and Kirk's normal structure, Markov–Kakutani, Browder's demiclosedness principle, maps with contracting iterates.
Analysis.title: Numerical analysis
Analysis.description: Algorithms with error analysis: bisection and Newton's method, Euler and Runge–Kutta methods, Galerkin and finite element estimates (Céa, Aubin–Nitsche, Strang, Banach–Nečas–Babuška), and methods for smooth unconstrained optimization (line searches and the Zoutendijk condition, nonlinear conjugate gradient, trust-region, quasi-Newton and Barzilai–Borwein methods).
Analysis.title: Approximation theory
Analysis.description: Approximation and interpolation of functions: Chebyshev equioscillation, best approximation, the minimax property of Chebyshev polynomials, Chebyshev series and interpolation, Lagrange interpolation, Bernstein polynomials and Voronovskaya, Korovkin, Müntz–Szász, Runge, Kolmogorov superposition, universal approximation, and sparse approximation: best M-term approximation in an orthonormal basis and greedy pursuits (matching pursuit and orthogonal matching pursuit).

Biology.title: Mathematical Biology
Biology.description: Mathematical biology models populations, genomes, and biochemical networks, from coalescents and reaction dynamics to the algorithms that read biological sequences.
Biology.title: Population genetics
Biology.description: Mathematical models of allele frequencies in populations under random mating, selection, mutation, migration and genetic drift, including the Wright–Fisher and Moran models and their diffusion limits.
Biology.title: Diffusion theory
Biology.description: The Wright–Fisher diffusion as the continuum limit of allele-frequency dynamics: generator and semigroup, fixation probabilities, absorption and sojourn times, mutation and stationary laws, allele age and the Poisson random field.
Biology.title: Selection, migration and transmission
Biology.description: Allele-frequency dynamics under viability selection and biased transmission, migration-selection balance, interference between linked selected loci and modifiers of transmission. Deterministic recurrences and finite-population stochastic interference remain distinct models.
Biology.title: Coalescent theory
Biology.description: Backward-in-time models of the genealogy of a sample of genes, from Kingman's coalescent and its generalizations to the site frequency spectrum, recombination and population structure.
Biology.title: Cannings models and multiple-merger coalescents
Biology.description: Exchangeable Cannings models of reproduction and the limits of their genealogies: convergence to Kingman's coalescent under the Möhle–Sagitov conditions, Λ-coalescent limits for heavy-tailed offspring, merger rates and the Beta-coalescents, coming down from infinity, and the site frequency spectrum under multiple mergers.
Biology.title: Detecting natural selection
Biology.description: Statistical tests of neutrality and genome scans for selection based on polymorphism, divergence and haplotype structure, and models of the distribution of fitness effects.
Biology.title: Population structure and admixture
Biology.description: f-statistics, admixture graphs, ancestry models and linkage-disequilibrium methods for inferring the relationships and mixture histories of populations.
Biology.title: Conservation genetics
Biology.description: Models coupling the genetics and demography of small or fragmented populations: kinship-minimizing management, genetic diversity summaries, effective-size requirements, genetic rescue and the separate risks of extinction and genetic loss.
Biology.title: Phylogenetics
Biology.description: Reconstruction of evolutionary trees from sequence data: substitution models, likelihood and parsimony, distance methods, tree metrics, splits and the enumeration of phylogenetic trees.
Biology.title: Phylogenetic inference and comparison
Biology.description: Statistical guarantees and identifiability for evolutionary trees, networks and recorded cell lineages, together with agreement-subtree models for comparing trees. Each article retains its own observation, sampling and evolutionary model.
Biology.title: Molecular evolution
Biology.description: Models of genome evolution at the molecular level: mutational bias in the introduction of variation, the mutational-hazard view of genome complexity and constructive neutral evolution.
Biology.title: Quantitative genetics
Biology.description: The genetics of continuously varying traits: decomposition of genetic variance, resemblance between relatives, kinship, mixed models and the response to selection.
Biology.title: Statistical genetics
Biology.description: Statistical methods for genome-wide association studies, heritability estimation from summary statistics, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization and gene constraint scores.
Biology.title: Association tests
Biology.description: Tests used in genetic association studies, and their calibration: tests of association between genotypes and a trait (the Cochran–Armitage trend test of genotype counts, the SKAT variance-component test with relatedness, genomic control) and the exact and asymptotic tests of Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium of genotype counts that accompany them. Fisher's exact test, the burden test and SKAT-O, multiple testing across genes, and genomic control with an estimated inflation factor are under Hypothesis testing in Probability.
Biology.title: Cancer genomics
Biology.description: Mathematical models for tumour sequencing data: purity and copy number, cancer cell fractions, mutation detection power, mutational signatures and the timing of genomic events.
Biology.title: Bioinformatics
Biology.description: Algorithms and statistical models on biological sequences and data: sequence alignment, genome assembly, motifs, RNA secondary structure, clustering and network reconstruction.
Biology.title: Sequence alignment
Biology.description: Pairwise and multiple alignment of biological sequences: Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman, affine gaps, banded, linear-space, semi-global and wavefront algorithms.
Biology.title: Systems biology
Biology.description: Dynamics of biochemical reaction networks and gene regulatory circuits: mass-action kinetics, enzyme kinetics, ultrasensitivity, feedback, metabolic flux analysis and gene expression noise.
Biology.title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics
Biology.description: Compartment models of drug absorption, distribution and elimination, linear and saturable, under bolus, infusion and repeated dosing; dose–response laws, reference models for drug combinations and models of concentration measurements. Enzyme kinetics as such is under Systems biology.
Biology.title: Population and evolutionary dynamics
Biology.description: Differential-equation and matrix models of population growth, structure, species interaction and evolutionary change, such as logistic growth, predator–prey systems, metapopulations, replicator dynamics, quasispecies and Leslie matrices, and the life tables and direct standardization of demography.
Biology.title: Reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
Biology.description: Reaction–diffusion models of biological spread and spatial patterning, including travelling waves, morphogen gradients and Turing instabilities.
Biology.title: Mathematical neuroscience
Biology.description: Models of excitable membranes and neurons: the Nernst potential and passive cable theory, the Hodgkin–Huxley and FitzHugh–Nagumo equations, integrate-and-fire neurons and Wilson–Cowan models of neural populations.
Biology.title: Mathematical epidemiology
Biology.description: Compartmental, renewal and branching-process models of infectious disease transmission and their reproduction numbers, the reporting of incidence, and the accuracy of diagnostic tests.

CategoryTheory.title: Category Theory
CategoryTheory.description: Category theory organizes mathematical structures through morphisms, functors, universal properties, limits, and adjunctions.
CategoryTheory.title: Categories, functors and natural transformations
CategoryTheory.description: The basic language of category theory: categories, functors, natural transformations and isomorphisms, monomorphisms and epimorphisms, equivalences, full and faithful functors, opposite and functor categories, the Yoneda lemma and representable functors, skeleta and size conditions.
CategoryTheory.title: Constructions of categories
CategoryTheory.description: Categories built from other categories: products, sums and joins, comma, arrow, slice and structured-arrow categories, categories of elements and the Grothendieck construction, full and wide subcategories, quotient and path categories, idempotent completion, graded objects and diagrams of composable arrows.
CategoryTheory.title: Special categories and examples
CategoryTheory.description: Particular categories and kinds of categories: the categories of types, of categories and of quivers, groupoids, preorders, discrete, thin, finite and single-object categories, concrete categories with their forgetful functors, and categories of objects with a monoid action. Categories of algebraic or topological objects are with the corresponding algebra and topology fields.
CategoryTheory.title: Classes of morphisms and objects
CategoryTheory.description: Properties of morphisms and of objects and their stability under composition, base change and limits: special epimorphisms, subobjects and subfunctors, generators and separators, lifting properties, weak factorization systems and the small object argument, and closure of classes of objects under limits, colimits and extensions.
CategoryTheory.title: Limits and colimits
CategoryTheory.description: Universal cones and cocones over diagrams: their existence, preservation, reflection and creation by functors, particular shapes such as products, pullbacks, equalizers, kernels and ends, filtered colimits and final functors, and ind-objects.
CategoryTheory.title: Limits of diagrams
CategoryTheory.description: Universal properties, existence results and constructions of limits and colimits, including pointwise limits of functors, limits in slice categories and iterated limits.
CategoryTheory.title: Shapes of limits and colimits
CategoryTheory.description: Initial and terminal objects, products, pullbacks, equalizers, kernels, images, ends and their duals. Biproducts are with additive categories.
CategoryTheory.title: Filtered diagrams and ind-objects
CategoryTheory.description: Filtered and cofiltered diagrams, sifted categories, final functors, transfinite diagrams and ind-completions. Cardinal bounds on filteredness are treated in accessible categories.
CategoryTheory.title: Preservation and creation of limits
CategoryTheory.description: Continuity and exactness properties of functors, including preservation, reflection and creation of limits and colimits of particular shapes.
CategoryTheory.title: Adjunctions and Kan extensions
CategoryTheory.description: Adjoint functors, units and counits, mates, reflective subcategories and adjoint functor theorems, adjoint triples, Kan extensions along functors, dense functors, exact squares and profunctors; monads are in their own field.
CategoryTheory.title: Monads and algebras
CategoryTheory.description: Monads and comonads, their Eilenberg–Moore and Kleisli categories, monadicity and comonadicity theorems, and algebras and coalgebras of endofunctors.
CategoryTheory.title: Localization of categories
CategoryTheory.description: Formally inverting a class of morphisms: localization functors and their universal property, the calculus of fractions, morphisms of localizers, Bousfield localization, and the localization of functors in several variables and of additive and monoidal structures; derived categories are in homological algebra.
CategoryTheory.title: Accessible and locally presentable categories
CategoryTheory.description: Categories generated under highly filtered colimits by a set of small objects: κ-filtered categories, presentable objects and accessible functors, locally presentable and accessible categories, and the orthogonal-reflection construction.
CategoryTheory.title: Regular, extensive and adhesive categories
CategoryTheory.description: Exactness properties of categories with finite limits and colimits: effective epimorphisms and regular categories, internal equivalence relations, extensive and distributive categories, universal and van Kampen colimits, and adhesive categories; abelian categories are in their own field.
CategoryTheory.title: Monoidal categories
CategoryTheory.description: Monoidal categories equip a category with a tensor product and unit object, with braided and symmetric variants governing how tensor factors may be exchanged.
CategoryTheory.title: Enriched categories
CategoryTheory.description: Categories whose hom-objects lie in a monoidal category: enriched categories and functors, enriched functor categories, ordinary categories with an enrichment, conical limits and the bicategory of enriched categories.
CategoryTheory.title: Bicategories and higher categories
CategoryTheory.description: Bicategories and 2-categories: lax, oplax and pseudofunctors, their transformations and modifications, coherence, adjunctions, mates and Kan extensions inside a bicategory, spans and the bicategorical Yoneda embedding. Quasi-categories and other simplicial models are in algebraic topology.
CategoryTheory.title: Fibered categories and descent
CategoryTheory.description: Functors viewed as families of categories: cartesian and cocartesian morphisms, fibered and cofibered categories, the Grothendieck construction for pseudofunctors, descent data, prestacks and stacks, and descent of properties of morphisms.
CategoryTheory.title: Sites and sheaves
CategoryTheory.description: Grothendieck topologies, sieves, coverages and pretopologies, sheaves on sites with values in a category, sheafification, continuous and cocontinuous functors, dense subsites, the coherent and canonical topologies, hypercovers, points of sites and sheaf cohomology.
CategoryTheory.title: Topos theory
CategoryTheory.description: Topos theory studies elementary and Grothendieck toposes, categories with finite limits, exponentials and a subobject classifier that behave like universes of sets.
CategoryTheory.title: Galois categories
CategoryTheory.description: Grothendieck's axiomatic Galois theory: Galois categories and fiber functors, Galois objects, pro-representability of fiber functors, and the fundamental group of a Galois category with its action on fibers.
CategoryTheory.title: Additive and abelian categories
CategoryTheory.description: Categories enriched in abelian groups and modules: preadditive, additive and linear categories, biproducts and additive functors, abelian categories and their embedding theorems, Grothendieck abelian categories and the AB axioms, and Serre classes; complexes, resolutions and derived functors are in homological algebra.
CategoryTheory.title: Triangulated categories
CategoryTheory.description: Categories with a shift functor and distinguished triangles: shifts and functors commuting with them, pretriangulated and triangulated categories, triangulated functors and subcategories, Verdier localization, homological functors and t-structures with their hearts; derived categories of abelian categories are in homological algebra.
CategoryTheory.title: Homological algebra
CategoryTheory.description: Homological algebra studies abelian categories through projective resolutions and the derived functors they define, such as Tor, together with their additivity.
CategoryTheory.title: Complexes and homology
CategoryTheory.description: Chain and cochain complexes indexed by complex shapes, short complexes, homology and exactness, diagram lemmas such as the snake and five lemmas, long exact homology sequences, quasi-isomorphisms, bicomplexes, total complexes and truncations; abelian categories as such are in the additive and abelian categories field.
CategoryTheory.title: Homotopy and derived categories
CategoryTheory.description: Chain homotopies, mapping cones and cylinders, the homotopy category of complexes and its triangulated structure, and derived categories obtained by inverting quasi-isomorphisms; triangulated categories in general are in the triangulated categories field.
CategoryTheory.title: Resolutions and derived functors
CategoryTheory.description: Projective and injective objects, resolutions and dimensions, left and right derived functors of additive functors, Ext and Tor, and derived functors between localized categories via derivability structures.
CategoryTheory.title: Spectral sequences
CategoryTheory.description: Spectral objects and spectral sequences, their pages and convergence, and the spectral sequences of filtered and double complexes.
CategoryTheory.title: Condensed mathematics
CategoryTheory.description: Sheaves on profinite sets and compact Hausdorff spaces for the coherent topology: condensed and light condensed sets and modules, discrete condensed objects, solid modules, and the comparison with topological spaces.

Combinatorics.title: Combinatorics
Combinatorics.description: Combinatorics studies finite and discrete configurations through counting, extremal structure, and constructive arguments.
Combinatorics.title: Binomial coefficients and identities
Combinatorics.description: Binomial, multinomial and generalized binomial coefficients and closed-form evaluation of finite sums built from them (alternating, reciprocal, harmonic-weighted, hypergeometric), including Apéry-like sequences such as Franel, Domb and Zagier numbers; q-binomials go to symmetric functions and q-analogues, Catalan-type numbers to Catalan numbers, Stirling-weighted sums to Stirling numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Binomial sums and hypergeometric identities
Combinatorics.description: Evaluations and bounds of sums of products of binomial coefficients: Chu–Vandermonde, Dixon, Knuth's old sum, Staver, Frisch, Klamkin, hockey-stick and Filipponi identities, partial-sum bounds, multisection identities, and Franel, Domb, Zagier and Catalan–Larcombe–French numbers defined by binomial sums.
Combinatorics.title: Central binomial coefficients and harmonic sums
Combinatorics.description: Finite sums and power series involving central binomial coefficients or their reciprocals, often weighted by harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, including arcsin-type series and Kollár's incomplete binomial sums.
Combinatorics.title: Generalized binomial coefficients and Pascal-like triangles
Combinatorics.description: Variants of the binomial coefficient and of Pascal's triangle: b-ary and digital (carry-free) binomial coefficients, Ward and totienomial coefficients from generalized factorials, trinomial and quadrinomial coefficients, rascal, hyperbolic Pascal and 2-Pascal triangles and their diagonals; the Pascal matrix viewed as a Riordan array goes to Riordan arrays.
Combinatorics.title: Catalan numbers and lattice paths
Combinatorics.description: The Catalan family of counting sequences and the lattice paths they count: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Narayana, Motzkin, Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Dyck and Motzkin paths and their statistics, Delannoy numbers and walks with prescribed steps, including arithmetic properties (parity, integrality, perfect powers) of these numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Catalan numbers and their generalizations
Combinatorics.description: Catalan numbers and generalizations defined by formulas or recurrences: Fuss–Catalan, super Catalan, (p,q)-Patalan, Whitt and Sabar arrays, generalized Catalan–Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Narayana numbers and polynomials, Touchard's identity, Raney's cycle lemma, and divisibility or growth of these numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Motzkin numbers and Motzkin paths
Combinatorics.description: Motzkin numbers and paths: colored, weighted and (u,l,d) Motzkin paths, humps and peaks, the Motzkin triangle, links with central trinomial coefficients, alternating Motzkin sums, Aigner's inequality, and Motzkin-related sequences such as A005773; weighted Motzkin paths used to compute Hankel determinants go to Hankel determinants and continued fractions.
Combinatorics.title: Dyck paths and lattice walks
Combinatorics.description: Statistics on Dyck paths (peaks, valleys, marked steps, subwords) and their variants (skew, rational, k-box Dyck paths), lattice walks with unit or diagonal steps, Delannoy numbers, Sulanke arrays, colored Dyck paths, and nonintersecting paths via the Lindström–Gessel–Viennot lemma.
Combinatorics.title: Stirling, Bell and Eulerian numbers
Combinatorics.description: The number triangles and sequences that count set partitions, permutations by cycles, descents and excedances, and their relatives: Stirling and Lah numbers and their generalizations, Bell and Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials, Eulerian numbers and polynomials, and Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers studied combinatorially.
Combinatorics.title: Stirling and Lah numbers
Combinatorics.description: Classical Stirling numbers of the first and second kind and Lah numbers: recurrences, explicit and addition formulas, rising and falling factorial expansions, orthogonality and inverse Stirling matrices, cycle counts, inequalities and identities such as Lee's and Gy's.
Combinatorics.title: Generalized Stirling numbers
Combinatorics.description: Deformations and generalizations of Stirling numbers: r-Stirling, associated Stirling, Hsu–Shiue, Jacobi–Stirling, Legendre–Stirling, meromorphic and degenerate Stirling numbers, α-Stirling and generalized Stirling matrices, and (q,r)-Whitney and Dowling numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Bell numbers, Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials
Combinatorics.description: Bell numbers (Dobinski, Spivey, Touchard and Turán-type identities, log-convexity), complete, partial and generalized Bell polynomials, potential polynomials, Fubini (ordered Bell) numbers and their congruences, and horse numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Eulerian numbers and polynomials
Combinatorics.description: Counting permutations by descents or excedances: Eulerian numbers and polynomials, refined, multiset and generalized Eulerian polynomials, associated Stirling–Eulerian numbers, Worpitzky's identity, gamma-positivity and Hankel determinants of Eulerian polynomials, Bell permutations by weak excedances.
Combinatorics.title: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers
Combinatorics.description: Combinatorial formulas for Bernoulli, Euler, tangent and Genocchi numbers (Garabedian's formulas, median Euler and Genocchi numbers, Euler–Seidel matrices, Carlitz q-Bernoulli polynomials), their divisibility, and sums of powers via Faulhaber coefficients.
Combinatorics.title: Riordan arrays and sequence transforms
Combinatorics.description: Infinite lower-triangular arrays and operators on sequences studied through generating functions: the Riordan group, number triangles and their diagonals, binomial, INVERT and Catalan transforms, Hankel and Toeplitz determinants and continued fractions; a specific named family (Motzkin triangle, Stirling matrices) stays with that family.
Combinatorics.title: Riordan arrays and number triangles
Combinatorics.description: Riordan arrays and their A- and Z-sequences, inverses, triple factorizations, pseudo-involutions and total positivity, the Pascal and Pell matrices as Riordan arrays, Barry's triangles, triangular recurrence arrays extended to negative rows, and diagonal or row sums of triangles.
Combinatorics.title: Hankel determinants and continued fractions
Combinatorics.description: Hankel transforms of sequences and their invariance under binomial transforms, Heilermann's formula linking Jacobi continued fractions to weighted Motzkin paths, Catalan-sum Hankel determinants, and Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinants.
Combinatorics.title: Sequence transforms and generating functions
Combinatorics.description: Operators on integer sequences and coefficient extraction: binomial, multiple and falling k-binomial transforms, INVERT and Catalan transforms, hypersequences, convolutions, C-finite sequences, and recovering terms from generating-function values.
Combinatorics.title: Integer partitions
Combinatorics.description: Partitions of integers as combinatorial objects: identities equating partition counts and their bijective proofs, Young diagrams and partition statistics, and counting partitions; congruences for partition functions and theta- or eta-quotient identities go to NumberTheory.
Combinatorics.title: Partition identities
Combinatorics.description: Theorems equating counts of two classes of partitions: Euler, MacMahon, Andrews, Andrews–Lewis, Rogers–Ramanujan, Stanley and Elder theorems, polarized and 2-distant partitions, colored Euler-type identities and Merca's sums of different parts.
Combinatorics.title: Young diagrams and partition statistics
Combinatorics.description: Statistics and structure of a single partition: conjugation, hook lengths, s-cores, perimeter, diagonal sequences, lit cells, rank and crank, max-rook numbers, perfect and double-perfect partitions, and reconstruction of a partition from pairwise products.
Combinatorics.title: Counting partitions
Combinatorics.description: The partition function and its relatives as counts: bounds and asymptotics for p(n), the pentagonal number theorem, partition polynomials, Landau's function, overpartitions and regular partitions counted (not their congruences), restricted Gaussian and bounded partitions.
Combinatorics.title: Integer compositions
Combinatorics.description: Ordered sums of positive integers: compositions with restricted, palindromic, colored or n-color parts, Arndt compositions, perfect compositions, shade, symmetric peaks and valleys, and convolution identities for weighted compositions.
Combinatorics.title: Permutations
Combinatorics.description: Permutations of a finite set as combinatorial objects: pattern containment and avoidance, and statistics and cycle structure; descent-counting numbers go to Eulerian numbers, Stirling cycle numbers to Stirling numbers.
Combinatorics.title: Permutation patterns
Combinatorics.description: Classical, consecutive, mesh and signed patterns in permutations and in inversion and ascent sequences, pattern-avoidance counts, pattern-replacement classes, stack sorting, and king and separable permutations.
Combinatorics.title: Permutation statistics and cycle structure
Combinatorics.description: Descents, peaks, major index, left-to-right maxima, fixed points and derangements, cycle counts and the smallest cycle of a random permutation, products of cyclic permutations, Stirling and flattened Stirling permutations, Josephus permutations and permutation-guessing puzzles.
Combinatorics.title: Set partitions
Combinatorics.description: Partitions of a finite set into blocks: finite partition API, ordered and cyclic set partitions, restricted-growth words, peaks and rises, noncrossing partitions, merging-free and marriageable-singles partitions, genus of a partition, and linear chord diagrams and hypermonopoles.
Combinatorics.title: Parking functions
Combinatorics.description: Parking functions and their variants (partial, weakly increasing, k-Naples, metered) and statistics on them: lucky cars, descents, displacement, and lucky statistics of Stirling permutations read as parking preferences.
Combinatorics.title: Tilings, dimers and board placements
Combinatorics.description: Covering and placement problems on lattices and boards: domino and lozenge tilings and perfect matchings of grid regions (Aztec diamonds, Möbius grids, cylinders and tori), polyominoes and polycubes, tilings of groups by translates and the periodic tiling conjecture, nonattacking chess pieces, rook and file placements on Ferrers boards, and self-avoiding walks on lattices.
Combinatorics.title: Symmetric functions, tableaux and q-analogues
Combinatorics.description: Algebraic combinatorics of symmetric functions and Young tableaux, Gaussian binomial coefficients and other q-analogues, alternating sign matrices and plane partitions (q-TSPP, Robbins numbers), Coxeter–Catalan positivity, chromatic symmetric functions, minuscule polynomials, and positivity or real-rootedness of permanents and gamma vectors.
Combinatorics.title: Combinatorics on words
Combinatorics.description: Finite and infinite words over finite alphabets: repetitions and avoidability, morphic and Sturmian words, factor complexity, automatic and regular sequences, Lyndon and primitive words, and integer sequences defined by self-description or self-generation.
Combinatorics.title: Repetitions in words
Combinatorics.description: Squares, overlaps, cubes and fractional powers in words: square-free and overlap-free words, abelian and k-abelian repetitions, power-free morphisms, Crochemore's test and Dejean's repetition threshold.
Combinatorics.title: Morphic and Sturmian words
Combinatorics.description: Infinite words generated by substitutions and their codings: Fibonacci, Tribonacci and Thue–Morse words and generalizations, pure morphic and morphic words, Sturmian and balanced words, factor complexity and Pansiot's classification, palindromic and relative-position properties, first differences of binary words.
Combinatorics.title: Automatic sequences and numeration systems
Combinatorics.description: k-automatic and k-regular sequences, Cobham's theorem and kernels, meta-automatic sequences, results proved with the Walnut prover, and numeration systems (Dumont–Thomas, Tribonacci and Zeckendorf representations) whose digit words define such sequences.
Combinatorics.title: Finite words
Combinatorics.description: Properties of finite words: Lyndon and primitive words, equilibrious words, Ulam words, keyword substitutions, universal cycles for subsets, capacity of Catalan words, rectangles in nondecreasing words, and intersections in pairs of words.
Combinatorics.title: Self-describing and self-generating sequences
Combinatorics.description: Integer sequences defined by self-reference, greedy or mex rules: Kolakoski, Gijswijt (curling numbers), Cloitre, Connell, Aronson, Smarandache, van der Laan, throwback and anti-recurrence sequences, self-generating sets, fractal sequences and inventory loops.
Combinatorics.title: Additive combinatorics
Combinatorics.description: The additive structure of sets in integers and abelian groups: sumsets and inverse theorems, sum-product growth, Sidon sets and difference sets, sum-free sets, additive bases, zero-sum problems, and arithmetic progressions in dense sets; colouring (Ramsey-type) versions go to Ramsey theory.
Combinatorics.title: Sumsets and inverse theorems
Combinatorics.description: Size and structure of A+B, hA and restricted or signed sumsets: Cauchy–Davenport and Vosper, Freiman-type, Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers and polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorems, small doubling, sums of dilates, h-fold sumsets with distinct terms, rectification, sets determined by k-sums, max-min (lunar) decompositions, and sum-product and product-set growth.
Combinatorics.title: Sets with more sums than differences
Combinatorics.description: Comparison of |A+A| with |A−A|: sum-dominant (MSTD) and difference-dominated sets, minimal MSTD and MPTQ sets, Chu's constructions, unions of progressions, and the single-set sum-difference exponent.
Combinatorics.title: Sidon sets and difference sets
Combinatorics.description: Sidon and B_h-sets (bounds, counts, greedy and thick constructions, isolated sums, the Sidon ideal), Golomb rulers, difference bases, cyclic and perfect difference sets including Singer's theorem, and difference sets of sparse sets.
Combinatorics.title: Sum-free sets
Combinatorics.description: Sets with no solution to x+y=z or similar: sum-free sets in abelian groups and intervals, counts of sum-free and maximal sum-free sets, large sum-free subsets, square-sum-free, divisor-sum-free and non-averaging sets.
Combinatorics.title: Additive bases
Combinatorics.description: Sets whose h-fold sums cover the integers or a group: asymptotic, exact and restricted bases, Schnirelmann density, Rohrbach's theorem, representation counts and convolutions, sums of cubes covering vector spaces, knight-move bases of the plane, and sumsets of infinite sets of positive or zero density.
Combinatorics.title: Zero-sum problems and subset sums
Combinatorics.description: Davenport and weighted Davenport constants, zero-sum subsequences and cross numbers, Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv-type results, perfect subset-sum covers, zero subset sums and balanced subset sums in finite abelian groups, and subset sums with bounded numbers of terms.
Combinatorics.title: Arithmetic progressions in dense sets
Combinatorics.description: Density versions: Szemerédi's and Roth's theorems and Roth-number bounds, Gowers uniformity norms and the generalized von Neumann theorem, Sárközy's theorem, cap sets, counts of three-term progressions, progressions in complements and in walks, arithmetic progression API, and polynomial triangle removal in vector spaces.
Combinatorics.title: Ramsey theory
Combinatorics.description: Unavoidable monochromatic structure under finite colourings of integers, words, sets and semigroups; graph and ordered-graph Ramsey problems go to GraphTheory, ordinal and infinite-cardinal partition relations to SetTheory, density statements without colouring to additive combinatorics.
Combinatorics.title: Van der Waerden-type theorems
Combinatorics.description: Monochromatic arithmetic progressions: van der Waerden's theorem and van der Waerden numbers (off-diagonal, W(3,k)), short or large-difference progressions, rainbow progressions, descending waves, accessible sets and diffsequences, and progression-free Ramsey sets.
Combinatorics.title: Schur and Rado theorems
Combinatorics.description: Monochromatic solutions of equations: Schur's theorem and Schur and modular Schur numbers, Rado's theorem and disjunctive Rado, monochromatic linear equations, monochromatic sums, sums of squares and products, and rainbow-free colourings of x−y=z^k.
Combinatorics.title: Ramsey's theorem, Hales–Jewett and Hindman
Combinatorics.description: Ramsey's theorem for sets and hypergraphs (including size Ramsey numbers and Paris–Harrington), Hales–Jewett and density Hales–Jewett, Hindman's and the pairwise sum theorem via ultrafilters, central, J-, C- and piecewise syndetic sets in semigroups, and grid Ramsey properties.
Combinatorics.title: Extremal set theory and hypergraphs
Combinatorics.description: Largest or smallest families of finite sets under intersection, union or containment constraints, and hypergraphs (uniform set systems) studied by Turán, colouring, matching and covering parameters; problems about graphs go to GraphTheory.
Combinatorics.title: Intersecting families, Sperner theory and sunflowers
Combinatorics.description: Erdős–Ko–Rado and its variants, Chvátal's conjecture, forbidden and singleton intersections, comparable pairs, union-free and union-closed families, shadows (Kruskal–Katona, Macaulay), Harper's isoperimetric inequality, and sunflower bounds.
Combinatorics.title: Hypergraph Turán problems
Combinatorics.description: Turán numbers and densities of uniform hypergraphs: Turán systems, de Caen's question, generalized triangles, the (6,3) problem, locally sparse triple systems, and dense 3-uniform hypergraphs.
Combinatorics.title: Hypergraph colouring, matchings and covers
Combinatorics.description: Property B and hypergraph colouring, Erdős–Faber–Lovász, Kneser hypergraphs, independence in Steiner and linear triple systems, set mappings, strongly maximal matchings, minimal covers, transversals, Baranyai's theorem and common elements of small set families.
Combinatorics.title: Designs, Latin squares and combinatorial matrices
Combinatorics.description: Block designs, Steiner systems, pairwise balanced designs and linear spaces, Latin squares and transversals, Hadamard and partial Hadamard matrices, magic squares, 0-1 matrices with prescribed margins (Gale–Ryser), binary matrices up to rotation, and sign tables from determinant-moment expansions; cyclic difference sets go to Sidon sets and difference sets.
Combinatorics.title: Matroid theory
Combinatorics.description: Matroids and their invariants: algebraic matroids, Edmonds' intersection and partition theorems, Rado's theorem, characteristic polynomials and log-concavity, the Mason conjectures, Hodge theory for matroids, Lorentzian polynomials and M-convex sets, and lines in weighted matroids.
Combinatorics.title: Partially ordered sets
Combinatorics.description: Finite posets as combinatorial objects: Dilworth's and Mirsky's theorems, Erdős–Szekeres monotone subsequences, linear extensions, Möbius algebras and flag vectors, chain polynomials and Neggers' conjecture, Sperner properties of the weak order, rowmotion and toggle homomesy, poset matrices and rooted trees; lattice theory goes to Order.
Combinatorics.title: Polytopes, Ehrhart theory and simplicial complexes
Combinatorics.description: Face numbers and h-vectors of simplicial spheres and polytopes (Dehn–Sommerville, upper bound theorem), Cohen–Macaulay, partitionable and interval-decomposable complexes, simplicial homology, Ehrhart polynomials, h*-vectors and the integer decomposition property, lattice parallelograms, and hyperplane arrangements.
Combinatorics.title: Discrepancy theory
Combinatorics.description: How evenly a set system, matrix or vector family can be two-coloured: matrix and vector discrepancy, the Komlós and Beck–Fiala problems, hereditary discrepancy, vector balancing, balanced weighted colourings and balancing infinite families.
Combinatorics.title: Probabilistic combinatorics
Combinatorics.description: Probabilistic methods and random discrete structures outside random graphs: the Lovász local lemma, Littlewood–Offord and Tomaszewski anti-concentration for signed sums, concentration of subset sums, the isolation lemma, thresholds and expectation thresholds, random k-SAT thresholds, perfect matchings in random hypergraphs, the Chvátal–Sankoff constant for longest common subsequences, and moment-based counting bounds.
Combinatorics.title: Boolean functions
Combinatorics.description: Functions from {0,1}^n to {0,1}: counting monotone, self-dual and unate Boolean functions and Dedekind numbers, enumeration of k-SAT functions, noise stability and juntas, and parity and small-bias counts over finite fields.
Combinatorics.title: Elementary enumeration
Combinatorics.description: Counting basic objects under simple constraints: subsets, multisets and functions with prescribed values, Schreier-type and weighted Schreier sets, combinations avoiding given differences, necklaces and counting up to rotation, fibre and double counting, introductory catalogues of special counting sequences, and small extremal puzzles such as the bridge and torch problem.

ComputerScience.title: Computer Science
ComputerScience.description: Computer science formalizes algorithms, programming-language structures, data abstractions, and correctness properties.
ComputerScience.title: Data structures
ComputerScience.description: Representations of collections with their invariants, operations and costs (worst-case and amortized), whether the structure is developed on its own or as an augmented variant; an algorithm that merely uses a structure goes to the field of the problem it solves.
ComputerScience.title: Search trees and skip lists
ComputerScience.description: Ordered dictionaries: binary search trees and their balanced variants (AVL, red-black, 2-3, B-trees, splay, treaps, weight-balanced, Cartesian, order-statistic) and skip lists, including their insertion and deletion procedures.
ComputerScience.title: Heaps and priority queues
ComputerScience.description: Priority queues: binary, d-ary, binomial, Fibonacci and catenable heaps, indexed min-queues, and their sift, decrease-key and merge operations and costs.
ComputerScience.title: Hashing
ComputerScience.description: Hash tables (chaining, open addressing, cuckoo, perfect), universal hash families and Bloom filters including their false-positive analysis.
ComputerScience.title: Lists, stacks, queues and dynamic arrays
ComputerScience.description: Sequential containers and their amortized costs: linked lists (singly, doubly, sentinel), stacks with multipop, queues, deques, dynamic tables, binary counters, LRU caches, and generic list operations (ordered insertion, splitting, chunking, inclusive prefixes) that support them.
ComputerScience.title: Range-query and spatial structures
ComputerScience.description: Structures answering range, interval or nearest-point queries: segment trees, Fenwick trees, sparse tables, interval trees, range trees, kd-trees, ball trees and fractional cascading.
ComputerScience.title: Tries, suffix structures and integer dictionaries
ComputerScience.description: Prefix- and bit-indexed structures: tries, radix (Patricia) tries, suffix arrays and suffix trees, van Emde Boas trees, x-fast and y-fast tries.
ComputerScience.title: Disjoint sets and dynamic trees
ComputerScience.description: Union-find with rank and path compression (including its connected-components application), link-cut trees and Euler-tour trees.
ComputerScience.title: Graph algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms computing properties of explicit graphs (traversal, connectivity, shortest paths, spanning trees, flows, matchings, Euler circuits) with correctness and cost proofs; pure graph theory belongs to GraphTheory, and verifiers or reductions for NP problems belong to TheoryOfComputation.
ComputerScience.title: Graph traversal and connectivity
ComputerScience.description: Graph representations as adjacency lists and adjacency matrices, breadth-first and depth-first search with predecessor trees, strongly connected components, topological sorting, transitive closure and Hierholzer's Euler circuits.
ComputerScience.title: Shortest paths
ComputerScience.description: Single-source and all-pairs shortest paths: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, DAG relaxation, min-plus matrix products and APSP, Floyd-Warshall and Johnson.
ComputerScience.title: Spanning trees, flows and matchings
ComputerScience.description: Minimum spanning trees (Kruskal, Prim), maximum flow and minimum cut (Edmonds-Karp), bipartite matching by augmenting paths, and Gale-Shapley stable matching.
ComputerScience.title: Sorting and searching
ComputerScience.description: Comparison and distribution sorting algorithms (including their expected-cost analyses), and searching and selection in lists and arrays (binary and linear search, quickselect, median of medians, simultaneous min-max). Comparator sorting networks, their depth and the 0-1 principle form the Sorting networks subfield.
ComputerScience.title: Sorting networks
ComputerScience.description: Comparator networks that sort: the bubble network, Batcher's bitonic and odd–even merge networks, depth bounds, and the zero-one and permutation principles.
ComputerScience.title: Dynamic programming
ComputerScience.description: Optimization problems solved by tabulated recurrences: knapsack variants, subset sum, rod cutting, matrix-chain ordering, optimal binary search trees, longest common and longest increasing subsequences (including patience sorting) and maximum subarray (Kadane and divide-and-conquer); string edit distance goes to String algorithms.
ComputerScience.title: Greedy algorithms and matroids
ComputerScience.description: Greedy choice and exchange arguments: the matroid greedy algorithm and its characterization of matroids, graphic matroids, interval scheduling and furthest-in-future offline caching.
ComputerScience.title: Approximation algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Polynomial-time algorithms with proved approximation ratios for NP-hard optimization: vertex cover, set cover, metric TSP, list scheduling, maximum coverage, MAX-CUT by semidefinite programming and random-hyperplane rounding, MAX-SAT by randomized rounding, and the primal–dual method for constrained forest problems.
ComputerScience.title: Online algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms that act on a request sequence without knowing the future, and competitive-ratio upper and lower bounds: paging, list update, ski rental, online bipartite matching.
ComputerScience.title: Randomized algorithms and probabilistic analysis
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms whose identity is their use of randomness or whose analysis averages over random inputs: expected running time under input distributions, Fisher-Yates shuffling, the hiring problem, Karger's minimum cut, Freivalds' matrix-product check and MinHash similarity sketches.
ComputerScience.title: Parallel algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Work-span models, Brent's theorem and greedy scheduling, parallel prefix sums (Blelloch, Kogge-Stone) and pointer-jumping list ranking.
ComputerScience.title: Memory-hierarchy algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms analyzed by the data they move between levels of a memory hierarchy: the ideal-cache model, cache-oblivious scanning and matrix transposition, and the simulation of optimal replacement by LRU.
ComputerScience.title: Algebraic and numerical algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms on numbers, polynomials and matrices: integer and polynomial multiplication (Karatsuba, FFT and convolution), matrix multiplication (iterative, recursive, Strassen), Horner evaluation, floating-point rounding, modular exponentiation and linear congruences, Miller-Rabin primality testing, and bit-level polynomial and bitvector arithmetic.
ComputerScience.title: Computational geometry
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms on points and segments in the plane: orientation and segment intersection, sweep-line intersection detection, convex hulls and closest pair; geometric search structures stay in Data structures.
ComputerScience.title: String algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Exact pattern matching (naive, finite automaton, Knuth-Morris-Pratt, Boyer-Moore, Rabin-Karp, Z algorithm) and edit distance with edit scripts; biological sequence alignment belongs to Biology.
ComputerScience.title: Heuristic search and planning
ComputerScience.description: Search and decision procedures from artificial intelligence: A* search, game-tree search with alpha-beta pruning, arc consistency for constraint satisfaction, and dynamic programming for Markov decision processes (value and policy iteration, optimality of stationary policies, stochastic shortest path problems).
ComputerScience.title: Cryptography
ComputerScience.description: Cryptographic schemes and their correctness and security reductions: the game-based framework of security proofs, symmetric-key encryption and authentication, hash functions and Merkle trees, public-key encryption and key agreement, signatures, identification protocols and commitments; and differential privacy, the definition of privacy for statistical data analysis, with its composition theorems and the Laplace and exponential mechanisms.
ComputerScience.title: Security games and proof techniques
ComputerScience.description: The framework of game-based security proofs: adaptive oracle algorithms and their probabilistic semantics, games and advantages, generic security experiments for encryption, MACs and signatures, asymptotic security, the hybrid argument and the difference lemma, and lazy sampling with the PRP/PRF switching lemma.
ComputerScience.title: Symmetric-key cryptography
ComputerScience.description: Perfect secrecy and the one-time pad, pseudorandom generators and stream ciphers, pseudorandom functions and permutations, message authentication, and authenticated encryption by encrypt-then-MAC.
ComputerScience.title: Hash functions
ComputerScience.description: Collisions and the birthday bound, the Merkle–Damgård transform and its padding, and Merkle trees with authentication paths.
ComputerScience.title: Public-key cryptography
ComputerScience.description: Discrete-logarithm, Diffie–Hellman and RSA hardness assumptions, Diffie–Hellman key agreement, ElGamal and RSA encryption with their security and insecurity, deterministic encryption, and key encapsulation with hybrid encryption.
ComputerScience.title: Signatures, identification and commitments
ComputerScience.description: Lamport one-time and Merkle many-time signatures, Schnorr identification and sigma protocols, and hash-based and Pedersen commitments.
ComputerScience.title: Databases
ComputerScience.description: Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normal forms and lossless decomposition, and transaction concurrency control (conflict serializability, two-phase locking).
ComputerScience.title: Quantum algorithms
ComputerScience.description: Algorithms for quantum computers and their analysis: Fourier sampling with the Deutsch–Jozsa and Bernstein–Vazirani algorithms, Grover search and the matching Ω(√N) query lower bound of Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard and Vazirani, and Shor's factoring algorithm with its classical reduction of factoring to order finding and its continued-fraction post-processing.
ComputerScience.title: Process calculi and behavioural equivalence
ComputerScience.description: Algebraic models of concurrent processes: labelled transition systems and their runs, strong and weak bisimulation, observational congruence, CCS (choice, parallel composition, restriction, recursion, finite-state agents) and the pi-calculus.
ComputerScience.title: Session types
ComputerScience.description: Session types for the π-calculus: binary protocols and their duality, linear endpoint typing with ownership contexts, subject reduction, progress by priorities, typing up to protocol equivalence, and shared and recursive services.
ComputerScience.title: Concurrent systems and protocols
ComputerScience.description: Specific concurrent or distributed systems and their verified properties: deadlock and its detection, the banker's algorithm, dining philosophers, and communication protocols such as the alternating-bit protocol and go-back-N.
ComputerScience.title: Programming language semantics
ComputerScience.description: Operational and denotational semantics of programming languages and correctness of compilation: the IMP language (syntax, big- and small-step, heap semantics, denotational semantics, stack-machine compilation), PCF with adequacy and contextual equivalence, CPS translation and closure conversion.
ComputerScience.title: Type systems and lambda calculi
ComputerScience.description: Typed lambda calculi and type inference: the simply typed lambda calculus (syntax, substitution, normalization, logical relations, normalization by evaluation, elaboration, its models), lambda calculus with references and type safety, and Hindley-Milner let-polymorphism with Algorithm W.
ComputerScience.title: Functional programming structures
ComputerScience.description: Functors, applicative functors, monads and traversal as structures of functional programming, together with recursive computations, lazy lists and streams. Abstract categories, functors and monads are treated under Category Theory.
ComputerScience.title: Program logics and verification
ComputerScience.description: Logics for proving programs correct: Hoare logic for partial and total correctness with soundness and relative completeness, weakest preconditions, verification-condition generation, and separation logic.
ComputerScience.title: Computer security
ComputerScience.description: Formal models of security policies and their decision problems, such as the access-matrix protection systems of Harrison, Ruzzo and Ullman.
ComputerScience.title: Computer systems
ComputerScience.description: Models of operating-system and hardware mechanisms and their correctness: paged address translation and page replacement, cache coherence protocols and memory consistency models.
ComputerScience.title: Machine learning
ComputerScience.description: Mathematical theory of learning from data, including the probabilistic modelling, inference and sampling methods used in machine learning.
ComputerScience.title: PAC learning
ComputerScience.description: Valiant's model of learning from random examples, on CSLib's PAC library (error, learners, version spaces, consistency, PAC learnability, VC dimension): Valiant's Bernoulli-trial bound, the Occam bound for consistent learners over a finite class, learning k-CNF by elimination, the fundamental theorem relating PAC learnability to the VC dimension, and the bridge between the 0-1 risk and CSLib's error. Uniform deviation bounds for the agnostic case are under [generalization bounds and concentration](../generalization-bounds-and-concentration/README.md); boosting weak learners is under [online learning and boosting](../online-learning-and-boosting/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Online learning and boosting
ComputerScience.description: Mistake and regret bounds for sequential prediction: perceptron, weighted majority, Hedge (multiplicative weights) and AdaBoost.
ComputerScience.title: Reinforcement learning theory
ComputerScience.description: Theory of reinforcement learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes: stochastic policies, discounted state occupancies, the performance difference lemma, conservative policy iteration, the simulation lemma, and policy gradient methods with the global convergence of natural policy gradient.
ComputerScience.title: Supervised learning and regression
ComputerScience.description: Prediction from labelled data: least squares, ridge, lasso and kernel or Gaussian-process regression (including GBLUP), the bias-variance decomposition, Bayes classifiers and optimal predictors, log loss, decision-tree information gain, backpropagation, and sufficient input subsets. Ridge regression is the finite-dimensional case of [Tikhonov regularization](../../../Analysis/convex-analysis-and-variations/tikhonov-regularization/README.md); point estimation theory (risk, sufficiency, James–Stein shrinkage) is under [statistical estimation](../../../Probability/statistical-estimation/README.md), and Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares under [linear models and multivariate analysis](../../../Probability/linear-models-multivariate/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Unsupervised learning and matrix factorization
ComputerScience.description: Structure in unlabelled data: k-means, single-linkage hierarchical clustering, archetypal analysis, nonnegative matrix factorization, the successive projection algorithm, and probabilistic PCA with the Gaussian factor-analysis marginal. Classical principal component analysis is under [linear models and multivariate analysis](../../../Probability/linear-models-multivariate/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Probabilistic graphical models
ComputerScience.description: Bayesian networks and their Markov properties, structure scores and Markov equivalence, causal networks and adjustment, belief propagation and variable elimination, conditional random fields, hidden Markov models (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch) and the Kalman filter.
ComputerScience.title: Bayesian inference and sampling
ComputerScience.description: Bayes' rule and conjugate models, expectation-maximization for mixtures and latent-variable models, variational mean-field inference, and Monte Carlo, rejection, Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings sampling. Bayesian nonparametric priors (the Dirichlet process and urn schemes, and the Chinese restaurant and Indian buffet processes as infinite limits of finite mixture and feature models) are under [Bayesian statistics](../../../Probability/bayesian-statistics/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Attention and low-rank adaptation
ComputerScience.description: Linear algebra of recent methods for adapting and running transformer layers: low-rank adaptation of a frozen weight matrix (LoRA), its initialisation from the principal singular values and vectors of the pretrained matrix (PiSSA), and the identity-plus-rank-one state transitions of delta-rule linear attention (DeltaNet). These pages are expositions of published methods without Lean formalization; each names the linear algebra it relies on, and how, under Informally uses. Singular value decompositions are under [matrix decompositions](../../../LinearAlgebra/matrix-decompositions/singular-value-decomposition/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Linear state-space sequence models
ComputerScience.description: Linear algebra of recent state-space sequence layers such as Mamba and Mamba-2: for fixed parameters, a linear time-varying state-space recurrence acts along the sequence as multiplication by a semiseparable matrix, and a time-invariant one as a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix, that is, a causal convolution. These pages are expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names the linear algebra it relies on, and how, under Informally uses. Semiseparable matrices are under [special matrices](../../../LinearAlgebra/special-matrices/semiseparable-matrices/README.md).
ComputerScience.title: Diffusion and flow-based generative models
ComputerScience.description: Linear algebra of diffusion and flow-based generative models: for Gaussian data, the score and the optimal denoiser are spectral functions of the data covariance and the probability-flow ODE is a linear system with commuting coefficients whose flow map is an explicit affine map; for any differentiable velocity field, the divergence in the log-density computations of flow models is the trace of a Jacobian. These pages are AI-authored expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names what it relies on, and how, under Informally uses, and marks results not stated in its sources as derived.
ComputerScience.title: Generalization bounds and concentration
ComputerScience.description: Uniform deviation bounds between the empirical and the expected risk, obtained from concentration inequalities: for a finite class, Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound; for a general class, McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality concentrates the supremum of the deviations around its mean, and Rademacher averages control its expectation. The finite-class bound, the reduction of empirical risk minimization to a uniform deviation bound and the dimension-free Rademacher average of a ball of linear predictors are formalized; the two pages marked as expositions are AI-authored expositions of published results without Lean formalization.

Dynamics.title: Dynamical Systems
Dynamics.description: Dynamics studies systems evolving through iteration or time, including recurrence, stability, and long-term behavior.
Dynamics.title: Ergodic theory
Dynamics.description: Ergodic theory studies measure-preserving transformations and their statistical behaviour: ergodic averages, recurrence, mixing and the structure of measure-preserving actions.
Dynamics.title: Topological and symbolic dynamics
Dynamics.description: Topological dynamics studies continuous maps of topological spaces through orbits, periodic points and recurrence, and symbolic dynamics studies shift spaces and cellular automata on sequences of symbols.
Dynamics.title: Low-dimensional dynamics
Dynamics.description: Low-dimensional dynamics covers maps of the interval and circle, continued-fraction-type maps, flows in the plane and homeomorphisms of surfaces.
Dynamics.title: Smooth dynamics
Dynamics.description: Smooth dynamics studies differentiable maps and flows: hyperbolicity, stable manifolds and shadowing, Lyapunov exponents and entropy, Hamiltonian perturbation theory, and stability of flows given by differential equations.
Dynamics.title: Complex dynamics
Dynamics.description: Complex dynamics studies the iteration of holomorphic maps, especially polynomials, together with their Julia sets and parameter spaces such as the Mandelbrot set.
Dynamics.title: Homogeneous dynamics
Dynamics.description: Homogeneous dynamics studies flows and group actions on homogeneous spaces of Lie groups, such as unipotent and horocycle flows on quotients by lattices and Kleinian groups, with applications to values of quadratic forms, lattice point counting and circle packings.

FieldTheory.title: Field Theory
FieldTheory.description: Field theory studies extensions of fields, algebraic elements, automorphisms, and Galois-theoretic structure.
FieldTheory.title: Galois theory
FieldTheory.description: Galois theory relates a field extension to its group of automorphisms, covering the Galois correspondence, infinite Galois groups, Hilbert's theorem 90, solvability by radicals and essential dimension.
FieldTheory.title: Finite fields
FieldTheory.description: Finite fields and polynomials over them: irreducible and primitive polynomials, permutation polynomials, and the arithmetic of squares.
FieldTheory.title: Field extensions and algebraic closure
FieldTheory.description: Algebraic field extensions and closures: minimal polynomials, separable and purely inseparable extensions, base change to separably closed fields, algebraic closures of series fields and quasi-algebraically closed fields.
FieldTheory.title: Transcendental extensions and function fields
FieldTheory.description: Algebraic independence, transcendence bases and transcendence degree, separably generated extensions, fields of rational functions and Lüroth's theorem, and differential fields with Liouville's theorem on elementary integrals. Algebraic extensions are under field extensions and algebraic closure; the arithmetic of global function fields is under number theory.

GameTheory.title: Game Theory
GameTheory.description: Game theory studies strategic and combinatorial interaction, equilibria, winning conditions, and optimal play.
GameTheory.title: Combinatorial game theory
GameTheory.description: Combinatorial game theory studies two-player games of perfect information without chance: impartial games such as Nim and its variants (P-positions, Sprague–Grundy values, remoteness), partizan games such as Snort, and Maker–Breaker positional games.
GameTheory.title: Cooperative game theory
GameTheory.description: Cooperative game theory studies games in which coalitions of players can make binding agreements, and solution concepts such as the core and the Shapley value for dividing a coalition's worth.
GameTheory.title: Mechanism design
GameTheory.description: Mechanism design studies how to choose the rules of a game, with or without money, so that self-interested agents with private information reach a desired outcome in equilibrium: the revelation principle, incentive compatibility and Myerson's characterization of single-parameter mechanisms, revenue equivalence and optimal auctions, Vickrey–Clarke–Groves mechanisms, and impossibility results for bilateral trade.
GameTheory.title: Noncooperative games
GameTheory.description: Noncooperative game theory studies strategic games in which each player chooses a strategy to optimise its own payoff or cost: Nash equilibria and the minimax theorem, evolutionarily stable strategies, potential and congestion games, routing games with Wardrop equilibria, the price of anarchy and of stability, learning dynamics such as no-regret play, regret matching and Blackwell approachability together with correlated and coarse correlated equilibria, and mean field games with a continuum of players.
GameTheory.title: Matching markets
GameTheory.description: Two-sided matching markets: stable matchings of marriage and college-admissions markets, the lattice of stable matchings and the opposition of the two sides' interests, properties shared by all stable matchings such as the rural hospitals theorem, and the incentives of stable matching mechanisms, from Roth's impossibility theorem to the strategy-proofness of deferred acceptance for the proposing side. The stable marriage problem and the Gale–Shapley existence theorem are under GraphTheory/matchings-and-flows, and the deferred-acceptance algorithm under ComputerScience/graph-algorithms.
GameTheory.title: Social choice theory
GameTheory.description: Social choice theory studies rules that aggregate individual preferences into a collective ranking or choice, and the impossibility theorems that limit them.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.description: Geometry studies shapes, spaces, transformations, curvature, and the invariants preserved by geometric equivalence.
Geometry.title: Affine and projective geometry
Geometry.description: Affine spaces over modules: affine maps and equivalences, affine subspaces, affine combinations and barycentric coordinates, affine independence and simplices; and projective spaces of vector spaces with their subspaces, independence and collinearity. Metric notions are under Euclidean geometry.
Geometry.title: Euclidean geometry
Geometry.description: Classical synthetic and metric geometry of the Euclidean plane and space: triangles, circles, conics, polygons, isometries and the foundations of geometry.
Geometry.title: Euclidean affine spaces
Geometry.description: Real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces of any dimension: unoriented and oriented angles, orthogonal projections onto affine subspaces, signed distances, and volumes of simplices. Plane rotations and other Euclidean isometries are under isometries and symmetry.
Geometry.title: Triangle geometry
Geometry.description: Theorems about triangles, their centers, cevians, inscribed and circumscribed circles, and triangle inequalities.
Geometry.title: Circles and conics
Geometry.description: Configurations of circles and conics, tangency, chains of circles, lunes, and mathematical billiards in elliptic and polygonal tables.
Geometry.title: Polygons and quadrilaterals
Geometry.description: Theorems about quadrilaterals, cyclic polygons and squares erected on polygon sides.
Geometry.title: Solid and spherical geometry
Geometry.description: Metric relations for tetrahedra and other solids, and trigonometry on the sphere.
Geometry.title: Isometries and crystallographic groups
Geometry.description: Distance-preserving maps of Euclidean space, their classification, and discrete symmetry groups such as wallpaper and space groups.
Geometry.title: Foundations and constructions
Geometry.description: Axiom systems for plane geometry and the limits of compass-and-straightedge constructions.
Geometry.title: Convex geometry
Geometry.description: Convex sets and convex bodies in Euclidean space: Helly-type and Radon-type theorems, partitions, sections, valuations and linear optimization over polyhedra.
Geometry.title: Packings and coverings
Geometry.description: Optimal arrangements of congruent bodies in space and the smallest sets or fewest translates needed to cover given families of shapes.
Geometry.title: Discrete geometry
Geometry.description: Finite point configurations and their distances, polytopes and polyhedra, dissections and tilings, lattice points and extremal shape problems.
Geometry.title: Metric geometry
Geometry.description: Geometry of general metric spaces: curvature bounds via comparison, length spaces, isometric embeddings and low-distortion embeddings.
Geometry.title: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces
Geometry.description: Curvature, tangents and global properties of curves and surfaces in Euclidean space, including knotted curves and inscribed figures.
Geometry.title: Riemannian and Finsler geometry
Geometry.description: Manifolds with smoothly varying inner products or norms on tangent spaces: connections, curvature, geodesics, differential operators and rigidity theorems.
Geometry.title: Differential topology
Geometry.description: Smooth manifolds and smooth maps between them: immersions, submersions, transversality, Morse theory, neighbourhood theorems and smooth structures.
Geometry.title: Complex and symplectic geometry
Geometry.description: Manifolds with complex, almost complex, symplectic or contact structures, Riemann surfaces, and integrable Hamiltonian systems.

GraphTheory.title: Graph Theory
GraphTheory.description: Graph theory studies vertices and edges through connectivity, coloring, minors, flows, and extremal structure.
GraphTheory.title: Graphs, subgraphs and homomorphisms
GraphTheory.description: Simple graphs and multigraphs, adjacency, degrees, subgraphs, deletion and copies of graphs. The algebraic theory of homomorphisms, cores and covers belongs to Algebraic graph theory.
GraphTheory.title: Paths, cycles and connectivity
GraphTheory.description: Walks, paths and cycles in graphs, Eulerian and Hamiltonian cycles, and vertex and edge connectivity, including Menger's theorem and Fleischner's theorem on squares of 2-connected graphs.
GraphTheory.title: Graph coloring
GraphTheory.description: Vertex, edge, list and fractional colorings of graphs and the chromatic number, from Brooks' and Vizing's theorems to perfect graphs and the four color theorem.
GraphTheory.title: Matchings and flows
GraphTheory.description: Matchings and factors in graphs, stable matchings, and flows in networks, including Kőnig's theorem, Berge's lemma and the max-flow min-cut theorem.
GraphTheory.title: Independence, cliques and domination
GraphTheory.description: Independent sets, cliques and dominating sets in graphs, with bounds on their sizes and polynomials counting them.
GraphTheory.title: Extremal graph theory
GraphTheory.description: How many edges or copies of a subgraph a graph can have while avoiding a forbidden structure: Turán and Zarankiewicz problems, saturation, and extremal graphs of given girth.
GraphTheory.title: Ramsey theory for graphs
GraphTheory.description: Ramsey numbers of graphs, their known small values, and Ramsey–Turán problems.
GraphTheory.title: Algebraic graph theory
GraphTheory.description: Graphs studied through groups and matrices: Cayley and vertex-transitive graphs, strongly regular and Moore graphs, graph homomorphisms, Laplacians and the matrix-tree theorem, and named graphs such as the Petersen and Coxeter graphs.
GraphTheory.title: Planar graphs and minors
GraphTheory.description: Graphs drawn in the plane and on the square lattice, crossing numbers, Euler's formula, discrete Jordan curve and turning-number theorems, and the theory of graph minors.
GraphTheory.title: Graph invariants and labelings
GraphTheory.description: Numerical and polynomial invariants of graphs such as degree sequences, arboricity, induced forest number, Shannon capacity and the chromatic symmetric function, and graph labelings.
GraphTheory.title: Directed graphs and tournaments
GraphTheory.description: Directed graphs, orientations of undirected graphs, digraph colorings and tournaments.
GraphTheory.title: Graph families and operations
GraphTheory.description: Graph products, line graphs and other constructions, together with special families such as expanders and the hypercubic lattice.
GraphTheory.title: Random graphs and graph limits
GraphTheory.description: Random graph models such as Erdős–Rényi, random regular and random k-out graphs, the typical values of their invariants (chromatic number, independence ratio, connectivity, spectra), and graphons as limits of dense graph sequences.
GraphTheory.title: Social and complex networks
GraphTheory.description: Graph-theoretic models of social and information networks: degree statistics and the friendship paradox, clustering and centrality measures, structural balance of signed graphs, and deterministic threshold processes on weighted graphs.

GroupTheory.title: Group Theory
GroupTheory.description: Group theory studies symmetry through groups, actions, subgroups, quotients, and structural decompositions.
GroupTheory.title: Groups, subgroups and quotients
GroupTheory.description: Group axioms and homomorphisms, subgroups and their lattice, cosets and index, normal subgroups, quotient groups and the isomorphism theorems, centres and centralizers, simple groups and particular groups such as cyclic, dihedral and dicyclic groups. Actions, conjugacy classes, commutators, extensions and the structure of abelian groups have their own fields.
GroupTheory.title: Semigroups and monoids
GroupTheory.description: Magmas, semigroups and monoids and their morphisms: units and invertible elements, commuting and semiconjugate elements, submonoids and subsemigroups, monoids and groups with zero, congruences and quotients, free magmas, semigroups and monoids, localization of commutative monoids, the Grothendieck group and Ore localization, opposites and adjoined identities; groups proper are under Groups, subgroups and quotients.
GroupTheory.title: Abelian groups
GroupTheory.description: Structure of abelian groups: finite and finitely generated abelian groups (invariant factors, elementary divisors, torsion, ranks, dual groups), torsion-free and infinite abelian groups (Baer–Specker group, pure subgroups, direct-sum cancellation, ultraproducts of abelian groups); colourings and partitions of abelian groups go to Combinatorics in groups.
GroupTheory.title: Group orders, element orders and spectra
GroupTheory.description: Arithmetic of finite groups through orders: cyclic numbers and groups of a given order (groups of order 10, dihedral groups from an index-two cyclic subgroup), counts of elements of each order, the spectrum (set of element orders), recognition of groups by spectrum or by order and spectrum, Thompson's type, and totient sums; conjugacy-class sizes go to Conjugacy classes.
GroupTheory.title: Conjugacy classes
GroupTheory.description: Conjugacy classes of groups as a structural invariant: class sizes and breadth, the class number, commuting probability, Thompson's conjecture on class sizes, products of conjugacy classes, and relations between class sizes and group structure; class sizes of p-groups go to Finite p-groups, and character-theoretic class arguments to Characters of finite groups.
GroupTheory.title: Finite simple groups and involutions
GroupTheory.description: Finite simple and almost simple groups and the local analysis behind their classification: specific simple groups (Mathieu, Suzuki, PSL), strongly embedded subgroups (Bender–Suzuki), classification by Sylow 2-subgroups (Gorenstein–Walter, Brauer–Suzuki), Baer–Suzuki, Glauberman Z*, Brauer–Fowler, involution centralizers and 3-transpositions; generation questions go to Generation of groups and spectrum recognition to Group orders, element orders and spectra.
GroupTheory.title: Generation of groups
GroupTheory.description: Minimal and special generating sets: generator numbers of almost simple and soluble groups, (2,3)-generation, generation by elements of prime-power order, spread, coprime generation, two-generated direct powers, Eulerian functions and probabilistic generation.
GroupTheory.title: Sylow and Hall subgroups
GroupTheory.description: Sylow theory and its generalization to sets of primes: Hall π-subgroups, the classes E_π, C_π and D_π, pronormality and intersections of Hall subgroups, groups whose maximal subgroups are Hall; questions on supplements of Sylow maximal subgroups forcing solubility go to Soluble and supersoluble finite groups.
GroupTheory.title: Subgroup embedding and subgroup lattices
