GroupTheory.description: How subgroups sit inside a group: subnormal, permutable, propermutable, pronormal, polynormal and paranormal subgroups, maximal subgroups and their conjugates, intersections of conjugates of nilpotent subgroups and injectors with the Fitting subgroup, centralizer lattices and complemented subgroup lattices.
GroupTheory.title: Soluble and supersoluble finite groups
GroupTheory.description: Structure of finite soluble groups: supersolubility criteria, p-solubility and p-length, chief factors and their complements, σ-solubility and σ-nilpotency, Schmidt subgroups, derived length bounds for finite groups of special type, and factorized groups; classes of groups closed under operations go to Formations and Fitting classes.
GroupTheory.title: Formations and Fitting classes
GroupTheory.description: Classes of finite groups: formations, local and hereditary formations, Fitting and radical classes, injectors, subgroup functors, residuals, and lattices of formations; varieties defined by laws go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations.
GroupTheory.title: Factorized groups
GroupTheory.description: Groups that are products G = AB of two or more subgroups, finite or infinite: solubility, nilpotency and derived length of products of abelian, nilpotent, minimax or soluble factors (Itô and Kegel–Wielandt type theorems), triple factorizations, subnormal subgroups of factorized groups, and classes of groups closed under such products; supersoluble factorizations and products of maximal subgroups stay in Soluble and supersoluble finite groups, formations and Fitting classes in general in Formations and Fitting classes, and products of periodic subgroups in Periodic and locally finite groups.
GroupTheory.title: Finite p-groups
GroupTheory.description: Groups of prime-power order: composition series, Frattini subgroups and Φ-extensions, special, powerful, metacyclic and Camina p-groups, conjugacy class sizes of p-groups, generalized quaternion groups, coclass and rank analogues, derived length bounds, and orders of automorphism groups of p-groups only when the p-group structure is the point.
GroupTheory.title: Characters of finite groups
GroupTheory.description: Complex characters and representations used to study finite groups: class functions and orthogonality, irreducible character bases, character degrees and values, McKay conjecture, rational groups, permutation characters, blocks of defect zero, Frobenius group determinant, convolution on finite groups, and Burnside's p^a q^b theorem; general representation theory of algebras and Lie groups belongs to RepresentationTheory.
GroupTheory.title: Permutation groups and group actions
GroupTheory.description: Groups acting on sets: orbits, stabilizers, fixed-point counts, transitivity, bases, closures, Frobenius groups, symmetric and alternating groups as permutation groups, and infinite permutation groups (highly homogeneous, cofinitary, oligomorphic, subdegree-finite).
GroupTheory.title: Group actions
GroupTheory.description: Actions of monoids and groups on sets in general: orbits, stabilizers and the orbit–stabilizer theorem, fixed points, quotients and orbit spaces, equivariant maps, invariant subsets, the conjugation action, actions on functions and pointwise actions on sets, faithful and pretransitive actions, and equidecompositions; finite and infinite permutation groups proper have their own subfields.
GroupTheory.title: Finite permutation groups
GroupTheory.description: Actions of finite groups on finite sets: Burnside-type counting, stabilizers, multiply and doubly transitive finite groups, Frobenius groups, bases and independent sets, 2-closures, regular orbits of linear actions, coverings and products in finite symmetric groups.
GroupTheory.title: Symmetric and alternating groups
GroupTheory.description: The symmetric group of a set as a group: support, cycles and cycle decomposition, cycle types and conjugacy classes, the sign homomorphism, generation by transpositions and cycles, the alternating group, its simplicity and its maximal subgroups, and centralizers of permutations; enumerative statistics of permutations are under Combinatorics.
GroupTheory.title: Infinite permutation groups
GroupTheory.description: Permutation groups on infinite sets: highly homogeneous groups of orders, circular orders and betweenness (Cameron), the pointwise topology on permutations, cofinitary and subdegree-finite groups, infinite sharply or doubly transitive groups, embeddings into the infinite symmetric group, class transpositions of the integers.
GroupTheory.title: Free groups and their automorphisms
GroupTheory.description: Free groups and free metabelian groups: subgroups (inert, compressed, retracts, fixed subgroups), elements (primitive, test, orbit-blocking words, normal closures), and the groups Aut(F_n), Out(F_n) and IA-automorphisms; equations over free groups go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations, and commutator length to Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions.
GroupTheory.title: Subgroups and elements of free groups
GroupTheory.description: Subgroup and element structure inside free and free metabelian groups: rank, inertness and compressedness, derived subgroups, retracts, primitive and equally distributed elements, independent sets, separation, Cayley–Hamilton analogues and characteristic quotients.
GroupTheory.title: Automorphisms of free groups
GroupTheory.description: The groups Aut(F_n) and Out(F_n): fixed points and fixed subgroups of automorphisms, word problem, automaticity, linearity of IA-automorphisms, embeddings of free products into Aut(F_n).
GroupTheory.title: Presentations and decision problems
GroupTheory.description: Combinatorial group theory: presentations, one-relator groups, HNN extensions and embeddings, SQ-universality, finitely presented simple groups, the word and conjugacy problems (Novikov–Boone, Boone–Higman), Andrews–Curtis moves, generic properties of presentations and torsion quotients.
GroupTheory.title: Braid and Artin groups
GroupTheory.description: Braid groups, pure braid groups and Artin–Tits groups of Coxeter matrices: endomorphisms, roots, conjugators and conjugacy questions.
GroupTheory.title: Geometric group theory
GroupTheory.description: Large-scale and analytic properties of finitely generated groups: growth, word-hyperbolic groups and their quotients, amenability and Følner sets, elementary amenable groups, property (T), soficity and permutation stability.
GroupTheory.title: Branch, automaton and Thompson groups
GroupTheory.description: Groups acting on rooted trees, branch and just-infinite groups of intermediate growth, finite-state (automaton) groups, and Thompson's group F and its piecewise-linear relatives.
GroupTheory.title: Orderable groups
GroupTheory.description: Left-, right- and bi-orderable groups: spaces of orders, generalized torsion, unique product groups, relatively convex subgroups, orderability of homeomorphism groups and amalgams, and decision problems for orderable groups.
GroupTheory.title: Varieties, quasivarieties and equations
GroupTheory.description: Groups defined by laws and quasi-identities: varieties, relatively free groups, test ranks, quasivarieties and their lattices, Hall's verbal conjectures, plus equations over groups, equationally Noetherian groups, geometric equivalence and elementary theories of groups.
GroupTheory.title: Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions
GroupTheory.description: Commutator calculus and nilpotency in (often infinite) groups: basic commutators, Engel elements, locally nilpotent and hypercentral groups, metabelian and polycyclic groups, localization of nilpotent groups, commutator width and length, word maps and their images, and local word identities.
GroupTheory.title: Automorphisms of groups
GroupTheory.description: Automorphism and endomorphism groups of groups other than free groups: their orders and realizations, outer automorphism groups, class-preserving automorphisms, and automorphisms with few fixed points or twisted conjugacy classes.
GroupTheory.title: Automorphism groups
GroupTheory.description: The automorphism group as an object: orders of automorphism groups, realizing groups as (outer) automorphism groups, class-preserving and inner automorphisms, automorphism orbits, endomorphism counts.
GroupTheory.title: Fixed points of automorphisms
GroupTheory.description: How an automorphism and its fixed points control a group: almost regular and fixed-point-free automorphisms, bounds on derived length and Fitting height, twisted conjugacy, e- and nil-automorphisms, squares of 2-automorphisms.
GroupTheory.title: Periodic and locally finite groups
GroupTheory.description: Infinite groups defined by torsion and finiteness conditions: Burnside problems and free Burnside groups, Golod groups, Tarski monsters, locally finite simple groups, periodic Frobenius groups, minimal and weak chain conditions, and embeddings into simple periodic groups.
GroupTheory.title: Profinite and topological groups
GroupTheory.description: Groups with topology or approximated by finite quotients: profinite and pro-p groups, residual finiteness and separability, profinite rigidity, Golod–Shafarevich inequality, just-infinite groups, totally disconnected locally compact groups, group topologies, Lie groups and their dense subgroups.
GroupTheory.title: Linear groups
GroupTheory.description: Groups of matrices over fields and rings: SL2, PGL2 and SU(2) and their conjugacy and subgroups (Dickson's classification), Jordan, Malcev and Selberg theorems, transvections, eigenvalues of elements of prime order, and linearity of specific groups.
GroupTheory.title: Group rings
GroupTheory.description: Group rings and group algebras: unit and zero-divisor questions (Kaplansky unit conjecture), Zassenhaus conjectures, augmentation and dimension subgroups, Ore conditions, Jordan decomposition, projective modules over group rings.
GroupTheory.title: Combinatorics in groups
GroupTheory.description: Additive and Ramsey-type combinatorics inside groups: approximate subgroups and product theorems, small doubling, partitions and colourings of groups, dense and coset-free partitions, subset factorizations, products of large normal subsets.
GroupTheory.title: Group extensions and cohomology
GroupTheory.description: Extensions and complements (Schur–Zassenhaus), splitting of extensions, homology and first cohomology of groups, cohomological dimension, and integrability of groups as derived subgroups.

InformationTheory.title: Information Theory
InformationTheory.description: Information theory quantifies information, uncertainty, compression, and transmission through entropy and coding.
InformationTheory.title: Entropy and mutual information
InformationTheory.description: Shannon entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Kullback–Leibler divergence, the basic measures of uncertainty and dependence between random variables.
InformationTheory.title: Information inequalities
InformationTheory.description: Inequalities relating entropies, divergences and mutual information, such as the log-sum, Pinsker, Fano, data-processing and Shearer inequalities.
InformationTheory.title: Source coding
InformationTheory.description: Lossless compression of information sources by variable-length codes, including prefix codes, the Kraft–McMillan inequality and Shannon's source coding bounds.
InformationTheory.title: Channel simulation
InformationTheory.description: Simulating a noisy channel with shared randomness and auxiliary random variables, including one-shot channel simulation and the functional representation lemma.
InformationTheory.title: Error-correcting codes
InformationTheory.description: Codes that detect or correct transmission errors, including linear codes, Hamming and Reed–Solomon codes, cyclic redundancy checks, and the Hamming-space geometry used to bound them.
InformationTheory.title: Channel coding
InformationTheory.description: Reliable transmission over noisy channels: channel capacity, Shannon's noisy-channel coding theorem, and its weak and strong converses.
InformationTheory.title: Signal processing and detection
InformationTheory.description: Discrete and continuous signals and linear time-invariant systems, sampling and reconstruction, filtering and frequency response, quantization, modulation and detection.

LinearAlgebra.title: Linear Algebra
LinearAlgebra.description: Linear algebra studies vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, duality, dimension, and spectral structure.
LinearAlgebra.title: Bases and dimension
LinearAlgebra.description: Linear independence, spanning families and bases of modules and vector spaces, rank and dimension (finite and infinite), finite-dimensional vector spaces, free modules and free modules over principal ideal domains, and the invariant basis number property.
LinearAlgebra.title: Linear maps and duality
LinearAlgebra.description: Vector spaces and modules, linear maps and their invariants such as trace, dual spaces, dual bases and perfect pairings, and exactness of sequences of linear maps.
LinearAlgebra.title: Matrices and matrix algebra
LinearAlgebra.description: Matrices over rings and their algebra: matrix multiplication, transposes and conjugate transposes, block matrices, permutation matrices, Kronecker products, matrices of linear maps and of bilinear and sesquilinear forms, invertibility and rank. Determinants, eigenvalues, decompositions and special classes such as diagonal matrices have their own fields.
LinearAlgebra.title: Eigenvalues and canonical forms
LinearAlgebra.description: Eigenvalues, eigenspaces and characteristic polynomials of matrices and endomorphisms, the normal forms they lead to (diagonalization, triangularization, Jordan and Smith normal forms), and eigenvalue algorithms (power iteration and the Rayleigh quotient).
LinearAlgebra.title: Matrix decompositions and linear systems
LinearAlgebra.description: Factorizations of matrices (QR, singular value, polar, Schur and LU decompositions), Gaussian elimination and the solvability of linear systems, linear least squares, Krylov subspace methods (Arnoldi, Lanczos, GMRES, conjugate gradients) and condition numbers.
LinearAlgebra.title: Determinants and matrix identities
LinearAlgebra.description: Determinant expansions and identities, determinants of special products and exponentials, derivatives of determinants, and algebraic identities between matrices.
LinearAlgebra.title: Positive definite matrices and matrix inequalities
LinearAlgebra.description: Positive definite and semidefinite matrices, criteria for definiteness, and inequalities for their determinants, traces and eigenvalues.
LinearAlgebra.title: Bilinear and quadratic forms
LinearAlgebra.description: Bilinear and quadratic forms on vector spaces and modules: rank, orthogonal sums, inertia and congruence, and lattices with their duals and neighbours.
LinearAlgebra.title: Tensor products and multilinear algebra
LinearAlgebra.description: Multilinear and alternating maps, tensor products of modules and of families of modules, tensor, symmetric and exterior powers and algebras, and Clifford algebras with their spin groups. Bilinear and quadratic forms have their own field.
LinearAlgebra.title: Root systems
LinearAlgebra.description: Root systems and root data in paired modules: reflections, root strings, simple roots and bases, Cartan matrices and their realizations, invariant bilinear forms and Weyl groups. Lie algebras constructed from root systems are under Algebra.
LinearAlgebra.title: Special matrices
LinearAlgebra.description: Classes of matrices defined by their structure or entries: Toeplitz, Hankel and circulant matrices, Hadamard and sign matrices, combinatorial matrices, nonnegative, row-stochastic, doubly stochastic and totally positive matrices.

Logic.title: Logic
Logic.description: Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.
Logic.title: Type-theoretic foundations
Logic.description: Propositional reasoning and constructions of dependent type theory: empty and inhabited types, unique existence, subtypes, quotients, universes and inductive and coinductive types. Formal propositional and first-order systems as objects of study have their own fields.
Logic.title: Propositional logic and satisfiability
Logic.description: Classical propositional logic: truth-table semantics, natural deduction and its completeness, functional completeness, normal forms and CNF transformations, resolution, interpolation, SAT-solving procedures (Davis–Putnam, DPLL, 2-SAT, Horn-SAT) and binary decision diagrams.
Logic.title: First-order logic
Logic.description: Syntax, proof calculi and semantics of first-order predicate logic, including soundness and Gödel's completeness theorem.
Logic.title: Proof theory
Logic.description: Structural study of formal proofs and provability: sequent calculi, linear logic and translations into it, and Gödel's incompleteness theorems.
Logic.title: Modal logic
Logic.description: Logics of necessity and possibility interpreted on Kripke models, their axiomatizations, completeness and decidability, and extensions such as epistemic logic, dynamic logic and the modal μ-calculus.
Logic.title: Temporal logic and model checking
Logic.description: Linear and branching-time temporal logics interpreted over infinite words and transition systems, with automata-theoretic and fixed-point model-checking procedures.
Logic.title: Model theory
Logic.description: Relations between formal theories and their structures: first-order languages of algebraic structures, quantifier elimination, categoricity and o-minimality.

MeasureTheory.title: Measure Theory
MeasureTheory.description: Measure theory provides the language of size and integration underlying probability and modern analysis.
MeasureTheory.title: Measurable spaces and measurable functions
MeasureTheory.description: σ-algebras and their generation, measurable maps and isomorphisms, product and countably generated σ-algebras, and Borel structures on topological and Polish spaces. Measures and their extensions are in Measures and measurable sets.
MeasureTheory.title: Measures and measurable sets
MeasureTheory.description: Construction and uniqueness of measures, atomless and vector measures, measures on Boolean algebras, and the limits of measurability shown by non-measurable sets and paradoxical decompositions.
MeasureTheory.title: Absolute continuity, densities and decompositions
MeasureTheory.description: Absolute continuity and singularity for pairs of positive measures, densities, the unsigned Hahn decomposition, Lebesgue decomposition and the Radon–Nikodym theorem. Signed and vector-valued analogues belong to Signed and vector measures.
MeasureTheory.title: Signed and vector measures
MeasureTheory.description: Signed, complex and vector-valued measures: construction, Hahn and Jordan decomposition, variation, Stieltjes vector measures and integration. Lyapunov’s range convexity theorem remains in Measures and measurable sets.
MeasureTheory.title: Lebesgue measure
MeasureTheory.description: Lebesgue measure on the real line and Euclidean space: volumes of concrete bodies, null sets and density phenomena.
MeasureTheory.title: Covering theorems and differentiation of measures
MeasureTheory.description: Vitali and Besicovitch covering theorems, Vitali families, differentiation of one measure with respect to another, doubling measures and Lebesgue's density and differentiation theorems; differentiation of real functions of bounded variation is in Differentiation of real functions.
MeasureTheory.title: Haar measure and fundamental domains
MeasureTheory.description: Invariant measures on locally compact groups, unimodularity, and fundamental domains for the actions of discrete subgroups.
MeasureTheory.title: Integration and convergence
MeasureTheory.description: The Lebesgue integral and its convergence theorems, modes of convergence of measurable functions, approximation by simple functions, product measures, convolution, differentiation under the integral sign and integral inequalities.
MeasureTheory.title: Lebesgue spaces
MeasureTheory.description: The spaces Lp of p-th power integrable functions: membership criteria, inclusions, dense subspaces, the essential supremum and weak convergence.
MeasureTheory.title: Differentiation of real functions
MeasureTheory.description: Absolutely continuous, Lipschitz and bounded-variation functions of a real variable, maximal functions and almost-everywhere properties of real functions.
MeasureTheory.title: Optimal transport
MeasureTheory.description: Couplings of probability measures, transport costs, existence of optimal couplings, Kantorovich duality, Wasserstein distances and Brenier's theorem, displacement convexity and Wasserstein gradient flows (the JKO scheme).
MeasureTheory.title: Geometric measure theory
MeasureTheory.description: Hausdorff measures and dimension, dimension functions and codimension, fractal sets such as attractors of iterated function systems, and the measure and dimension of distance sets.

NumberTheory.title: Number Theory
NumberTheory.description: Number theory studies integers, primes, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and their analytic and algebraic structure.
NumberTheory.title: Congruences and power residues
NumberTheory.description: Modular arithmetic: Wilson, Wolstenholme and Fermat-quotient congruences, lifting the exponent, primitive roots, Legendre/Jacobi symbols, reciprocity, covering systems.
NumberTheory.title: Congruences and modular arithmetic
NumberTheory.description: Congruences for factorials, quotients and power sums (Wilson, Wolstenholme, Fermat quotients), lifting the exponent, multiplicative order, primitive roots, residue systems.
NumberTheory.title: Power residues and reciprocity
NumberTheory.description: Quadratic and cubic residues, Legendre, Jacobi and Kronecker symbols, quadratic reciprocity and its extensions, Legendre-symbol sums.
NumberTheory.title: Covering systems
NumberTheory.description: Covering and exact covering systems of residue classes, minimum moduli, Erdős–Graham and Fraenkel-type results.
NumberTheory.title: Primes, divisibility and factorization
NumberTheory.description: Divisibility, factorization and individual primes: divisors, greatest common divisors, Bézout's identity, coprimality and prime factorization; special prime families, primality criteria, pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers, Fermat and Mersenne numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Divisibility and factorization of integers
NumberTheory.description: Elementary arithmetic of the natural numbers and integers: divisibility, divisors and divisor sets, greatest common divisors and least common multiples, Bézout's identity and the Euclidean algorithm, coprimality, prime factorization and multiplicities of prime factors; primality tests and special primes are in the neighbouring subfields, congruences in Congruences and power residues.
NumberTheory.title: Primality tests and pseudoprimes
NumberTheory.description: Primality criteria (Proth, Pocklington, Lucas–Lehmer), Fermat, Lucas, Frobenius and strong pseudoprimes, Carmichael and Korselt numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Special classes of primes
NumberTheory.description: Fermat, Mersenne, Sophie Germain, Wieferich, Cullen and other named prime families, Fermat numbers, Sierpiński–Riesel numbers, prime-producing formulas.
NumberTheory.title: Distribution of primes
NumberTheory.description: Counting primes: prime number theorem, explicit Chebyshev-type bounds, prime gaps and short intervals, primes in progressions, sieves, prime patterns.
NumberTheory.title: Prime number theorem and explicit bounds
NumberTheory.description: PNT and its proofs, Chebyshev theta and psi, explicit bounds for π(x) and the nth prime (Dusart, Axler, Rosser), Mertens constants.
NumberTheory.title: Prime gaps and primes in short intervals
NumberTheory.description: Bertrand-type and Breusch theorems, Ramanujan primes, prime gaps, bounded gaps, Sylvester–Schur on prime factors of consecutive products.
NumberTheory.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions
NumberTheory.description: Dirichlet density, PNT for progressions, Siegel–Walfisz, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Brun–Titchmarsh, prime races.
NumberTheory.title: Sieve methods
NumberTheory.description: Selberg, Brun and large sieves, almost primes, parity problem, counting integers with restricted prime factors via sieves.
NumberTheory.title: Prime patterns and conjectures
NumberTheory.description: Twin primes and Brun's constant, Hardy–Littlewood tuples, Goldbach/Lemoine-type statements, primes represented by polynomials (Friedlander–Iwaniec).
NumberTheory.title: Arithmetic functions
NumberTheory.description: Divisor sums, totients, Möbius and multiplicative functions, their mean values and extremal orders, and integers classified by them.
NumberTheory.title: Perfect numbers and their relatives
NumberTheory.description: Perfect, multiperfect, odd perfect, abundant, practical, Zumkeller, Giuga, amicable numbers, spoof factorizations, Lehmer's totient problem.
NumberTheory.title: Divisor and totient functions
NumberTheory.description: σ, τ, φ, Jordan and Dedekind ψ, unitary and biunitary divisors, gcd-sums, Ramanujan sums, totient multiplicities and values.
NumberTheory.title: Multiplicative functions and mean values
NumberTheory.description: Dirichlet and unitary convolution, completely multiplicative and additive functions, Wintner and Euler-product mean values, additive uniqueness sets, Mertens bounds.
NumberTheory.title: Integers with restricted factorization
NumberTheory.description: Squarefree, k-free, k-full and powerful, smooth and rough numbers, highly composite numbers, integers with prescribed prime factors.
NumberTheory.title: Zeta and L-functions
NumberTheory.description: Riemann zeta and xi, Dirichlet characters and L-functions, Dedekind and Artin L-functions, Riemann hypothesis criteria, multiple zeta values.
NumberTheory.title: Riemann zeta function
NumberTheory.description: Continuation and zeros of ζ, zero-free regions, moments and subconvexity, RH criteria (Robin, Lagarias), de Bruijn–Newman constant, zeta values.
NumberTheory.title: Dirichlet characters and L-functions
NumberTheory.description: Dirichlet characters, conductors, primitive and quadratic characters, Dirichlet series continuation, L-function bounds, Artin and Selberg-class functions.
NumberTheory.title: Multiple zeta values
NumberTheory.description: Multiple zeta and zeta-star values, Hoffman bases, word algebras, cyclic sum formulas, finite and q-analogue multiple zeta values.
NumberTheory.title: Exponential and character sums
NumberTheory.description: Gauss sums, Weyl and Vinogradov sums, incomplete exponential sums, Burgess bounds, Dirichlet polynomials, trigonometric and cotangent sums.
NumberTheory.title: Diophantine equations
NumberTheory.description: Integer and rational solutions of polynomial and exponential equations, Pell equations, Thue equations, Diophantine tuples, Egyptian fractions.
NumberTheory.title: Exponential Diophantine equations
NumberTheory.description: Equations with unknown exponents: Pillai, Catalan, Størmer, Nagell–Ljunggren, Ramanujan–Nagell and Terai-type equations, powers plus one.
NumberTheory.title: Pell and quadratic Diophantine equations
NumberTheory.description: Pell and negative Pell equations, norm equations, Pythagorean triples, Markov triples and quadratic equations in two or three variables.
NumberTheory.title: Higher-degree Diophantine equations
NumberTheory.description: Thue equations, generalized Fermat equations, sums of cubes, x^y = y^x, abc conjecture, Brocard–Ramanujan and symmetric-function equations.
NumberTheory.title: Diophantine tuples and Egyptian fractions
NumberTheory.description: Diophantine m-tuples, Erdős–Straus problem, Egyptian fraction representations and greedy unit-fraction algorithms.
NumberTheory.title: Quadratic forms and sums of squares
NumberTheory.description: Representations by quadratic forms: sums of two, three and four squares, binary forms and class numbers, universality theorems, Waring's problem.
NumberTheory.title: Sums of squares and representation numbers
NumberTheory.description: Two-, three- and four-square theorems, Jacobi-type counts, Gaussian and Hurwitz integer methods, x²+2y² and similar representations.
NumberTheory.title: Binary and higher quadratic forms
NumberTheory.description: Reduction theory, discriminants and class numbers of binary forms, quaternary forms, 15 and 290 theorems.
NumberTheory.title: Waring's problem and figurate numbers
NumberTheory.description: Hilbert–Waring, g(3)=9, Fermat polygonal theorem, polygonal, triangular and polytopic numbers and their sums.
NumberTheory.title: Diophantine approximation and transcendence
NumberTheory.description: Approximating reals by rationals or algebraics, Roth and subspace theorems, linear forms in logarithms, transcendence, uniform distribution, geometry of numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Transcendence and irrationality
NumberTheory.description: Hermite–Lindemann, Lindemann–Weierstrass, Gelfond–Schneider, Mahler functions, irrationality and linear independence of constants.
NumberTheory.title: Roth's theorem and linear forms in logarithms
NumberTheory.description: Thue–Siegel–Roth, Ridout, Schmidt subspace, Baker, Baker–Wüstholz, Matveev bounds, Baker–Davenport reduction, approximation by algebraic numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Uniform distribution and metric approximation
NumberTheory.description: Weyl equidistribution, three-gap theorem, Duffin–Schaeffer, normal numbers, Beatty sequences, discrepancy, lattice points and Minkowski-type theorems.
NumberTheory.title: Continued fractions and expansions of reals
NumberTheory.description: Continued fractions, Farey sequences, Stern–Brocot tree, Engel, Pierce, Lüroth and similar series expansions of real numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Heights and Mahler measure
NumberTheory.description: Absolute heights of algebraic numbers, Mahler measure, Lehmer's problem, Dobrowolski bounds, Schinzel–Zassenhaus, house and trace problems.
NumberTheory.title: Algebraic number theory
NumberTheory.description: Number fields and rings of integers: quadratic and cyclotomic fields, discriminants, ramification, ideals, adeles and ideles, class field theory, Galois cohomology and p-adic representations.
NumberTheory.title: Number fields and embeddings
NumberTheory.description: Number fields, their rings of integers, embeddings and signatures, CM fields, Minkowski geometry and class-number finiteness. Units, regulators, ideals and ramification belong to Discriminants, ramification and ideals; the theory of places belongs to Adeles, ideles and class field theory.
NumberTheory.title: Quadratic fields and integer rings
NumberTheory.description: Gaussian, Eisenstein and ℤ[√d] integers, prime factorization there, imaginary quadratic discriminants, class numbers, Stark–Heegner.
NumberTheory.title: Cyclotomic fields
NumberTheory.description: Cyclotomic fields and polynomials, real cyclotomic polynomials, 2cos(2πk/n), cyclotomic units, ramification and inertness in cyclotomic fields.
NumberTheory.title: Discriminants, ramification and ideals
NumberTheory.description: Discriminants and their bounds, ramification and inertia, orders, units, ideal counting, local degrees under completion, field enumeration and towers.
NumberTheory.title: Adeles, ideles and class field theory
NumberTheory.description: Places, adeles and ideles, ray class groups, Artin map, Hilbert class fields, Neukirch–Uchida-type Galois characterization.
NumberTheory.title: Galois representations and p-adic Hodge theory
NumberTheory.description: ℓ-adic and p-adic representations of the Galois groups of local and global fields and their Galois cohomology: Galois cohomology of local and global fields (local Tate duality, Euler characteristic formulas, the Poitou–Tate sequence, Selmer and Bloch–Kato groups), Weil–Deligne representations and the ℓ-adic monodromy theorem, Fontaine's period rings with crystalline, semistable, de Rham and Hodge–Tate representations and (φ, Γ)-modules, p-adic comparison theorems for varieties and p-divisible groups, and prismatic cohomology. Class field theory is under Adeles, ideles and class field theory, cohomology of abstract groups under group cohomology, ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes under Grothendieck topologies on schemes, and Galois representations of elliptic curves under elliptic curves.
NumberTheory.title: p-adic numbers and local fields
NumberTheory.description: p-adic integers and expansions, valuations of integer sequences, Hensel lifting, Strassmann's theorem, Hilbert symbols, p-adic gamma, local fields.
NumberTheory.title: Modular forms, q-series and partitions
NumberTheory.description: Modular forms and functions, congruence subgroups, Ramanujan tau, theta functions, mock theta functions, Lambert series, partition congruences.
NumberTheory.title: Modular forms
NumberTheory.description: Modular and cusp forms, congruence subgroups, cusps, Eisenstein series congruences, Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture, spectral gaps.
NumberTheory.title: Theta functions and q-series
NumberTheory.description: Jacobi and Ramanujan theta functions, q-Pochhammer symbols and Euler products, Rogers–Ramanujan and related continued fractions, mock theta functions, Lambert series and q-series identities.
NumberTheory.title: Partition congruences
NumberTheory.description: Ramanujan-type congruences, dissections and densities for partition functions and their variants (overpartitions, regular, cubic, core, colored, mex, designated-summand and smallest-part partitions), proved with q-series and eta quotients.
NumberTheory.title: Linear recurrence sequences
NumberTheory.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Pell, Tribonacci and other linear recurrences: identities, divisibility, periods, primitive divisors and Diophantine properties.
NumberTheory.title: Fibonacci and Lucas numbers
NumberTheory.description: Identities, sums, reciprocal series, determinants and generating functions specifically for Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.
NumberTheory.title: Lucas sequences and primitive divisors
NumberTheory.description: General Lucas sequences U_n, V_n, Lucas pairs, divisibility, Bang–Zsigmondy and primitive-divisor theorems, Fibonacci prime divisibility.
NumberTheory.title: Pell, Jacobsthal and other second-order sequences
NumberTheory.description: Pell, Pell–Lucas, Jacobsthal, gibonacci, Horadam, Leonardo, Oresme, bi-periodic and (a,b)-Fibonacci sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Tribonacci and higher-order sequences
NumberTheory.description: Tribonacci, tetranacci, pentanacci, k-generalized Fibonacci, Padovan, Perrin and Narayana sequences, dominant roots and Binet forms.
NumberTheory.title: Fibonacci and Lucas polynomials
NumberTheory.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Jacobsthal and gibonacci polynomials, their sums, squares and generating function values.
NumberTheory.title: General theory of recurrences
NumberTheory.description: C-finite, P-recursive and MC-finite sequences, Binet formulas, Skolem–Mahler–Lech, growth, generating functions and decomposable forms.
NumberTheory.title: Recurrences modulo m
NumberTheory.description: Pisano periods, periods and zero indices of recurrences modulo primes and prime powers, residue distribution.
NumberTheory.title: Diophantine problems in recurrences
NumberTheory.description: Squares, perfect powers, repdigits, factorials and powers of two among terms of recurrence sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Special numbers and polynomials
NumberTheory.description: Arithmetic of classical number families: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers, harmonic numbers, binomial and Catalan-type coefficients.
NumberTheory.title: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
NumberTheory.description: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, identities, denominators, Kummer congruences, Faulhaber sums, Appell sequences, higher-order and Apostol variants.
NumberTheory.title: Euler, Genocchi and poly-Bernoulli numbers
NumberTheory.description: Euler numbers and polynomials, Genocchi numbers, poly-Bernoulli, Bernoulli of the second kind, degenerate variants.
NumberTheory.title: Harmonic numbers and harmonic sums
NumberTheory.description: Harmonic, hyperharmonic and multiple harmonic sums, binomial-harmonic identities, non-integrality, harmonic congruences, Euler–Mascheroni bounds.
NumberTheory.title: Binomial coefficients and factorials
NumberTheory.description: Divisibility and valuations of binomial coefficients, Lucas-type theorems, factorial ratios and Fibonomial coefficients; b-nomial, totienomial and other generalized binomial coefficients go to Combinatorics.
NumberTheory.title: Catalan and Fuss–Catalan numbers
NumberTheory.description: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Lucasnomial and FiboCatalan numbers: integrality and prime divisibility.
NumberTheory.title: Digits and numeration systems
NumberTheory.description: Base-b digits of integers, repdigits and palindromes, Kaprekar and happy numbers, Zeckendorf and base-φ systems, automatic sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Digit properties of integers
NumberTheory.description: Digit sums and products, Niven, happy, Kaprekar, Keith numbers, comma sequences, decimal expansions of fractions (Midy, repetends).
NumberTheory.title: Repdigits, palindromes and reverse multiples
NumberTheory.description: Repdigits, palindromes, reverse multiples and Young graphs, permutiples, digit reversal, special squares by digits.
NumberTheory.title: Numeration systems and automatic sequences
NumberTheory.description: Zeckendorf, base-φ, negative and signed bases, Cobham's theorem, base-recognizable sets, Mahler substitution, regular sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Integer sequences
NumberTheory.description: Named nonlinear integer sequences: Collatz and iterated maps, self-referential sequences, Sylvester and Euclid sequences, realizable and Dold sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Iterated maps and self-referential sequences
NumberTheory.description: Collatz problem, EKG, Stern diatomic, Hofstadter, Golomb, Ulam, Ducci, Josephus and Conway-type sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Arithmetic properties of sequences
NumberTheory.description: Dold, Newton and realizable sequences, Sylvester, Euclid and Göbel sequences, gcd and divisibility sequences, OEIS-specific sequences.
NumberTheory.title: Additive number theory
NumberTheory.description: Representing integers as sums from special sets, and the density of integer sets: sumsets of integers, subset sums and complete sequences, primitive sets, natural and logarithmic density, Romanoff's theorem; additive bases and complements and zero-sum constants go to additive combinatorics.
NumberTheory.title: Numerical semigroups and the Frobenius problem
NumberTheory.description: Sylvester's coin theorem, Frobenius numbers, pseudo-Frobenius sets and numerical semigroups generated by special sequences.
Rational points of varieties over number fields: torsion and rank of elliptic curves, naive heights, Hasse principle, local-global failures.
NumberTheory.title: Arithmetic of function fields
NumberTheory.description: Number-theoretic analogues over F_q[T] and finite fields: polynomial primes, h-free polynomials, function-field adeles, positive-characteristic zeta values.

Order.title: Order Theory
Order.description: Order theory studies comparison relations, lattices, intervals, monotonicity, and order-complete constructions.
Order.title: Ordered sets
Order.description: Partial, strict and total orders, dense linear orders, monotone maps and sequences, and representations of finite posets.
Order.title: Well-founded orders and order types
Order.description: Well-founded relations and well-orders, well-founded and partially well-ordered sets, well-quasi-orders, initial and principal segments, order types and their arithmetic, and transfinite constructions along well-orders. Ordinals and cardinals are under Set Theory.
Order.title: Intervals, covers and graded orders
Order.description: Intervals and order-connected sets, locally finite orders, the covering relation, successor and predecessor orders, chains and relation series, graded orders, and the height and Krull dimension of partially ordered sets.
Order.title: Lattices and Boolean algebras
Order.description: Lattices and Boolean algebras, their representation theorems, and Boolean functions viewed as maps between Boolean lattices.
Order.title: Filters and ultrafilters
Order.description: Filters on a set as an order-theoretic structure: the lattice of filters, filter bases, images and products of filters, eventual properties and limits along filters (including limits at infinity and limits superior and inferior), germs, ultrafilters and ultraproducts. Convergence in topological spaces is under Topology; order ideals and filters of a lattice are under lattices.
Order.title: Fixed points and domain theory
Order.description: Least and greatest fixed points of monotone and Scott-continuous maps, Kleene iteration, and the complete partial orders that underlie denotational semantics.

Probability.title: Probability
Probability.description: Probability studies random phenomena through distributions, expectation, independence, concentration, and stochastic processes.
Probability.title: Foundations of probability
Probability.description: Probability measures and laws of random variables, expected value and the change of variables formula, construction of probability measures and processes (Kolmogorov extension, measures from Stieltjes functions), independence and the Borel–Cantelli lemmas, conditional expectation and regular conditional distributions, exchangeability and de Finetti's theorem, and zero–one laws for sequences (Kolmogorov, Hewitt–Savage); zero–one laws for continuous processes go to Brownian motion and stochastic calculus, tail sigma-algebras of random walks to Random walks.
Probability.title: Markov kernels and disintegration
Probability.description: Measurable families of measures, their composition, products, integration, densities, disintegration and the Ionescu–Tulcea theorem. Regular conditional distributions are in Foundations of probability; Markov chains as processes have their own field.
Probability.title: Expectation, variance and moments
Probability.description: Means, variances and covariances, among them the variance of a sum and Chebyshev's inequality, central moments, conditional variance, covariance forms and operators, and moment- and cumulant-generating functions; the definition of the expected value and the change of variables formula are in Foundations of probability. Characteristic functions and probability-generating functions have their own field, as do the other concentration inequalities.
Probability.title: Stochastic processes and stopping times
Probability.description: General processes indexed by time: filtrations, adapted, progressively measurable and predictable processes, stopping times, stopped processes and hitting times, indistinguishable processes and modifications, finite-dimensional distributions and localization of process properties; martingales and Brownian motion have their own fields.
Probability.title: Probability distributions
Probability.description: Named discrete and continuous laws and their moments, densities, mass functions and tails, together with distribution functions, quantiles, medians and joint laws; sampling laws used in tests (t, F) go to Linear models and multivariate analysis.
Probability.title: Discrete distributions
Probability.description: Laws on countable sets, with their mass functions, moments and tails: discrete uniform, binomial, Poisson, Poisson binomial, hypergeometric, multinomial, negative binomial and beta-binomial laws, and expectation under a probability mass function.
Probability.title: Continuous distributions
Probability.description: Laws with densities, with their moments and tails: beta, gamma, exponential, Laplace, chi-square, log-normal, Weibull and Dirichlet laws, the multivariate normal law with Gaussian conditioning, orthant probabilities and L² limits, and the Poisson–Gamma duality.
Probability.title: Distribution functions and quantiles
Probability.description: Cumulative distribution functions and their continuity points, quantile functions and inverse transform sampling, medians, and joint laws.
Probability.title: Characteristic functions and generating functions
Probability.description: Characteristic functions, probability generating functions and positive-definite functions (Bochner), Taylor bounds for characteristic functions, lattice support, Lévy's continuity theorem and Cramér's decomposition theorem for the normal law.
Probability.title: Infinitely divisible laws and regular variation
Probability.description: Infinitely divisible and stable distributions, convolution powers, the Lévy–Khintchin representation, and regularly varying and slowly varying functions (Karamata's theorem, Potter bounds, generalized inverses) with the truncated moments and tail integrals of heavy-tailed laws.
Probability.title: Convergence of probability measures
Probability.description: Weak convergence and convergence in probability, tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, Helly selection, Skorokhod representation, the continuous mapping theorem, the Cramér–Wold device and total variation distance; specific limit laws go to the limit-theorem fields.
Probability.title: Laws of large numbers and random series
Probability.description: Almost-sure behaviour of sums of independent variables: strong and weak laws of large numbers, Kolmogorov's three-series theorem and maximal inequality, truncation techniques, the law of the iterated logarithm, and the Monte Carlo variance rate of sample means.
Probability.title: Central limit theorems and Poisson approximation
Probability.description: Convergence in law of normalized sums and their error terms: central limit theorems (Lindeberg–Feller, lacunary and infinite-variance variants), Berry–Esseen bounds and constants, global and local de Moivre–Laplace theorems, Edgeworth expansions, Donsker's invariance principle, and Poisson limit theorems for binomial and urn models.
Probability.title: Concentration inequalities
Probability.description: Non-asymptotic tail and moment bounds: Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Efron–Stein, Khintchine and Paley–Zygmund inequalities, sampling without replacement, sub-exponential variables and Bernstein's inequality, chi-square and Gaussian Lipschitz concentration, sub-Gaussian convex comparison, Talagrand's convex distance and concentration inequality, and hypercontractivity (Bonami–Beckner, p-biased two-point inequalities) on the discrete cube.
Probability.title: Large deviations
Probability.description: Large deviation principles and rate functions, Cramér's theorem and Chernoff bounds for empirical means, log-moment generating functions and the Legendre–Fenchel transform used to build them, principles at other speeds, and the Ben Arous–Guionnet principle for the empirical spectral measure of Gaussian ensembles.
Probability.title: Martingales and optional stopping
Probability.description: Discrete-time martingales, sub- and supermartingales: convergence theorems (almost sure, L^p, backwards, Lévy's downward theorem), uniform integrability, Doob's maximal inequalities, orthogonality and conditional variance of increments, optional stopping in all its forms, and Wald's equations for stopped sums. Finite-horizon optimal stopping by the Snell envelope, and the secretary problem. Martingale measures and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing.
Probability.title: Random walks
Probability.description: Sums of i.i.d. steps as processes: the drift/oscillation dichotomy, limsup and liminf of partial sums, tail measurability of asymptotic events, the strong Markov property of i.i.d. sequences at stopping times, and ballot theorems.
Probability.title: Markov chains
Probability.description: Discrete-time Markov chains (construction, path measures, finite-dimensional distributions, Chapman–Kolmogorov, Markov and strong Markov properties), finite chains, ergodicity and convergence to stationarity, mixing, reversibility and Kolmogorov's cycle criterion, finite continuous-time Markov chains with rate matrices, semigroups and hitting times, and Dirichlet forms of symmetric Markov processes.
Probability.title: Branching processes
Probability.description: Galton–Watson processes, extinction probabilities, total progeny and the hitting-time theorem, and linear birth–death processes.
Probability.title: Brownian motion and stochastic calculus
Probability.description: Continuous-time processes with continuous paths or independent increments: the construction and sample-path properties of Brownian motion, Kolmogorov's continuity theorem, Blumenthal-type zero–one laws, the simple and strong Markov properties and the reflection principle, quadratic variation, the Itô integral and Itô's formula, Lévy's characterisation and Girsanov's theorem, stochastic differential equations, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and Fokker–Planck equations for diffusions.
Probability.title: Point processes and stationary processes
Probability.description: Poisson processes on the line and Poisson point processes on general spaces (arrival times, counts, restriction theorem), and stationary random functions.
Probability.title: Random fields on lattices
Probability.description: Spin and bond configuration spaces, Bernoulli product measures and cylinder events, Gibbs-type conditional distributions given the outside of a region, translation invariance and ergodicity, weak and monotone limits of measures on configuration space, and marginals and conditional independence for weights on finite configuration spaces.
Probability.title: Percolation
Probability.description: Bernoulli bond and site percolation: percolation probability, critical points, number and uniqueness of infinite clusters, sharpness and sharp thresholds, and crossing estimates in two dimensions.
Probability.title: Phase transition and critical probability
Probability.description: The percolation probability theta, bounds 0 < p_c < 1 (Peierls and enclosure arguments), percolation on product graphs, the number and uniqueness of infinite clusters (Burton–Keane), and sharp thresholds from influences (KKL).
Probability.title: Sharpness of the phase transition
Probability.description: The Duminil-Copin–Tassion proof of exponential decay below p_c: the quantity phi_p(S), Russo's formula and pivotal edges, exploration and last-exit decompositions, the differential inequality, the mean-field bound and subcritical decay.
Probability.title: Crossing probabilities in two dimensions
Probability.description: Crossings of rectangles and annuli in bond percolation on Z^2, the box-crossing property, gluing and square-root tricks, Russo–Seymour–Welsh theory and planar separation lemmas.
Probability.title: Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination
Probability.description: Inequalities comparing probabilities of monotone or disjointly occurring events under product measures, and stochastic orderings and monotone couplings of measures.
Probability.title: Harris, FKG and BK inequalities
Probability.description: Increasing events, the Harris and FKG inequalities, Holley's inequality, disjoint occurrence and the van den Berg–Kesten inequality (finite, countable and inhomogeneous), pivotal coordinates and Russo's formula on product spaces.
Probability.title: Reimer's inequality
Probability.description: Reimer's inequality for arbitrary events and its proof machinery: configurations as finsets, down-compression, doubled ground sets, disjoint-pair counts and weighted pair sums, and special and mixed-monotone cases.
Probability.title: High-dimensional and geometric probability
Probability.description: Probability in high dimension and on geometric objects: log-concave and uniform convex-body laws, isotropic constants, the KLS and thin-shell conjectures and their bounds, random matrices (singularity of Bernoulli matrices, Tracy–Widom limits, singular values of Gaussian matrices, Wigner's semicircle law), free probability (free independence, free cumulants, the R-transform and the free central limit theorem), random Euclidean optimization (Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley), suprema of selector and positive empirical processes (Park–Pham theorems), and uniform laws of large numbers via Rademacher complexity.
Probability.title: Statistical estimation
Probability.description: Point estimation theory and confidence sets: bias, risk and mean squared error, likelihood and maximum likelihood (consistency and asymptotic normality), Fisher information and Cramér–Rao, sufficiency, factorization (Fisher–Neyman, Halmos–Savage) and Rao–Blackwell, Stein's lemma and James–Stein shrinkage, contiguity and Le Cam's lemmas, asymptotic efficiency (Hájek's convolution theorem and adaptive estimation), and the bootstrap with the Mallows metric. The local asymptotic normality of the log-likelihood ratio is under [local power of the likelihood-ratio test](../hypothesis-testing/local-power-of-the-likelihood-ratio-test/README.md) in Hypothesis testing. Penalized least squares (ridge regression, and the lasso with its soft-thresholding solution for an orthonormal design) is under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md) in Machine learning.
Probability.title: Hypothesis testing
Probability.description: Tests and their validity and power: Neyman–Pearson, likelihood-ratio, score and Wald tests, monotone likelihood ratio, exact conditional tests (Fisher, Hardy–Weinberg), rank tests and ROC area (Mann–Whitney), permutation p-values, sequential tests (Wald's sequential probability ratio test) and quickest change detection (Shiryaev's rule and CUSUM), multiple testing (familywise error control by Bonferroni, Holm and closed testing; false discovery rate control by Benjamini–Hochberg; and the two-groups model with local and tail-area false discovery rates, Storey's positive false discovery rate and q-values), and meta-analysis and heterogeneity statistics.
Probability.title: Linear models and multivariate analysis
Probability.description: Multivariate normal theory and linear models: Gaussian maximum likelihood, Cochran's theorem on quadratic forms, t and F sampling laws, Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares, principal component analysis, regularized covariance estimation by banding, Gaussian graphical models, and sparse high-dimensional regression: exact recovery by basis pursuit under the restricted nullspace property, and ℓ₂- and prediction-error bounds for the Lasso under restricted eigenvalue conditions. Ridge regression and the lasso as penalized least squares are under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md), and probabilistic principal component analysis, with the factor-analysis marginal, under [probabilistic principal component analysis](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/unsupervised-learning/probabilistic-principal-component-analysis/README.md), both in Machine learning.
Probability.title: Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis
Probability.description: Distribution-free and semiparametric methods: empirical distribution functions (Glivenko–Cantelli), U-statistics, the Kaplan–Meier estimator, Cox partial likelihood and the log-rank test, and design-based causal inference with potential outcomes. Park and Pham's theorem on when the supremum of a positive empirical process over a finite family of nonnegative functions is large compared with its expectation is under [suprema of selector and empirical processes](../high-dimensional-probability/suprema-of-selector-and-empirical-processes/README.md) in High-dimensional and geometric probability.
Probability.title: Bayesian statistics
Probability.description: Bayesian inference and nonparametric priors: the Dirichlet process and stick-breaking, Pólya and Blackwell–MacQueen urns, Ferguson conjugacy, infinite limits of finite mixture and feature models (the Chinese restaurant and Indian buffet processes), and posterior computations. Parametric conjugate models, Bayesian linear regression, expectation–maximization, mean-field variational inference, and Monte Carlo and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling are under [Bayesian inference and sampling](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/bayesian-inference-and-sampling/README.md) in Machine learning. The two-groups model for large-scale testing, in which the local false discovery rate is the posterior probability of the null, is under [Hypothesis testing](../hypothesis-testing/two-groups-model-and-local-false-discovery-rates/README.md).
Probability.title: Queueing theory
Probability.description: Sample-path relations between arrivals, sojourn times and occupancy, and normalized balance laws for queueing rate models.

QuantumInformation.title: Quantum Information
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum information studies states, channels, measurement, entanglement, communication, and quantum computation.
QuantumInformation.title: Quantum foundations
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum foundations studies what quantum mechanics rules out and allows at the level of measurement outcomes, including contextuality, Bell nonlocality and bounds on quantum correlations.
QuantumInformation.title: Quantum operations and channels
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum operations and channels covers the physically allowed transformations of quantum states, such as isometries and completely positive maps, and impossibility results like the no-cloning theorem.
QuantumInformation.title: Quantum error correction
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum error correction protects quantum information against noise by encoding it into a subspace of a larger system: quantum codes, the Knill–Laflamme conditions for correctability, and stabilizer and CSS codes.
QuantumInformation.title: Quantum Shannon theory
QuantumInformation.description: Information transmission and source coding for quantum states: accessible information, random-access codes, Holevo bounds and Schumacher compression. Quantum error-correcting codes have their own field.
QuantumInformation.title: Quantum states, distances and entropy
QuantumInformation.description: Density operators and their purifications, trace distance and fidelity, and continuity bounds for quantum entropy. Transformations of states and channel properties are under quantum operations and channels.

RepresentationTheory.title: Representation Theory
RepresentationTheory.description: Representation theory studies symmetry by realizing groups and algebras as transformations of linear spaces.
RepresentationTheory.title: Representations of groups and monoids
RepresentationTheory.description: Linear representations of monoids and groups over commutative rings: subrepresentations, intertwining maps, invariants and coinvariants, restriction, induction and coinduction, and the category of representations. Ordinary representation theory of finite groups and continuous representations have their own fields.
RepresentationTheory.title: Representations of finite groups
RepresentationTheory.description: Ordinary representation theory of finite groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero: characters, irreducibility, Schur's lemma, multiplicities and the Wedderburn decomposition of the group algebra.
RepresentationTheory.title: Group cohomology
RepresentationTheory.description: Homology, cohomology and Tate cohomology of groups with coefficients in modules, with their functoriality, additivity, periodicity and the Herbrand quotient.
RepresentationTheory.title: Representations of topological and Lie groups
RepresentationTheory.description: Representations of infinite groups and Lie algebras: continuous and unitary representations of compact and topological groups (Peter–Weyl theorem, complete reducibility), continuous representations over topological rings, representations of Lie algebras and of general linear groups (Schur–Weyl duality), and groups characterized by their irreducible representations.
RepresentationTheory.title: Reductive groups over local fields and their representations
RepresentationTheory.description: Reductive groups over archimedean and non-archimedean local fields and their representations: structure theory (parabolic subgroups and their Langlands decompositions, Cartan, Iwasawa and Bruhat decompositions, symmetric spaces of real groups, Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahoric subgroups and Moy–Prasad filtrations, dual and L-groups); smooth and admissible representations of p-adic groups (parabolic induction and Jacquet modules, cuspidal, square-integrable and tempered representations, the Bernstein–Zelevinsky and Zelevinsky classifications for GL(n), Iwahori-fixed vectors and depth); admissible representations, Harish-Chandra modules and smooth globalizations of real reductive groups such as U(p, q), with their discrete series; and the classical and p-adic local Langlands correspondences. Representations of compact and general topological groups and of Lie algebras, and Schur–Weyl duality, are under representations of topological and Lie groups; the Weil representation and the theta correspondence, local and global, are under automorphic forms and representations.
RepresentationTheory.title: Automorphic forms and representations
RepresentationTheory.description: Automorphic forms and automorphic representations of reductive groups over number fields and their adele rings: smooth adelic functions of moderate growth, constant terms and cusp forms, Whittaker models, the decomposition of automorphic representations into local components, multiplicity one, Eisenstein series, the spectral decomposition and trace formulas, Rankin–Selberg and doubling integrals and the L-functions they define, base change, the cohomology of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces with its Hecke action, and the Weil representation and the theta correspondence, local and global (Howe duality, the Siegel–Weil and Rallis inner product formulas). Classical modular forms, theta functions and q-series are under modular forms, q-series and partitions, adelic points of algebraic groups with their measures and class numbers under algebraic number theory, and the representations of the local groups have their own field.

RingTheory.title: Ring Theory
RingTheory.description: Ring theory studies addition and multiplication through ideals, modules, localization, dimension, and homological structure.
RingTheory.title: Commutative rings and ideals
RingTheory.description: Ideals of commutative rings and the operations on them: generation, sums, products, colons and quotients, prime and maximal ideals, radicals, nilpotent elements, coprimality and the Chinese remainder theorem, the Jacobson radical and Jacobson rings, and the prime and maximal spectra with the Zariski topology. Localization is under ideals, localization and ring constructions; fractional ideals are under Dedekind domains.
RingTheory.title: Factorization in integral domains
RingTheory.description: Unique factorization domains and monoids, principal ideal domains, Euclidean and Bézout domains, multiplicities and radicals of elements, contents of polynomials and Gauss's lemma, and criteria for factoriality and irreducibility over integral domains. Divisibility and GCD monoids as such are under algebra; factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains is under Dedekind domains.
RingTheory.title: Noetherian and Artinian rings
RingTheory.description: Rings and modules with chain conditions: Noetherian and Artinian rings and modules, the Hilbert basis theorem, the Hopkins–Levitzki theorem, associated primes and primary decomposition. Krull dimension and length of modules are under local rings.
RingTheory.title: Integral extensions and integral closure
RingTheory.description: Integral and algebraic elements over commutative rings, integral closure and integrally closed domains, primes lying over and the going-up and going-down theorems, and Noether normalization. Dedekind domains have their own field; algebraic field extensions are under field theory.
RingTheory.title: Dedekind domains and ideal theory
RingTheory.description: Dedekind domains and their characterizations, unique factorization of fractional ideals into primes, the ideal class group, invertible fractional ideals and the conductor of an order.
RingTheory.title: Ramification theory
RingTheory.description: How primes split, ramify and stay inert in finite extensions of Dedekind domains and discrete valuation rings, measured by the different, the discriminant, ramification indices, inertia degrees and Frobenius elements.
RingTheory.title: Valuation rings and Henselian rings
RingTheory.description: Discrete valuation rings and general valuation rings, their completions and finite extensions, residue fields, Hensel's lemma and the Krull–Akizuki theorem.
RingTheory.title: Local rings, dimension and completion
RingTheory.description: Local rings and their residue fields, Krull dimension, adic completion, regular local rings and length of modules.
RingTheory.title: Ideals, localization and ring constructions
RingTheory.description: Ideals and submodules under localization, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, Gröbner bases, toric ideals and Markov bases, zero divisors, products of rings and fields, and ring constructions such as Witt vectors.
RingTheory.title: Étale algebras, norms and differentials
RingTheory.description: Algebras over commutative rings: étale algebras and the trace form, norm and trace maps, Kähler differentials and derivations.
RingTheory.title: Syzygies and free resolutions
RingTheory.description: Free resolutions of modules over polynomial rings, Hilbert's syzygy theorem, and graded Betti numbers and Poincaré series of multigraded modules.
RingTheory.title: Formal power series
RingTheory.description: Rings of formal power series in one or several variables and Hahn series, with formal exponentials, derivatives, coefficient operators and Lagrange inversion.
RingTheory.title: Modules over commutative rings
RingTheory.description: Projective, free and finitely generated modules over commutative rings and module-finite extensions: Kaplansky's theorem, the Quillen–Suslin theorem, descent of Noetherianness (Eakin–Nagata) and the direct summand theorem.
RingTheory.title: Invariant theory
RingTheory.description: Rings of invariants of finite groups acting on commutative rings: finiteness of invariant rings and Hilbert–Poincaré series of modular invariant rings of polynomial algebras.
RingTheory.title: Cluster algebras
RingTheory.description: Cluster algebras of Fomin and Zelevinsky: exchange matrices and matrix mutation, seeds and seed mutation, the Laurent phenomenon, rank-two cluster algebras and their periodicity in finite type, Somos sequences, and the finite type classification by Cartan–Killing types. Total positivity of matrices is under Linear algebra.

SetTheory.title: Set Theory
SetTheory.description: Set theory studies membership, cardinality, ordinals, infinity, and foundational constructions for mathematics.
SetTheory.title: Sets, functions and relations
SetTheory.description: Sets and their operations, images and preimages, products, disjoint unions, quotients, functions, bijections, partial maps, relations and countability. Finite subsets and cardinal numbers have separate fields.
SetTheory.title: Finite sets and finite types
SetTheory.description: Finite subsets and finite types: cardinality, lattice operations, products, powersets, bounded natural numbers, finite tuples and symmetric powers. Lists and multisets have their own field; enumerative identities are under Combinatorics.
SetTheory.title: Lists and multisets
SetTheory.description: Finite sequences and collections with repetition: operations on lists, chains, permutations, multisets and multiplicities, fixed-length lists, association lists and finite maps. Sorting algorithms are under Computer Science.
SetTheory.title: Finitely supported functions
SetTheory.description: Functions and dependent families that vanish outside a finite set, their supports, singletons, algebraic operations, orders and descriptions by multiplicities. Free modules and polynomials are treated under Linear Algebra and Algebra.
SetTheory.title: Number systems
SetTheory.description: Construction, embeddings, arithmetic and order of the natural numbers, integers, rationals, real and complex numbers, and extensions by infinity. Divisibility, factorization and modular arithmetic are under Number Theory.
SetTheory.title: Ordinals and ordinal arithmetic
SetTheory.description: Ordinals as order types of well-orders, transfinite arithmetic, normal functions, fixed points, fundamental sequences and ordinal notation. Cardinal arithmetic and general well-founded orders have separate fields.
SetTheory.title: Cardinal arithmetic and cardinal characteristics
SetTheory.description: The arithmetic of infinite cardinals, including the continuum hypothesis and the singular cardinals hypothesis, together with cardinal invariants of the continuum and the cofinal structure of directed sets.
SetTheory.title: Axiomatic set theory and models of ZFC
SetTheory.description: Models of Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, sets and classes, transitive sets, von Neumann ordinals, rank and the cumulative hierarchy, and hereditarily finite sets with atoms. Forcing and large cardinals have their own fields.
SetTheory.title: Large cardinals
SetTheory.description: Cardinals with strong closure or reflection properties, such as inaccessible, Mahlo, weakly compact and measurable cardinals, whose existence cannot be proved in ZFC.
SetTheory.title: Infinitary combinatorics
SetTheory.description: Combinatorics of infinite and uncountable sets: clubs and stationary sets, partition relations, Δ-systems, almost disjoint families, combinatorial principles such as diamond and square, set-theoretic trees, Ramsey ultrafilters and the structure of P(ω)/fin.
SetTheory.title: Forcing and forcing axioms
SetTheory.description: The forcing method and the axioms that assert the existence of generic filters, such as Martin's axiom and the proper forcing axiom, together with combinatorial dichotomies like the open coloring axiom and the P-ideal dichotomy that follow from them.
SetTheory.title: Infinite games and determinacy
SetTheory.description: Infinite two-player games of perfect information on A^ℕ: the Gale–Stewart theorem for open and closed games, Martin's Borel determinacy, analytic determinacy from a measurable cardinal, the failure of the axiom of determinacy under the axiom of choice, and the regularity properties (perfect set property, property of Baire, measurability) that determinacy gives to sets of reals. The Banach–Mazur game on the reals is under Topology/descriptive-set-theory.

StatisticalMechanics.title: Statistical Mechanics
StatisticalMechanics.description: Statistical mechanics studies lattice models of interacting spins and bonds through Gibbs measures, partition functions, correlation inequalities, and phase transitions.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Lattice spin models
StatisticalMechanics.description: Spin models on finite graphs: the Ising Hamiltonian, Gibbs distribution and partition function and their agreement with the canonical ensemble, the pressure and its independence of boundary conditions, and the Lee–Yang theorem on the zeros of the partition function.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Correlation inequalities for spin systems
StatisticalMechanics.description: Inequalities for the correlations of ferromagnetic Ising models: the Griffiths (GKS) and FKG inequalities, monotonicity in the couplings and the temperature, and the Griffiths–Hurst–Sherman inequality with its consequences for the magnetization.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Gibbs states and phase transitions
StatisticalMechanics.description: Infinite-volume states of the Ising model and its phase transition: weak limits of box measures and the DLR condition, translation invariance, ergodicity and extremality of the plus state, spontaneous magnetization and the critical temperature, and Peierls' contour argument for long-range order.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Exact solutions and duality
StatisticalMechanics.description: Exact results for the two-dimensional Ising model: Kramers–Wannier duality between high- and low-temperature expansions, and Onsager's formula for the free energy through Kac–Ward determinants, Sherman's loop identities and the homology of the torus.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Random currents and sharpness
StatisticalMechanics.description: The random-current representation of Ising correlations and the switching lemma, and the sharpness of the Ising phase transition: the Simon–Lieb inequality, exponential decay of correlations below the critical point and the mean-field lower bound on the magnetization above it.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Random-cluster model
StatisticalMechanics.description: The random-cluster (Fortuin–Kasteleyn) model and its Edwards–Sokal coupling with the Potts and Ising models: finite-volume measures, the FKG inequality and comparison with Bernoulli percolation, infinite-volume limits, translation invariance and ergodicity, the free energy, agreement of free and wired measures, and the critical point.
StatisticalMechanics.title: Mean-field spin glasses
StatisticalMechanics.description: Disordered mean-field spin systems with Gaussian couplings: the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model and its free energy, the Parisi functional, Guerra's replica-symmetry-breaking bound and the Parisi formula.

TheoryOfComputation.title: Theory of Computation
TheoryOfComputation.description: The mathematical study of what can be computed and at what cost: machine models, computability and undecidability, automata and formal languages, and computational complexity.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Turing machines
TheoryOfComputation.description: Definitions, semantics and programming of Turing machines (single-tape, multi-tape and multi-stack), simulations between tape models, and universal machines with their machine codes. Results showing that a model computes exactly the recursive functions go to Equivalence of models of computation.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Single-tape Turing machines
TheoryOfComputation.description: Single-tape machines: configurations, steps, halting, composition of machines, tape views, state restriction, and translation of multi-stack machines to one tape (simulation and its halting behaviour, not its time cost).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Multi-tape and multi-stack machines
TheoryOfComputation.description: Multi-tape and multi-stack (TM2) machines and their program library: bit primitives, cleanup, composition, stack embeddings and generic host machines that run component machines, and state relabelling.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Universal Turing machines
TheoryOfComputation.description: Codes for machines, clocked evaluators and universal machines, completeness of codes, and the cost of universal simulation. Diagonalization against time-bounded codes goes to Hierarchy theorems.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Equivalence of models of computation
TheoryOfComputation.description: Register (URM), counter and RAM machines, and theorems that Turing machines and other models compute exactly the partial recursive functions or decide and recognize exactly the recursive and r.e. predicates (Church–Turing equivalences).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Computability and undecidability
TheoryOfComputation.description: Recursive and recursively enumerable predicates and their closure properties, the halting problem, Rice's and Rice–Shapiro theorems, the recursion and s-m-n theorems, enumerators, index sets such as totality, finiteness and minimal programs, and Busy Beaver functions.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Degrees of unsolvability and the arithmetical hierarchy
TheoryOfComputation.description: Turing and many-one reducibility, Turing degrees and the jump, recursive isomorphism (Myhill), productive, creative, simple and immune sets, r.e.-completeness, and the arithmetical hierarchy.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Undecidable problems
TheoryOfComputation.description: Specific undecidable problems and the reductions proving them undecidable: the Post correspondence problem and its variants, string rewriting, undecidable questions about context-free grammars (ambiguity, intersection, universality, regularity), and emptiness of linear bounded automata.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Decision procedures for automata, grammars and strings
TheoryOfComputation.description: Algorithms deciding questions about finite automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars given as data: emptiness, membership, universality, equivalence, and computable grammar reduction, together with the encodings of automata and grammars they operate on; and satisfiability of string constraints (word equations with regular membership and length bounds).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Finite automata and regular languages
TheoryOfComputation.description: Deterministic, nondeterministic, two-way and ε-automata, transducers, regular expressions and Kleene's theorem, closure properties of regular languages, automaton minimization, and the algebraic theory of recognition by monoids.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Automata and regular expressions
TheoryOfComputation.description: DFA, NFA, ε-NFA and two-way automata, sequential transducers and Mealy and Moore machines, regular expressions, Thompson's construction and Kleene's theorem, star height, and closure of regular languages under homomorphism, quotient, shuffle and substitution.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Automaton minimization
TheoryOfComputation.description: Nerode equivalence, the minimal automaton and its universal property, and the minimization algorithms of Moore, Hopcroft and Brzozowski with their correctness and cost.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Syntactic monoids and algebraic recognition
TheoryOfComputation.description: Recognition of languages by monoid morphisms, syntactic congruences and monoids, transition monoids, language contexts and quotients, and inverse images under word morphisms.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Automata on infinite words and infinite games
TheoryOfComputation.description: Büchi, generalized Büchi, parity, Rabin, Streett and Muller automata on infinite words, their emptiness and conversions, and parity games with attractors and traps.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Context-free languages
TheoryOfComputation.description: Context-free grammars and derivations, normal forms, parsing algorithms, pushdown automata, deterministic and ambiguous languages, closure and non-closure properties, pumping and Ogden's lemmas, and Parikh images.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Grammars, parsing and pushdown automata
TheoryOfComputation.description: Grammar basics and derivation forests, Chomsky and Greibach normal forms, ε- and unit-production elimination, CYK and Earley recognizers, leftmost derivations and (inherent) ambiguity, pushdown automata, deterministic context-free languages, and the grammar–PDA equivalence.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Closure properties and pumping lemmas
TheoryOfComputation.description: Closure of context-free languages under union, concatenation, star, homomorphism, inverse homomorphism, substitution, regular intersection and quotients, non-closure under intersection and complement, the pumping and Ogden lemmas, and Parikh's theorem.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Context-sensitive languages
