TheoryOfComputation.description: Context-sensitive grammars, linear bounded automata and space-bounded single-tape machines, and the equivalence between them.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Complexity classes
TheoryOfComputation.description: Definitions of time and space complexity on machine models (P, NP, PSPACE, EXP, L, NL, the polynomial hierarchy, FPT and W[1]), polynomial-time encodings and reductions, simulation overheads, Blum measures, and inclusions and collapses among deterministic and nondeterministic classes (Savitch, Immerman–Szelepcsényi, Karp–Lipton, Ladner, Mahaney). Randomized, counting, circuit and quantum classes have their own fields.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Hierarchy theorems and proof barriers
TheoryOfComputation.description: Time and space hierarchy theorems and diagonalization against time-bounded machines, separations such as P ≠ EXP, and barriers to separating classes: relativization (Baker–Gill–Solovay, oracle separations), natural proofs and algebrization.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Probabilistic classes (RP, BPP), Arthur–Merlin and interactive proofs (AM, MA, IP = PSPACE, graph (non)isomorphism), BPP versus nonuniform and alternating classes, randomized reductions (Valiant–Vazirani), and quantum classes BQP and QMA.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Counting complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: #P and PP: #P-completeness (counting SAT, permanent), PP-completeness, Toda's theorem, threshold languages, and approximate counting algorithms and schemes (Stockmeyer, Karp–Luby, Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Pseudorandomness and one-way functions
TheoryOfComputation.description: Complexity-theoretic foundations of cryptography and derandomization: one-way functions, hardcore predicates (Goldreich–Levin), hardness amplification (Yao's XOR lemma), hardness-versus-randomness generators (Nisan–Wigderson), and Impagliazzo's five worlds.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Communication complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Yao's two-party model: deterministic protocols as trees, the rectangle lemma, fooling-set and rank lower bounds, the deterministic complexity of equality, the log-rank conjecture, and randomized protocols with public or private coins (Newman's theorem). Yao's minimax principle for randomized algorithms in general goes to Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Boolean circuit complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Boolean circuits as a model of computation, including arithmetic circuits built from gates (adders, two's complement), parallel classes AC0, NC1 and NC, and circuit lower bounds (parity and majority not in AC0, Smolensky, Razborov's monotone bound, Shannon counting, Williams).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Algebraic complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Arithmetic circuits over a field and the complexity of algebraic problems: matrix multiplication exponents (square, rectangular, dual) and their bounds, tensor rank, and the bit complexity of integer multiplication.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Descriptive complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Logical characterizations of complexity classes on finite structures: Fagin's theorem, Immerman–Vardi (least fixed point and P), and transitive closure logic and NL.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Kolmogorov complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Algorithmic information content of individual strings: universal description methods, incompressible strings, non-computability and upper semicomputability of Kolmogorov complexity.
TheoryOfComputation.title: NP-completeness
TheoryOfComputation.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and NP-completeness of specific decision problems, by the problem's domain; includes both machine-level Karp reductions and stated NP-completeness results.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Cook–Levin theorem
TheoryOfComputation.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and its machinery: SAT verifiers, dense and binary CNF encodings and converters between them, tableau formulas and the generator machines that emit them.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Satisfiability and constraint satisfaction
TheoryOfComputation.description: Variants of SAT and CSP: 3SAT and the SAT-to-3SAT reduction, bounded-occurrence, monotone, not-all-equal and 1-in-3 SAT, MAX-SAT, MAX-2SAT, MIN-ONES, circuit SAT, binary CSP and betweenness.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Cliques, covers and domination in graphs
TheoryOfComputation.description: Clique, independent set, vertex cover, domination variants, feedback vertex and arc sets, odd cycle transversal, bicliques, densest subgraph, induced matching and minimum fill-in.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Graph coloring, cuts and layouts
TheoryOfComputation.description: Vertex, edge, list and precoloring-extension coloring, achromatic number, graph homomorphism, maximum and k-cuts, bisection, multiway cut, partition into triangles or paths, bandwidth, linear arrangement and linear ordering.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems
TheoryOfComputation.description: Hamiltonian paths and cycles, longest paths and cycles, disjoint paths and path covers, constrained spanning and Steiner trees, minimum equivalent digraph, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing, and (induced) subgraph isomorphism.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Network design, spanning trees and routing
TheoryOfComputation.description: Constrained spanning trees and forests (bounded diameter, bounded components, capacities), connectivity and diameter augmentation, superconcentrators, phylogenetic tree construction, and arc, postman, bus and delivery routing. The classical spanning tree, Steiner tree, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing problems are under Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Code generation and register allocation
TheoryOfComputation.description: Optimal code generation: parallel assignments, address expressions, unfixed variable locations, and expression evaluation with unlimited registers, with and without commutativity.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Number partitioning, knapsack and packing
TheoryOfComputation.description: Subset sum, subset product, partition, 3-partition, multiway partition, knapsack variants, bin and strip packing, numerical 3-dimensional matching and 0-1 integer programming.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Set systems, assignment and location
TheoryOfComputation.description: 3-dimensional matching, exact cover, set cover, set packing, set splitting, maximum coverage, minimum test set, generalized and quadratic assignment, facility location, k-center and k-median.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Databases, concurrency control and protection
TheoryOfComputation.description: Relational database design and querying (keys, prime attributes, normal forms, covers of functional dependencies, evaluation, containment and folding of conjunctive queries, index selection, anonymization), concurrency control (serializability of histories, locking policies, deadlock) and safety of protection systems.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Scheduling problems
TheoryOfComputation.description: Single-machine, parallel-machine, flow-shop, precedence-constrained and resource-constrained scheduling with deadlines, tardiness or weighted completion objectives.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Strings, puzzles and Latin squares
TheoryOfComputation.description: String problems (closest string, longest common subsequence, shortest common supersequence) and puzzles (Sudoku, Nonogram, Akari, Minesweeper, Latin square completion).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Probabilistically checkable proofs and inapproximability
TheoryOfComputation.description: The PCP theorem and Dinur's gap amplification, optimization classes (NPO, APX, MAXSNP), and hardness of approximation results such as Håstad's MAX-3SAT bound and the absence of a PTAS for MAX-CUT.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Completeness for other complexity classes
TheoryOfComputation.description: Problems complete for classes other than NP: P (circuit value), NL (s-t connectivity), coNP (UNSAT), PSPACE (TQBF, Geography), levels of the polynomial hierarchy (QSAT_k), EXP, NEXP and EXPSPACE (succinct problems, regular expressions with squaring).
TheoryOfComputation.title: Problems solvable in polynomial time
TheoryOfComputation.description: Proofs or statements that specific problems lie in P or L: graph reachability (PATH) with its marking machine, undirected connectivity in L, 2-SAT, primality, matching, maximum flow, linear programming, integer programming in fixed dimension, and hypergraph matching and cut questions.
TheoryOfComputation.title: Fine-grained and exponential-time complexity
TheoryOfComputation.description: Exact running times of hard problems beyond the polynomial/non-polynomial divide: exponential, subexponential and quasipolynomial algorithms for NP-hard or NP-intermediate problems, such as the tensor-network 2^o(n)-time algorithm for 3-SAT and Babai's quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism theorem, and the exponential time hypothesis.

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.description: Topology studies continuity, open sets, compactness, connectedness, and invariants preserved by homeomorphism.
Topology.title: Topological spaces and continuous maps
Topology.description: Foundations of point-set topology: open and closed sets, closure and interior, neighbourhood filters, limits and cluster points, continuity, bases and countability axioms, subspace, product, sum and quotient topologies, the lattice of topologies, embeddings, open, closed and quotient maps, and homeomorphisms; connectedness, separation and finer invariants are in General topology.
Topology.title: General topology
Topology.description: Point-set topology of topological and metric spaces: connectedness, separation and cardinal invariants, homogeneous spaces, direct and inverse limits of spaces, restricted products, and dimension theory.
Topology.title: Compactness and compactifications
Topology.description: Compact, locally compact, σ-compact, Lindelöf, countably compact and paracompact spaces, compactly generated spaces, proper maps, and the one-point and Stone–Čech compactifications; compactness in metric and uniform spaces is under those fields.
Topology.title: Metric spaces
Topology.description: Metric, pseudometric and extended metric spaces: balls, boundedness and diameter, Cauchy sequences and completeness, Lipschitz, Hölder and antilipschitz maps, isometries and dilations, Hausdorff distance and thickenings, covering numbers, ultrametrics and metrizability; curvature, geodesics and Gromov–Hausdorff convergence are in Geometry's metric geometry.
Topology.title: Uniform spaces
Topology.description: Uniform structures and uniform continuity, Cauchy filters, completeness and Hausdorff completion, total boundedness, uniform, locally uniform and compact convergence, equicontinuity and the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem; uniform groups and rings are under Topological groups and Topological rings, fields and algebras.
Topology.title: Ordered topological spaces
Topology.description: Order topologies and order-closed topologies on ordered sets: the intermediate value theorem, compactness of intervals, monotone functions and their one-sided limits, liminf and limsup, local extrema, semicontinuity, the extended real line, upper, lower, Scott and Lawson topologies, topological lattices, and Priestley and Esakia spaces.
Topology.title: Spaces of continuous functions
Topology.description: Spaces of continuous maps with the compact-open topology, bounded continuous functions, functions vanishing at infinity or with compact support, algebras and ideals of continuous functions, locally constant functions, and the Stone–Weierstrass theorem; Banach-space theory of function spaces is in Analysis.
Topology.title: Descriptive set theory
Topology.description: The topology of Polish spaces and their definable subsets: classical characterizations of Cantor space, Baire space and the rationals, Borel complexity, Bernstein sets and topological games.
Topology.title: Continuum theory and infinite-dimensional topology
Topology.description: Compact connected spaces, Peano continua and space-filling curves, absolute retracts, hyperspaces, the Hilbert cube and fixed-point properties.
Topology.title: Topological groups
Topology.description: Groups carrying a compatible topology: metrizability, profinite groups and profinite completions, and functions on locally compact groups.
Topology.title: Topological rings, fields and algebras
Topology.description: Rings, fields and algebras with compatible topologies: ideals, localization and completion of topological rings, adic and linear topologies, nonarchimedean and valued rings and fields, topological algebras and star algebras, and topological monoids with zero; topological modules and vector spaces have their own field.
Topology.title: Topological modules and vector spaces
Topology.description: Modules and vector spaces over topological rings with continuous operations: continuous linear, multilinear, alternating and affine maps and equivalences, closed submodules and topological complements, finite-dimensional spaces, module topologies, weak and weak-star topologies, and topologies on spaces of continuous linear maps; normed and Banach spaces are in Analysis.
Topology.title: Infinite sums and products
Topology.description: Unconditional summation of families in topological monoids, groups, rings and modules: summable families with their sums and products, summation filters, regrouping and reindexing, sums over ℕ and ℤ, sums in ordered spaces and the extended nonnegative reals, uniformly convergent sums of functions and discrete convolution; convergence tests and closed-form series are in Analysis.
Topology.title: Categories of spaces and locales
Topology.description: Categories of topological spaces and their limits and colimits, compact Hausdorff, profinite and Stonean spaces as used in condensed mathematics, convenient categories such as compactly generated and delta-generated spaces, topological pairs, and locales and frames; individual topological properties are in the point-set fields.
Topology.title: Sheaves on topological spaces
Topology.description: Presheaves and sheaves on topological spaces with values in a category: equivalent forms of the sheaf condition, stalks, sheafification and étale spaces, pushforward and pullback, skyscraper and flasque sheaves, and sheaves of functions and of rings; sheaves on general sites are in Category theory and sheaves of modules in Algebra.
Topology.title: Algebraic topology
Topology.description: Homotopy groups, singular homology and other algebraic invariants of spaces, with classical theorems such as Borsuk–Ulam, Hurewicz and Hopf invariant one, and their use on data in topological data analysis: Čech and Vietoris–Rips complexes, persistence modules and barcodes, and Mapper.
Topology.title: Simplicial homotopy theory
Topology.description: The simplex category, simplicial and cosimplicial objects, simplicial sets with their standard simplices, horns, boundaries, skeleta and subcomplexes, Kan complexes and quasicategories, nerves and homotopy categories, anodyne extensions, simplicial homology, geometric realization, and the Dold–Kan correspondence; model categories are in Model categories and homotopical algebra.
Topology.title: Model categories and homotopical algebra
Topology.description: Quillen model categories and categories with fibrations, cofibrations and weak equivalences: fibrant and cofibrant objects, cylinders, path objects and homotopies, homotopy categories and the fundamental lemma, Reedy categories and relative cell complexes; localization of categories as such is in Category theory.
Topology.title: Manifolds and geometric topology
Topology.description: Topological and smooth manifolds in low and high dimensions: surfaces, 3- and 4-manifolds, the Poincaré conjecture, exotic spheres, triangulations, diffeomorphism groups and transformation groups.
Topology.title: Knot theory
Topology.description: Embeddings of circles in three-space up to ambient isotopy: knot and link diagrams, chirality, slice knots, and geometric invariants such as ropelength, distortion and quadrisecants.

Economics.title: Mathematical Economics
Economics.description: Mathematical economics studies accounting identities, markets, decisions and the quantitative structures used in economic models.
Economics.title: Choice, utility and risk
Economics.description: Individual decision making: preference relations and choice, ordinal utility representations, revealed preference and Afriat's theorem, expected utility and its paradoxes, risk aversion, certainty equivalents, insurance and stochastic dominance as seen by an expected-utility maximizer. Stochastic orders of measures in general are under Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination in Probability.
Economics.title: Consumer theory
Economics.description: The consumer's problem and its duality: budget sets, Marshallian demand and its properties, demand for standard utility families, the expenditure and indirect utility functions, Shephard's lemma, the Slutsky equation and matrix, the envelope theorem, and money measures of welfare change such as compensating variation and consumer surplus.
Economics.title: Producer theory
Economics.description: The competitive firm: production sets and profit maximization, the profit and cost functions and their convexity, concavity and homogeneity, Hotelling's lemma, the law of supply, returns to scale and product exhaustion.
Economics.title: Partial equilibrium and public economics
Economics.description: Single markets in isolation: supply and demand, existence of partial equilibrium, elasticities, price controls, the incidence and deadweight loss of taxes, and the correction of externalities and provision of public goods (Pigouvian taxes, the Coase theorem, the Samuelson condition). Markets with market power are under imperfect competition.
Economics.title: Imperfect competition
Economics.description: Markets in which firms have market power: monopoly pricing and the Lerner rule, monopsony, and oligopoly models such as Cournot and Bertrand competition. Equilibrium concepts for strategic games in general are under Game theory.
Economics.title: General equilibrium and input–output analysis
Economics.description: Economies with many interacting markets: exchange economies, Walras' law, existence of competitive equilibrium, the first and second fundamental theorems of welfare economics, and Leontief's input–output model of interindustry production.
Economics.title: International economics
Economics.description: Trade between countries and the prices that link them: comparative advantage and Ricardian gains from trade, the Stolper–Samuelson theorem, tariffs, and real exchange rates.
Economics.title: Labor markets and income distribution
Economics.description: Labor supply and human capital, wage decompositions, flows between employment and unemployment, and the measurement of inequality and poverty: the Gini coefficient, the principle of transfers, inequality-averse social welfare and poverty indices.
Economics.title: National accounts, money and prices
Economics.description: Macroeconomic measurement and its identities: the product, income and expenditure measures of national accounts, sector balances, stock-flow accounting, price indices and real values, the quantity equation and the Fisher equation linking money, inflation and interest rates.
Economics.title: Macroeconomic models
Economics.description: Models of the aggregate economy: Solow growth, the golden rule and growth accounting, overlapping generations, intertemporal consumption and Ricardian equivalence, government debt dynamics, the Keynesian cross and IS–LM, loanable funds, the Phillips curve, the Lucas critique and the stability of linear policy models.
Economics.title: Financial accounting
Economics.description: The arithmetic of a firm's books: double-entry ledgers and the accounting equation, closing entries and retained earnings, depreciation schedules, inventory cost flows, the cash flow statement, and financial ratios such as the DuPont decomposition and the cash conversion cycle.
Economics.title: Interest theory and fixed income
Economics.description: Present values of deterministic cash flows: discounting and internal rates of return, annuities, perpetuities and loan amortization, bond prices and discount factors, duration, convexity and immunization, cash-flow matching and swap rates. Defaultable bonds, forwards and options are under Asset pricing and financial risk.
Economics.title: Asset pricing and financial risk
Economics.description: Asset pricing by absence of arbitrage and the measurement of financial risk: static replication, parity relations and no-arbitrage bounds (option payoffs and put–call parity, properties of call prices, forwards and futures, covered interest parity), pricing by replication in one-period and multi-period binomial models and the early exercise of American calls, the Black–Scholes formula and its sensitivities, state prices and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing in state-price form, the law of one price, stochastic discount factors and linear factor pricing, asset and portfolio returns, mean–variance portfolios, the tangency portfolio and the capital asset pricing model, value at risk and expected shortfall, credit risk (expected loss, defaultable bonds), and optimal execution: liquidation schedules trading off quadratic impact costs against inventory risk. The fundamental theorem of asset pricing for martingale measures, in gain form, and finite-horizon optimal stopping and the Snell envelope are under Martingales and optional stopping in Probability; present values of deterministic cash flows, annuities and bonds are under Interest theory and fixed income, and the valuation of firms and their securities under Corporate finance.
Economics.title: Corporate finance
Economics.description: Valuation of firms and their securities: dividend discount and Gordon growth models, retained earnings and the value of growth, capital structure and the Modigliani–Miller theorems, the debt tax shield, payout policy, debt and equity as claims on the firm's assets, and real options. Pricing of forwards and options by absence of arbitrage, and asset and portfolio returns, are under Asset pricing and financial risk; present values of deterministic cash flows are under Interest theory and fixed income.
Economics.title: Inventory, transport and spatial models
Economics.description: Quantitative models of stocks and of movement in space: inventory dynamics with lead times and backlogging, accessibility measures of transport networks, and spatial interaction models distributing trips or demand among destinations.
Economics.title: Actuarial mathematics
Economics.description: Mathematics of insurance and pensions: life tables and survival functions, life insurance and annuity present values and their identities, multiple-state and multiple-life models with reserve recursions and Thiele's equation, aggregate loss models and stop-loss premiums, ruin theory, credibility theory and claims reserving. Interest-only present values are under Interest theory and fixed income; survival estimation from data is under Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis in Probability.

Physics.title: Mathematical Physics
Physics.description: Mathematical physics describes mechanical, electromagnetic and quantum systems through mathematical models and their laws.
Physics.title: Quantities, units and measurement
Physics.description: Physical quantities and their dimensions in the International System of Quantities, unit conversions and dimensionless groups, and the propagation of measurement uncertainty through linear, linearized and Lipschitz models. Calibration in analytical chemistry is under Chemistry.
Physics.title: Classical mechanics
Physics.description: Newtonian mechanics of particles, rigid bodies and simple systems, and its application to flight and spaceflight: work, energy and potentials, harmonic, damped, forced and nonlinear oscillators, modal analysis and random response, frames and rigid-body dynamics, statics, linkages and impacts, Newtonian gravitation and orbits, aircraft and spacecraft motion, and elementary models of muscle power and the energy budget of exercise. Elastic structures are under Elasticity and structural mechanics.
Physics.title: Particles, work and oscillations
Physics.description: Newtonian dynamics of particles and lumped systems: kinetic energy, power and the work of conservative forces, harmonic, damped, forced, base-excited and nonlinear oscillators, modal analysis of linear multi-degree-of-freedom systems, the random response of a first-order mechanical system, and elementary models of muscle power and the energy budget of exercise.
Physics.title: Rigid bodies, frames and mechanisms
Physics.description: Frames and rigid bodies: body-fixed and inertial frames, rotating frames and the Coriolis force, rigid-body motion, angular momentum and Euler's equations, statics of force systems, a constrained two-link pendulum, gear trains and linkages, and impacts.
Physics.title: Gravitation and orbital mechanics
Physics.description: Newtonian gravitation and orbits: potentials of point masses and uniform spheres and their superposition, Kepler's third law and orbit averages, two-body orbits, the vis-viva equation and impulsive manoeuvres, regularity of the inverse-square field and the restricted three-body problem.
Physics.title: Flight mechanics and spaceflight
Physics.description: Motion of aircraft and spacecraft: aircraft performance, six-degree-of-freedom flight dynamics with trim and linearization, rocket and electric propulsion, ballistic atmospheric entry, spacecraft attitude with reaction wheels, and mission resource ledgers.
Physics.title: Elasticity and structural mechanics
Physics.description: Linear elasticity and the mechanics of structures: Cauchy stress, small strain and Mohr's circle, isotropic elastic energy, Euler–Bernoulli beams and their vibration modes, the stiffness method for beams and frames, trusses and their load envelopes, plastic collapse of beams, rigid footings on elastic foundations, and fracture under linear elastic fracture mechanics.
Physics.title: Fluid mechanics
Physics.description: Hydrostatics and elementary fluid dynamics: hydrostatic pressure and buoyancy, Bernoulli's theorem, Stokes settling, and continuum models of traffic flow with their shocks. Rotating and stratified flows of the ocean and atmosphere, water waves and open-channel hydraulics are under Earth Science.
Physics.title: Waves and acoustics
Physics.description: Linear waves and acoustics: frequency, wavenumber and wavelength, travelling-wave solutions of the wave equation, sound intensity and pressure levels, transmission of sound through patches and limp panels, Sabine reverberation and the energy of coupled structural–acoustic systems. Water waves are under Earth Science.
Physics.title: Quantum mechanics
Physics.description: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics: states, observables and the Born rule in finite dimensions, unitary evolution, and exactly solvable models such as the particle in a box and the harmonic oscillator. Quantum chemistry is under Chemistry and quantum information under Quantum Information.
Physics.title: Engineering thermodynamics and heat transfer
Physics.description: Thermodynamic states and balances of engineering systems, power and refrigeration cycles, exergy, and conduction, convection and radiation heat transfer.
Physics.title: Nuclear reactor physics
Physics.description: Neutron diffusion and transport models of nuclear reactors: one-group diffusion, buckling and the criticality of bare reactors.

Chemistry.title: Mathematical Chemistry
Chemistry.description: Mathematical chemistry studies quantitative models of chemical systems and reactions.
Chemistry.title: Amounts, composition and stoichiometry
Chemistry.description: Amounts of substance, molar masses and composition, flows of process streams, and the stoichiometry of balanced reactions: conserved balance coordinates, reaction extents, limiting reagents and yields.
Chemistry.title: Chemical thermodynamics
Chemistry.description: Equilibrium thermodynamics of gases and chemical systems: equations of state and the kinetic theory of gases, the canonical ensemble, the first and second laws, the fundamental relation, thermochemistry, Gibbs energy, phase equilibria and the phase rule.
Chemistry.title: Solutions and aqueous equilibria
Chemistry.description: Concentrations of solutions and the equilibria of aqueous systems: charge and mass balances and the proton condition, acid dissociation, carbonate speciation and alkalinity, Henry's law and air–water gas exchange.
Chemistry.title: Chemical kinetics and reactors
Chemistry.description: Rates of chemical reactions and reactors: integrated rate laws and half-lives, the Arrhenius law, conservation laws, deficiency and stochastic dynamics of reaction networks, Turing patterns of the Brusselator, and stirred-tank and box reactors. Biochemical reaction networks are under Biology.
Chemistry.title: Quantum chemistry and spectroscopy
Chemistry.description: Quantum models of atoms and molecules and their spectra: angular momentum, the rigid rotor and hydrogen-like atoms, variational and perturbation methods and Hückel theory, molecular symmetry and vibrational modes, and nuclear magnetic resonance.
Chemistry.title: Analytical chemistry
Chemistry.description: Quantitative chemical analysis: statistical treatment of replicate measurements, calibration lines and inverse prediction with their error budgets, and mass spectrometry and isotope patterns.

EarthScience.title: Earth Science
EarthScience.description: Earth science uses mathematical models to describe the Earth and its physical systems.
EarthScience.title: Solid Earth geophysics
EarthScience.description: Physics of the solid Earth: isostasy and flexure, the density structure of the interior, conductive geotherms and convection, plate motions, the geomagnetic dipole, seismic waves, rays and earthquake magnitudes, and the optics of minerals.
EarthScience.title: Geochronology and stratigraphy
EarthScience.description: Dating of rocks and sediments: radioactive decay and decay chains, radiometric ages, isochrons and the concordia curve, cosmogenic exposure ages, sediment accumulation, hiatuses and decompaction.
EarthScience.title: Geochemistry and biogeochemical cycles
EarthScience.description: Chemical processes in the Earth system: melting and partitioning of trace elements, isotope fractionation, box models of reservoirs and the carbon and nutrient cycles. Aqueous equilibria are under Chemistry.
EarthScience.title: Atmosphere, radiation and climate
EarthScience.description: Thermodynamics and radiation of the atmosphere and the energy balance of the climate: hydrostatic and adiabatic structure, static stability, water vapour and cloud droplets, radiative transfer and optical depth, planetary energy balance and climate feedbacks.
EarthScience.title: Geophysical fluid dynamics
EarthScience.description: Rotating and stratified flows of the ocean and atmosphere: geostrophic and thermal wind balance, Ekman layers, Sverdrup balance, Rossby waves, potential vorticity and quasigeostrophic conservation, shallow-water and surface gravity waves, buoyancy frequency and box models of the ocean circulation.
EarthScience.title: Hydrology and surface processes
EarthScience.description: Water at and below the land surface and the materials it moves through: catchment budgets, infiltration, hydrographs and flood routing, flood frequency, open-channel hydraulics, groundwater flow and solute transport, river water quality, hillslope evolution and soil mechanics.
EarthScience.title: Geophysical data and inversion
EarthScience.description: Observation and analysis of geophysical data: coordinates and grids on the sphere, satellite positioning, sampling and filtering of time series, spatial interpolation and kriging, remote-sensing indices and the null space of tomographic inverse problems.
